Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.21） Exhibit 48 · LPG 炼厂产出环比 +110 kb/d 至 1.60 mb/d，同比 -130 kb/d（-8%） | LPG refinery output was up 110 kb/d MoM but down 130 kb/d YoY (-8%) in September — Source: 中国海关总署, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.21） SECTION 08 库存观测 Inventory Data 可观测库存指可用卫星测量的浮顶罐地上储油，9 月底合计 11.8 亿桶 原油。其中大部分记为"商业库存"，但鉴于北京设定央企存储义务并保留动用控制权，相当部分商业库存实为"社会责任库存"（准战略储备）；地下洞穴储油（战略储备为主，约 1 亿桶，Oxford Institute for Energy Studies 估算）可见度差。 9 月可观测原油库存环比大降 61.7 百万桶 （隐含 -2.1 mb/d），为 2024 年 9 月以来首次出现某月同比下降（同比 -4%、-53.9 百万桶），且已 连续 6 个月下降 ，5-9 月平均去库 700 kb/d。降幅几乎全部来自商业库存（-57.6 百万桶至 9.84 亿桶），SPR 仅 -4.1 百万桶至 1.91 亿桶（同比大致持平）。维持约 14 mb/d 开工而不增进口，是加速去库的直接原因。成品油可观测库存环比 -6.3 百万桶、同比 -20 百万桶：柴油 -5.7 百万桶至 90.6 百万桶（同比 -13%，高出口+全球柴油紧），汽油 -0.6 百万桶至 85.9 百万桶（同比 -8%）。 出口的政策闸门正在收紧： 出口资格取决于库存不低于战前水平，而今夏的强劲去库意味着炼厂越来越难达标——Argus 报道有企业将化工调合组分计为成品油虚增申报库存，三大央企也削减对贸易公司的柴油销售以留存集团库存；Oilchem 称 10 月底商业柴油库存已降至其 2011 年有数据以来最低。10 月原油去库已放缓至 -11.3 百万桶；若北京要求国企补库（商业 8000 万桶 + SPR 6000 万桶），将直接抬升年末进口。 Exhibit 49 · 中国可观测原油库存已连续 6 个月下降（按月：商业/炼厂/SPR） | Change in China onshore crude inventory by month — Source: Vortexa, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.22） Exhibit 50 · 可观测原油库存 9 月环比 -61.7 百万桶、同比 -53.9 百万桶 | Observable crude inventories (Vortexa) fell 61.7 mln bbls MoM and were 53.9 mln bbls lower YoY in September — Source: Vortexa, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.23） Exhibit 51 · 可观测成品油总库存环比 -6.3 百万桶、同比 -20 百万桶 | Observable product inventories fell 6.3 mln bbls MoM and were 20 mln bbls lower YoY in September — Source: Oilchem, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.23） Exhibit 52 · 汽油库存环比 -0.6 百万桶至 85.9 百万桶（同比 -8%） | Observable gasoline inventories fell 0.6 mln bbls MoM and were 7.1 mln bbls lower YoY in September — Source: Oilchem, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.23） Exhibit 53 · 柴油库存环比 -5.7 百万桶至 90.6 百万桶（同比 -13%） | Observable diesel inventories fell 5.7 mln bbls MoM and were 12.9 mln bbls lower YoY in September — Source: Oilchem, Morgan Stanley（Morgan Stanley, Oil Data Digest, p.23） SECTION 09 数据源交叉验证 Comparison with Other Data 同为政府表观数据的直接计算，走势一致且降幅走阔：大摩同比降幅从 12% 扩至 16% 、Argus 从 10% 扩至 15%，环比均约 -460 kb/d。Energy Aspects 最接近表观需求图像，同比降幅从 8% 走阔至 11%；S&P Global 与 IEA 因叠加自家调整而平滑，均显示约 -4% 的稳定同比降幅。五家平均，9 月需求同比约 -1.7 mb/d（-10%） 。 Uncertainty 来源： Morgan Stanley Research — Global · Commodity Research · 报告日期： 2026 年 11 月 16 日 · 作者： Martijn Rats / Charlotte Firkins / Amy Gower · 期号： The Oil Manual · Chartbook Edition · 整理：研报工作台 AI 精读 · 观点归属 Morgan Stanley，仅供研究参考 目录 CONTENTS 核心观点 · Key Points 总览：实物走软 vs 消息驱动 · Summary 霍尔木兹与中东供应 · Hormuz 平价与基准价 · Flat Price & Benchmarks 期限结构与时间价差 · Term Structure 原油品质与升贴水 · Quality & Differentials 成品油与裂解价差 · Products & Cracks 供应：OPEC · Supply — OPEC 供应：非 OPEC · Supply — non-OPEC 供应：美国页岩油 · US Shale 需求 · Demand 炼厂 · Refining 贸易流与海上原油 · Trade Flows 库存 · Inventories 平衡表与价格预测 · Balance & Forecasts 宏观跨资产与持仓 · Macro & Positioning 核心观点 KEY POINTS 实物走软 vs 消息驱动： MEG7 出口恢复至 ~22 mb/d（战前 ~25）、cash Dubai premium 归零（本周一度转负）、北海升水从 $25-28 砍到 $0-5、远程油种到鹿特丹比 Dated 低 $4-20/bbl、VLCC 平均航程缩短 ~500 海里令运费大跌；但两周内 1 月布伦特跌 $18/bbl 集中在三天，全部由美/伊消息触发（11-2 卡塔尔斡旋 -$9、11-4 中期选举 -$9、11-9 白宫"highly unlikely" -$6）。 预测不变： 1Q27 布伦特 $100/bbl 维持，4Q27 随基本面转向过剩回落至 ~$75/bbl ；Dated Brent 2026 全年 $96.7、2027 $86.3（base 情景）。 需求： 2026 共识 -2.7 mb/d（中国 -0.9、中东 -0.7、其他亚洲 -0.6）；2027 修复 +2.2 mb/d，但仍比 2025 低 ~0.5 mb/d。 供应： OPEC 8+3 恢复至 ~28-30 mb/d（低于配额 3-5、伊朗仅 ~1.8、俄罗斯短 ~1.3）；2026 非 OPEC 增长共识从 1 月 +880 kb/d 被砍到 +115 kb/d（卡塔尔 -675、俄罗斯 -405，巴西 +630 抵消）；页岩钻机 +15% 但单井产量平台化，2027 仅温和增长 ~170 kb/d。 炼厂： 全球开工低于 2022-25 趋势 ~3 mb/d；俄罗斯开工 ~3.7 mb/d、较 1 月 -31%（今年 116 次无人机袭击）；4Q26 计划检修 ~3.1 mb/d 为同期史上最低、2Q27 已挂 ~6.4 mb/d；利润率仍是常态 3-5 倍（ARA 柴油裂解 ~$83 接近纪录）但已自 9-10 月峰回落 $15-20。 库存与平衡： 全球油库存 ~80 亿桶 8 月起走平（同比 -470 mb）；美国 SPR ~283 mb 为 1982 年以来最低、1 月底降至 ~238 mb（低于法定下限），3-10 月政府已释放 ~228 mb、第二轮 ~44 mb 至 1 月，2H27 才开始回补；MS 平衡表 4Q26 起转为过剩且 2027 扩大（+2.3/+2.9/+2.3/+3.7 mb/d）。 SECTION 01 · SUMMARY p3-9 总览：实物面持续走软，平价却跟着美伊消息走 Physical Softening vs Lingering Supply Uncertainty 这份 Chartbook 记录的原油市场主线是： 实物条件稳步走软，但平价（flat price）主要由美国/伊朗消息驱动 。中东原油出口已经恢复（MEG7 近四周均值约 22 mb/d，接近战前约 25 mb/d），本周 cash Dubai premium 一度转负；中东货回归令亚洲炼厂对大西洋盆地原油的拉力减弱，大西洋市场转向宽松——VLCC 平均航程缩短（平均约 4,000 海里、同比短约 500 海里），运力被释放、运价进一步下跌。 这对北海品种利空：运费走低后，巴西、西非、美国等远程油种在西北欧越来越有竞争力， 多种远程原油在运后仍能以比 Dated Brent 低 $4-20/bbl 的价格在鹿特丹交货 。价格端已经确认：Dated 低于布伦特首行、布伦特 CFD 曲线转为 contango、实物升贴水走弱。 平价的驱动是消息面： 两周内 1 月布伦特累计下跌 $18/bbl，且集中在三天——11 月 2 日卡塔尔斡旋和平消息 -$9；11 月 4 日（美中期选举）-$9；11 月 9 日白宫称新一轮打击"highly unlikely" -$6。本周布伦特再跌约 $6 至 $92/bbl，Dated 四周累计下跌约 $35/bbl（北海升水、CFD 与运费同步崩塌）。 展望： 维持 1Q27 布伦特 $100/bbl 预测不变 ；中期看，随市场自身基本面转向过剩，预计 4Q27 布伦特回到约 $75/bbl 。 图 1 · 复杂炼厂毛利（产品价值）已超 2022 年高点，但增量大部分被航运与炼油环节拿走，原油本身并未获得对应溢价 | Dated Brent: product worth vs price / Where the value of a barrel goes — Source: S&P Global Commodity Insights, Argus, Bloomberg, Baltic Exchange（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p5） 图 2 · 鹿特丹 1 月到岸成本：西非/巴西/美国等远程油种可比 Dated Brent 低 $4-20/bbl 交货，大西洋市场明显宽松 | Landed cost in Rotterdam, Jan-27 delivery — Source: Platts, Baltic Exchange, Bloomberg（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p9） SECTION 02 · STRAIT OF HORMUZ p8-19, 93 霍尔木兹与中东供应 Strait of Hormuz & Middle East 过峡流量恢复但仍低于战前： 自 9 月下旬起霍尔木兹流量约 11-14 mb/d（战前约 20 mb/d）；MEG7 原油出口近四周均值约 22 mb/d，接近冲突前约 25 mb/d。分品种看，过峡出口中原油/凝析油仍是主体，石脑油、LPG、柴油已恢复至战前区间的偏低位置。 安全风险重新上升： 过去六周商船遇袭显著增加（10 月初单周最高约 12 起，MS 新闻口径），跨越海峡的运费溢价维持在高位：湾内装载对湾外装载的 VLCC 现货溢价 11 月 13 日达 $18.8/bbl （航程调整后），为系列高位；但 FFA 远期曲线定价溢价自 1 月起回落至 $4-5/bbl ，不足上月曲线的一半——市场押注风险溢价是暂时的。 图 3 · 商船遇袭次数近六周显著上升（左）；湾内装载 VLCC 运费溢价升至 $18.8/bbl 高位（右） | Attacks on merchant shipping / VLCC freight premium for loading inside the Strait of Hormuz — Source: UKMTO, Platts, Argus; Baltic Exchange（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p15） 图 4 · MEG7 原油出口四周均值回到约 22 mb/d（战前约 25）；霍尔木兹分品种出口中原油已恢复至 12 mb/d 上下 | Oil exports – MEG7 countries / Strait of Hormuz: oil exports by product group — Source: Petro-Logistics, Vortexa（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p17） 图 5 · 现货溢价创 $18.8/bbl 新高（左），但 FFA 曲线自 1 月起把溢价压回 $4-5/bbl（右） | VLCC & forward VLCC freight premium for loading inside the Strait of Hormuz (TD3C vs TD34) — Source: Baltic Exchange（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p93） 配套观察：也拉延布（Yanbu）原油出口已从 10 月初约 2.0 mb/d 低点恢复至 2.7-3.0 mb/d，但仍低于正常；Fujairah 原油出口自 9 月底约 2.45 mb/d 高点回落至约 1.85 mb/d，仍比正常高约 0.8 mb/d——部分海湾货物绕行外海装货。 SECTION 03 · FLAT PRICE & BENCHMARKS p20-23 平价与基准价 Flat Price & Benchmarks 本周 ICE Brent M1 收于 $96.1/bbl （周环比 -$2.2、四周 -$10.7），NYMEX WTI 12 月 $88.9（四周 -$10.1）；Dubai Mo01 实货 $92.0 （四周 -$14.6）。Dated Brent $96.0 、四周 -$7.3——Dated 较四周末已累计下跌约 $35/bbl，但仍比 2008、2011-14、2022 年的真实（通胀调整）高点低不少。 价差结构全面收敛：cash Dubai premium 从 9 月约 $30/bbl 崩落至 约 $0.3-0.4/bbl （本周一度转负）；Brent/Dubai EFS 收窄至 $4.6/bbl （10 月初约 $11）；北海各品种对 Dated 的升水已所剩无几（Forties -1.6、Ekofisk +0.84、J. Sverdrup -4.2）。 图 6 · 全球油价总表（截至 11 月 13 日）：基准、期限结构、北海/西非/美国/中东价差、运费与主要裂解价差一览 | Global oil prices (latest as per 13 Nov 2026) — Source: Argus, Bloomberg, Platts, General Index（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p21） 图 7 · Brent/Dubai EFS 收窄至约 $3.7-4.6/bbl（10 月初约 $11）；cash Dubai premium 从 9 月约 $30 崩至约 $0.3、本周一度转负 | Brent/Dubai spread (London MOC EFS) / Cash Dubai premium — Source: S&P Global Platts（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p23） SECTION 04 · TERM STRUCTURE & TIME SPREADS p24-33 期限结构与时间价差 Term Structure & Time Spreads 布伦特日历价差自 10 月末走弱：曲线前端较 10 月初低约 $7/bbl，两年以后的合约几乎没动—— 整条曲线的下跌集中在近端 。近月价差两周内腰斩：Mo2-Mo6 从约 $13 收窄到约 $6/bbl，Mo1-Mo2 仅约 $2/bbl。 CFD 曲线崩塌是本周实物走软的最直接信号： 前端 CFD 从三周前约 $14/bbl 跌至约 $1/bbl ，近周合约已低于第 3-6 周合约（曲线转为 contango）；DFL 也从约 $7.6 减半至约 $3.8/bbl。作为对照，商业 OECD 库存仅比五年均值低约 1%——该水平历史上通常对应平缓的价差，而布伦特此前一度深度 backwardation，说明此前近月紧张更多是战时物流扭曲而非库存状态。 估值坐标：$92 的 Dated Brent 仍比曲线开始支付满 carry（2-3 年仓储成本）所需的水平高 $25-30/bbl；按通胀调整，布伦特处于 2007 年以来第 50 百分位附近，而 ICE gasoil（约 $177/bbl）处于第 87 百分位—— 柴油仍是整个链条中最紧的一环 。跨大西洋套利窗口：WTI-鹿特丹在正常价差下窗口关闭，亏损收窄至 $1-4/bbl。 图 8 · 布伦特 CFD 曲线三周内从前端约 $14/bbl 崩至约 $1/bbl（左）；CFD Week 2 长周期视角下本轮战时冲高正在快速回吐（右） | Brent CFD curve / Brent CFD Week 2 — Source: S&P Global Platts（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p28） SECTION 05 · CRUDE QUALITY & DIFFERENTIALS p34-40 原油品质与升贴水 Crude Quality & Differentials 中质原油产量仍比战前低约 5 mb/d，轻质原油已回到高位——品质分化仍在，但 价格上的紧张正在快速消退 ：北海各品种对 Dated 的升水从 10 月中的约 $25-28/bbl 跌至 $0-5/bbl （图 9 左， Forties 已转负）；CPC Blend 从创纪录的 -$34/bbl 回升至约 -$20/bbl。 远程油种方面：Djeno 贴水从创纪录的约 -$32 收窄至约 -$26/bbl；美国方面 WTI/Brent 回到约 -$7/bbl（10 月末约 -$14）。东西价差：ESPO 仍对 Dated strip 升水约 $10-12/bbl，Urals 到印度已滑至平价；伊朗贴水因封锁持续。含硫折价创纪录： sour 原油每 1% 含硫的折价达到约 $9/bbl ，超过 2022 年极值——湾外含硫油相对充裕，而战前 much of the world's medium-sour supply 所在的海湾区域物流仍受扰动。 图 9 · 北海各品种对 Dated 升水从约 $25-28/bbl 崩落至 $0-5/bbl（左）；CPC Blend 从 -$34 纪录低点回升至约 -$20/bbl（右） | North sea: differential to North Sea CIF Dated Brent strip / CPC Blend: premium/(discount) to BTC Dated Strip — Source: S&P Global Platts（Morgan Stanley, The Oil Manual – Chartbook Edition, p36） SECTION 06 · REFINED PRODUCTS & CRACK SPREADS p41-50 成品油与裂解价差 Refined reports.stext: 石脑油国际周报 #46 核心整理 NIS NAPHTHA INTERNATIONAL · WEEKLY · WEEK 46 石脑油国际周报 #46：东方急跌，西方静观 East of Suez correction, West of Suez quiet 来源： NIS (Naphtha Information Services Pte Ltd) — Naphtha International · 2026 年 11 月 13 日（周五）· Week 46 · 整理：研报工作台 AI 精读 · 观点归属 NIS，仅供研究参考 目录 CONTENTS 核心观点 · Key Points 苏伊士以东 · East of Suez 苏伊士以西 · West of Suez 市场分析：欧洲俄罗斯对东方流出下降 · Market Analysis 净回值与套利 · Netbacks & Arbitrage 公允价值 · Fair Value 核心观点 KEY POINTS 东方急跌（本刊主线） ：12 月"超级紧张"预期一周内逆转——中东装载续升、12 月套利到货回升至约 1.50 mmtons 、终端用户明确不提负荷，70-min CFR 前月差 4 个交易日从 $47.00 崩至 $24.00 （周四尚有 $32.00）；OSN C&F 东京（含 Chiba 溢价）周五单日跌 $71/ton ，同期 NWE 仅跌 $36。 但 NEA 仍是全球最好去向 ：CFR 乙烯–石脑油价差守住 $300/ton ，即使价格跳水，Chiba/Yosu 对 Med FRN 货的回报仍远好于 Rotterdam/Antwerp——欧洲人"担心一下"即可，无需真慌。 俄供应新冲击 ：Ust-Luga 分裂装置遭无人机重创，可合理假定其石脑油到货 12 月底骤降甚至归零、1Q '27 保持极低——这是套利流量中仅存的看多因素。 西方极静 ：NYH 五天零成交、USG"多年最淡"；Med 货源几乎全部东行套利，NWE 大货仅两船，北西班牙 FRN 到 ARA +$19.00/ton 确立 70-min 溢价。 专题（俄罗斯→东方） ：'26 年 1–11 月欧洲俄罗斯东流仅 8.0 mmtons （全年约 8.5，'24/'25 均为 12），俄罗斯占东西套利份额从 '23 年 61% 降至 36% ；纯 Euro–Africa 货仅勉强补缺，合计东向仍钉在约 1.70 mmton/月。 公允价值 ：FOB 受运费+月差双重压缩——印度 MR-AG LR FV 差距自 $170 收窄但仍可观；CFR FV 全线降 $14–17/ton，Chiba 降至 40.0、Yosu 26.0。 SECTION 01 苏伊士以东：从"超级紧张"到普遍回调 East of Suez 12 月平衡：多头逻辑一周内双双失守 市场快速掉头，周五已到处是"回调过头（至少其理由撑不到一月）"的说法。 供应端 ：中东 11 月装载延续 10 月上行趋势；曾被视为主忧的 12 月套利到货持续改善——由 45 周 <1.00 mmtons 增至 46 周约 1.50 mmtons ，且 11 月最终核算近 2.0 mm 、12 月非俄部分（或未结束）已与 11 月的 1.30 mmtons 相当——尘封数周的"rollover（顺延展期）"话题回归。 需求端 ：早在 flat price 回升前，终端用户已明确本月与下月都不提负荷；年末库存管理与大范围转向"最大容差交付"也限制采购。NEA CFR 乙烯–石脑油价差虽有 $300/ton 的健康水平，但单体走强把苦苦挣扎的聚乙烯打亏（PE–ethylene 价差转负）。中国进口因外货骤然便宜于国内 + Gulei 二号裂解装置临近投产而大增，恰好迎头撞上 2H 12 月俄罗斯流入的下行拐点。 图 1 · 东京数字：CFR 石脑油（周均 $/ton，42–46 周 1017→1036→1088→1005→899）、Inter-month 月差与 Brent×7.5 裂解 | Tokyo Numbers, $/ton — Source: NIS, Naphtha International Week 46, p1 70-min CFR 公允价值崩塌： 前月差四个交易日从 $47.00 直落至周五 $24.00（周四仍 $32.00），"评估必须对齐实际成交"在本周 CFR 得到最彻底的证明：周五 Yosu 2H 以 MOPJ + $17.00 成交，Chiba 港溢价从数日前的 $60.00 骤降至约 $30.00。 跌势路径：45 Europeans watched the 70-min price drop in the East. They worried a little. After all, shipments to Asia keep their region’s supply and demand in balance. But they needn’t have. Cracking naphtha gets a huge premium in NEA these days. It fetches much more money there than in Europe. Even when physical dived on Friday, Chiba and Yosu remained much better destinations for Med FRN cargoes than Rotterdam and Antwerp. East of Suez A super-tight East for December? Not anymore. The market reversed course. It did its about-face so quickly Friday brought widespread talk of an overdone correction – or, at least one with a justification which won’t carry into January. Both sides of the balance lost bullishness. Mideast loadings showed November sustaining October’s upward trend. December arb arrivals, once the main cause of concern, steadily improved. Days when requirements drew no offers gave way to days when they got plenty of them. Demand played a role, too. Even before flat-price began to creep upward, end-users made clear they won’t boost runs this month or next. Including prompt premiums, NEA’s CFR ethylene– naphtha spread held at a healthy $300/ton. But monomer improvement ruined the economics of struggling polymers production. PE–ethylene went negative. Naphtha procurement for December was also restricted by end-year inventory management and a broad shift to maximum-tolerance deliveries. Lastly, a large increase in China imports – driven by foreign supply suddenly selling cheaper than domestic and the Gulei No.2 cracker’s approaching start-up – confronts the prospect of a downturn in Russian inflows beginning in 2H December. Maintaining the prompt crack around $200/ton when LR freight nosedived gave Asia the arb result it needed. December arrivals, less than 1.00 mmtons in week 45, grew toward 1.50 mmtons in week 46. Limited end- user buying for 2H (except by China) made that figure sufficient, especially as final accounting for November surpassed expectations at nearly 2.0 mm. In fact, December’s non-Russia portion, perhaps not finished yet, roughly matched November’s 1.30 mmtons. Little wonder “rollovers,” a dormant topic in recent weeks, returned to discussions. But arb trade had a bullish element, too. A devastating UAV attack made assuming Ust-Luga’s splitter naphtha arrivals will drop sharply or even disappear completely by end-December and stay little or nothing into 1Q ’27 perfectly reasonable. 70-min CFR fair-value crashed. Its dive shocked the market. It floated remarkably high just days ago. Then it plunged. Various industry organs have published spreads far-removed from latest physical results for the final stage of 2H December. Based on those results, Naphtha International tracked a front-month plummet from $47.00 to Friday’s $24.00 in four sessions. Even Thursday, the spread was still $32.00. If the need to match spread assessment to deal-done ever needed proof, week-46 CFR provided it. The hammer of reality fell hardest on Friday. Yosu bought 2H for MOPJ plus $17.00/ton. The freight differential to Chiba suggested the port’s value, so recently $60.00, was suddenly about $30.00. At least on Thursday, January’s spread, matched to December’s, gave no indication of a 1H January rebound in week 47. Indeed, main-port buyers which considered pre-period orders reversed to “wait and see.” The last round for 2H December started weakly with domestic sales in Korea in the low $40’s. Then, paper markets began to relax to a degree which called front spreads into doubt. The first physical step downward in week 46 came from Merak: MOPJ minus about $8.00 for 2H December on Wednesday, a cheap result untainted by “special conditions.” As usual, an SEA deal was difficult to translate into an NEA-driven time spread. But given a port premium around $20.00 and a nearly $40.00 freight differential to Korea, the discount was close to the day’s NEA-equivalent fair- value. That bearish level was set by 2H Yosu at a $26.00 premium on Thursday. The buyer also took 1H at $26.50, a hint at emerging prompt length, plus 15 ktons for Daesan in 2H at $32.00–$33.00. Weak premiums weren’t the only market movers. Asia observed plenty of untaken offers for 2H. November’s FEI–MOPJ, showing a low-$70’s premium for spot C3, and C4’s additional $60.00 premium, kept spot procurement off the table. Minor amounts of term C3 continue to arrive in December. Singapore’s “gas-nap” bottomed at $10.00/bbl then revived to $15.00, a move which prevented further decline in blending and, in fact, attracted a USGC C5+ cargo. Korea finalized its ’26 splitter-feed business at 326 cargoes (term and spot) after December touched a seven- month-high thirty lots. The country’s imports declined forty-four cargoes ’25 to ‘26. December’s tally, still well above the prior four-month average of twenty-four, could’ve been even larger if not for late decisions to restrain year-end stocks. Once again, local splitters held down splitting-naphtha purchases by obtaining 0.90–1.00 mmtons of condensate. Splitting outfits have differing views of Skikda value heading into January CFR. Some of them believe gasoil cracks at three-month lows will finally break the stream’s sustained elevation above 70-min plus $30.00, even for the most Skikda-dedicated outlets. Others agree there’s no upside. But they worry about 1H January CFR starting without, as yet, any H-FRN arb commitments. Mailiao withdrew a Thursday HVN/H-FRN tender for any-December, denying the market genuine, transaction-demonstrated naphthenic premiums. The most to be said was Asia believed 70-min’s correction probably limited HVN to a notional level no higher than MOPJ plus low $70’s on a Japan basis. October’s AG exports assessment slipped from 2.75 mmtons to 2.65 after inquiries revealed some end-month activity moved products other than naphtha to market. It’s too early to make a call for the November cycle. 1H nominations have reached 1.20 mmtons. As is normal at this time in the month’s progression, observations for actual sailings from ports and STS points remain well below the 1.20 mm total. Observers expect November’s outflow to continue at October’s rate or, maybe, manage a moderate increase. They don’t see a second surge as likely. Like the wider oil industry, naphtha- watchers noted the volume of crude transiting Hormuz increased considerably more than the volume of any and all products. With the new October tally only 62 percent of the January–February average, Asian naphtha buyers have understandably abandoned hopes for a recovery beyond 3.00 mmtons/month within ’26. Meanwhile, tracking permitted comprehensive analysis of October’s export destinations. Korea led the way with 0.65 mmtons, its best reading since February. Taiwan, at 0.40 mm, revisited its January–February high. Japan and China rounded to 0.35 mmtons. In both cases, the receipts matched year-to-date averages but were understandably higher than March–September paces, rates around 0.25/month. Thailand distinguished itself. Its 0.25 was highest since January, the result of petrochemical-plant capacity re-started late in September. Around 0.20 mmtons each, Indonesia and Singapore were slightly above normal. In an obvious reaction to reduced Russian avails, India took 0.25 mmtons, a yearlong high. India left the trade guessing about November exports climbing above 0.30 mmtons. Non-Reliance has remained unmoved from just 0.07 ex-Chennai. Time for an increase has grown very short. India didn’t export more than it imported in October. Most likely, again in November, it will not have a surplus. Kuwait’s spot LR1 for December 10–25 DES Chiba was done at MOPJ plus $105/ton based on 1H January pricing. West of Suez None of the Western markets generated much cargo-naphtha activity during week 46. New York Harbor and USA’s Gulf coast produced little business of any kind. Barge-lots predominated in NW Europe. Med sellers booked some cargoes to go to Asia. But they didn’t place any supply in southern Europe. Just two sizable cargoes traded in NWE. Sellers only had those two to offer. Med suppliers get a much better return sending their FRN to Asia than to the north. So, they’ve committed essentially all they have to arb business. The absence of Med shipments has left ARA and the rest of the north depending on small parcels from local sources. The Rhine water level has risen enough to allow barge-shipments into Germany. That fresh demand has kept the NWE cracking-naphtha balance tight. LVN and LDF sellers take advantage of that tightness to sell petrochemical companies coaster-lots gasoline blenders don’t want. Some companies mix their light naphtha with hard-to-sell HVN to make 65-min for the ethylene-feed pool, too. A cargo of good- quality north-Spain FRN sold for ARA delivery. It got plus $19.00/ton. That transaction established the 70- min premium. It influenced barge cracking-naphtha value, too. Barge freight runs $7.00–$8.00/ton. So, the FOB sales confirmed plus $19.00 as the top of ethylene-feed-FRN’s range. Some players put the bottom of the range at plus $15.00 on Friday. But that number seemed a little low unless in described what unfamiliar mixtures, like LVN plus HVN, could get. Good refinery LVN appeared able to get plus $18.00–$20.00. In the absence of sales for delivery to steam-crackers on the Continent’s south coast and shipments from the Med to the north, Naphtha International must surmise southern paraffinic FRN has two prices. Sellers would’ve needed a Lavera premium around $37.00–$38.00 on Friday to deliver an MR or larger cargo to a south-coast ethylene plant. Below that premium, they would’ve got a better return sending their FRN to NE Asia. Southern ethylene makers probably wouldn’t pay anywhere near plus $37.00–$38.00. So, they would have to meet their feedstock requirements with parcels too small for economical shipment to far-away destinations. While unlikely, those small cargoes might go to the north today. So, C&F ARA minus the difference between Med/ARA and cross-Med freight gives a decent idea of the south-coast price. That method put the C&F Lavera premium at $18.00–$19.00 on Friday. A cargo of top-quality light gasoline-blending naphtha, North Sea natural gasoline, sold for steam cracking during the week. It fetched plus $37.00. But it went to a plant in the Baltic where freight makes cracker-feed from outside the Baltic more expensive than in ARA. Market participants agree the difference between North Sea natural gasoline’s price and its cracking value has narrowed lately. But the oil continues to get a big enough premium from gasoline blenders to avoid selling as cracker feed except in unusual circumstances. Heavy naphtha demand’s shrunk to almost nothing. Two small parcels sold for reforming during week 46. Refiners must make most of their production disappear. They can adjust cut-points to reduce their yield in some cases. Some of them can increase the amount they reform or blend into their own gasoline. But some of them have had to mix their HVN and LVN to make merchant FRN. That resort has dropped some heavy naphtha’s premium to cracker-feed value. The New York Harbor naphtha market stayed inactive for five days. When asked on Friday, market participants couldn’t name even one trade done between Monday, November 9, and Friday, November 13. Harbor activity gets thin sometimes. But at least something – maybe a barge-load ex-tank, if nothing more – changes hands. If any of that minor trading interrupted week-46’s inactivity, the parties did it very quietly. Several considerations discourage naphtha business. First of all, blenders take advantage of readily available railcar butane to pressurize their mogas. Perhaps they do that because very little seaborne naphtha has reached the Harbor lately. South- Atlantic suppliers send their cargoes elsewhere. Recently, steady inflow of Argentina’s light export mixture has become unsteady. That stream has found buying interest in Asia. The most recent Bonny cargo went to Europe. Europe hasn’t sent much naphtha to New York for months. NWE organizations send semi-finished mogas, CBOB and RBOB, across the Atlantic rather than blending components these days. A cargo of Spanish H-FRN reportedly heads for USA now. But it hasn’t sold in the Harbor. Colonial Pipeline space has become hard to get and expensive. Shippers use the space they have to move mogas blends, not naphtha. Tankers, including foreign-flag ships exempted from the Jones Act, carried naphtha to the Harbor during Summertime. But USG sellers prefer other destinations for their seaborne supply this Autumn. A cargo sailed from Houston at the end of week 45 bound for Point Tupper in Atlantic Canada. Lacking new business, and even guidance for promising negotiations, Naphtha International can’t update prices reported Friday, November 6: light sub- octane at December RBOB minus $0.36 and heavy at minus $0.32. Players described light- naphtha’s week as the dullest they’ve seen in years. Some observers saw the light marker, November Enterprise Belvieu C5+, at one level and some, at another on Friday, November 13. Naphtha International found $1.915/gallon, $773/ton, the most believable reading of the close. The marker went much too high late in October and didn’t fully correct during November’s first week. Friday, the 6th, to Friday, the 13th, it fell $0.085/gallon, $34/ton, 4.3 percent. Gasoline fell even more than that. The December RBOB settle dropped $0.1553/gallon, 5.6 percent, the 6th to the 13th. So, the RBOB-C5 spread fell from $0.7767/gallon on the 6th to $0.7064 on the 13th. But the marker strengthened from 72.0 percent of the settle to 73.1 percent. It didn’t strengthen against crude-oil. The December WTI settle dropped $2.27/bbl, 2.5 percent, the 6th to the 13th. So, the marker weakened from 92.5 percent of the settle to 90.8 percent. Even though the marker corrected, the waterborne sour-light differential fell. We can only guess how far it dropped. High-sulfur natural gasoline and LVN didn’t find much buying interest during the week. Refiners showed no spot requirements. Exporters didn’t look for barge-lots to complete cargoes going overseas. Friday afternoon, a plus $0.01 offer got a minus $0.07 bid. Minus $0.02 seemed a reasonable compromise between an over-optimistic offer and an over-aggressive bid. Despite the market’s correction, sour-light remained too expensive for Canada’s diluent pool. Players didn’t buy any Belvieu supply for shipment to Illinois and onward to Alberta during the week. No doubt they saw no reason to pay a premium while barge buyers looked for discounts. Belvieu producers likely preferred to keep their natural gasoline in the wells rather than sell it below the marker. So, we put injects’ value, what the producers effectively paid themselves for it, at marker parity. Sweet-light got as little buying interest as sour-light during the last few days. Players gave it a notional mid-single-digit value. Waterborne action established heavy-naphtha’s price more clearly than light-naphtha’s during the week. Good blending- quality HVN traded for December RBOB minus $0.52. Reformer feed sold in the minus mid-$0.60’s. Market Analysis: European Russia sends the East less naphtha in ’26 than in ’23, ’24, and ‘25. Reduced Russian naphtha flows to the East in recent months put a spotlight on what remains, despite sanctions, a major component of West-to-East trade. The “energy ceasefire” USA announced in September went nowhere. Ukraine’s indication in October it would stop attacks if Russia did – and its November proposal to halt them if USA supplied Patriot inceptors – quickly shifted to resumption of targeting refineries. Tracing the trend from the war’s beginning in February ’22, annual arrivals from all parts of European Russia raced from 7.70 mmtons in ’22 to 14.10 in ’23. They reached 42 percent and 61 percent of total arb. Then, after sanctions were solidified, ’24 and ’25 volume stabilized at 12 mmtons each. A sharper change of direction, again lower, occurred in ’26. January–November got to 8.0 mmtons, assuring the year will finish not much above 8.50. Because arb from all Western sources hasn’t changed much in recent years, the up and down Russian portion shows in its share of arb as a whole and as a component of the dominant Euro–Africa sailings. This year’s Mideast conflict generated neither an upswing in Russian flows nor a major increase – certainly not as big as Asia expected – in non-Russian cargoes from Euro–Africa. Rather, major change was limited to adjustments in Russian naphtha’s load ports. Within the up and down trend, shipments from the north, almost entirely Ust-Luga, dominated. Arrivals from the Black Sea, affected first by various Asian bans on Russian splitter feed then by severe damage to southern refineries, have taken a bigger hit than supply coming from the Baltic since ’23. Ust-Luga – its condensate-splitter complex and separate terminal loading inland naphtha – sent an average 0.33 mmtons per month to the East in ’22. The various Black Sea streams totaled slightly less, 0.31. A year later, the pace was 0.65 mmtons and 0.48. Novorossiysk and Tuapse, the former frontrunners, basically disappeared since July. Indeed, since mid-April attacks, “Tuapse” exports are believed to be limited to inland naphtha shipped to the coast by rail. Not ‘til ’26 did the Ukraine war slash Russia’s share of overall arbitrage. It initially shot from ‘22’s 42 percent to ‘23’s 61 percent as West sanctions and Asian bans developed slowly. The share was still 52 percent in ’24 and 49 percent in ’25. This year, it’s fallen to 36 percent. Reduced avails, not new obstacles to sales, dropped it that low. Russia remained more than half of total Euro– Africa arb ‘til ’26, averaging 61 percent through 1H ’25 before fading to 0.45 percent. Analysis shows ”pure” arb from ARA, the Mediterranean, and west Africa barely compensated for declining Russian flows. Volume-wise, Russian and other Euro-African ran parallel during January–September ’25, recording monthly rates of 1.05 mmtons and 0.57. Their numbers started deviating in 4Q ’25. Nevertheless, then through November ’26, Russian and the “pure” Euro-African, together, didn’t increase shipments to the East. Despite brief surges – the largest in May – their combined Eastbound arb held close to a 1.70 mmton monthly average. Some major changes occurred in Russian’s destinations. Most obvious was a plunge in Mailiao’s intake following a late ’25 agreement with the EU to stop the installation’s predominantly naphthenic intake. The rest of the East didn’t compensate for Taiwan’s 3.70 mmton decline. Total direct deliveries to other petrochemical outlets contracted 1.20 mm. Even including the additional placements into storage and blending, deliveries outside Taiwan fell 0.90. Pretty much, China and India were left as the remaining outlets for deliveries not first placed into the East’s commercial storage. Yet, neither China nor India increased direct receipts in a notable way. China’s ten-month performance amounted to less than 40 percent of its 2.25 mmton ’25 tally after substantial declines for Dalian (naphthenic) and Yangpu (mostly paraffinic). India will likely beat ’25 in ’26. But performance so far, and still-limited Russian avails, suggest the gain from 2.35 mmtons will be modest. Mundra, entryway for the Bhatinda cracker, replaced Mailiao as the single biggest outlet for direct Russian sales. That said, neither Mundra nor Sikka, the second-largest Indian receiver, was on track for substantial annual growth. Other ports in the country, some of them known as export points in the past, boosted India’s ten-month results. A few SEA crackers took Russian product this year, mainly when bans on sanctioned cargoes were eased at the height of the Mideast crisis. But these ethylene-feed sales didn’t add much to the ’26 tally. Storage and blending were 3.60 mmtons in ’25, one of every three Russian shipments to the East. Distribution between Singapore-area tanks and the AG (Fujairah and Sohar) was 80:20. Around half the Singapore amount went to gasoline blending. For this reason, China’s true Russian intake was considerably larger than the direct-deliveries amount. Netbacks Eastern naphtha prices plunged at the end of week 46. The Asian physical market’s participants and diligent observers know CFR NEA took a beating on Friday. Many other folks don’t. That second crowd, judging by reports published after the close, includes the window world’s trusted and trusting inhabitants. The Microsoft Outlook failure surely inhibited circulation of good information. Even though cracking naphtha’s price declined much more in NEA than in ARA, Med sellers saw their paraffinic FRN got much better netbacks from the East than from north Europe. Med/NWE by MR remained remarkably expensive during week 46. The voyage cost $88/ton on Friday. Meanwhile, Med/NEA by berth-loaded LR declined considerably. LR2 owners appeared ready to take $122/ton for the voyage, $22 less than on the 6th. LR1 owners cut their rate ideas even more, $29/ton, $133 on the 6th to $104 on the 13th. Those concessions compensated for much of the difference between NEA’s and ARA’s price declines. MR owners wanted $128 for the Med/NEA voyage (Red Sea route) on the 13th, about $7 more than on the 6th. But the difference between C&F Tokyo and C&F Rotterdam remained large enough for arb using those most readily available ships to remain workable. Sour-light, premium included and adjusted for Brent movement between 4:30 PM Singapore time and 1:30 Houston time, declined $42/ton the 6th to the 13th. USG/NEA by MR increased about $3/ton. But the netback from Chiba remained much better than the return from Ship-Channel barge business. Anybody who didn’t changed his mind after a decidedly weak Korea 70-min trade on Thursday. Though physical action was limited, it exposed a deepening weakness unlikely to be exhausted during December CFR. December and January spreads plunged. Freight eroded FOB FV more than CFR FV. MR cases were hit hardest. 2H December, January, and February opened at $25.00, $42.00, and $32.00. Week-45’s last trade, a domestic deal at MOPJ plus low- $40’s per ton using thirty-day pricing, spurred an initial week-46 front-spread correction. Tuesday, continued paper weakness lowered February to $28.00 – a move which pulled January to $39.00. Forward weakness infected 2H December, too. 日期： 2026-11-20 （Week 47，K206 期） ｜ 页数： 6 本页为研究学习笔记，观点归属原机构 NIS。 目录 Contents 苏伊士以东：看空情绪从 12 月末蔓延至 1 月，溢价两连崩 苏伊士以西：欧洲掉期连跌三日，美湾轻石脑油"史上最差" 市场分析：NEA 溢价是维系西→东套利之门的关键砝码 净回值与套利价差：东方"示意性"压价未能关闭套利窗口 Key Takeaways · 核心观点 Week 47：裂解、月差、溢价与原油同步下跌，三地全部供应过剩 全球三个定价发现地区（NEA、NWE、USG）的石脑油自身定价要素——裂解价差、月差、品质溢价—— 与油价同步下跌 ；东方想放缓西方套利流入但 未能成功 ：它们降价幅度并不比西方更大。欧洲担心美湾把 LVN 横跨大西洋运来。 东方 ：12 月末的看空情绪蔓延至 1 月。韩国 70-min 在 1H 1 月 CFR 首周大跌约 $15.00/ton ，Yosu 物理成交把 Chiba 值压至 MOPJ+$25.00 ；一周前 Chiba 还被多头情绪抬到 MOPJ+$60.00 。op-tol（opportunity tolerance）切换过量是多头难以招架的导火索。 平衡表反转 ：市场原以为 12 月短缺，但前几个月的过剩（最初被掩盖）使 12 月转为宽松；13 日至 20 日裂解价差暴跌 $70.00/ton ，显示亚洲正在为"不那么短缺的 1 月"重新定价——所需的套利量在减少。 西方 ：欧洲掉期周一至周三连跌、周四小幅反弹、周五回吐一半；USG/ARA MR 运费一周下跌 $29/ton ，令横跨大西洋套利颇具吸引力。美湾轻石脑油市场被称为 "参与者所经历过的最差市场" 。 套利之门仍开 ：东方（含 Brent 调整后）把 70-min C&F Chiba 一周砍价 $88/ton 、鹿特丹砍 $86/ton，但 Med→NEA 与 USG→NEA 套利窗口依然敞开 ——JOSN 与 Chiba 溢价仍高到足以让地中海卖家东行赚钱。 Section 01 苏伊士以东：看空蔓延至 1 月，溢价两连崩 East of Suez — bearishness spills into January 12 月末的看空气氛延续到 1 月，随着 Week 48 的 CFR 结果陆续公布，一轮 大规模回调 蓄势待发。周五时已不难发现： 东方的基本面与流入套利，都没有即期溢价变化得那么快、那么剧烈 。亚洲说套利是关键因素，但套利量——尤其是"pure"纯石脑油船货——的增长相比 Week 45 大家还在谈"超级紧张"平衡时并不显著。疲弱从石蜡基（paraffinic）蔓延到环烷基（naphthenic）贸易，完全无视 1 月的补库需求。买家觉得被之前的 bullish 情绪"骗了"——它曾把 Chiba 值抬到 MOPJ+$60.00/ton ；低需求市场中的卖家则辩解：包括"op-tol"在内的边际供给变化被放大了。所有人都选择关闭东西方套利。 即期溢价第二连崩 ：终端用户在周中前买够了船货，确认即期溢价连续第二周暴跌；充足报价促使他们把采购推迟到 Week 48。韩国 70-min 在 1H 1 月 CFR 首周跌去约 $15.00/ton ，几乎复刻 2H 12 月最后一周的跌幅；Yosu 物理成交 MOPJ+$11.50 把 Chiba 值压至 $25.00 。未售的 12 月桶"从藏身处现身"，叠加进 1H 1 月供应，开始超过看起来还算健康的补库需求。此前 转向最大 op-tol 掺混 的切换明显超多头承受能力。周一 1H 1 月 CFR 开价立刻重申：11 月 13 日的亚洲回调不是孤立事件。两笔日本成交同定在约 MOPJ+$18.00 （鹿岛 2H 12 月：14 kt 按 2H 11 月定价 + 8.5–13.5 kt 按 1H 12 月；水岛买 70-min OSN：25% 按 2H 11 月、75% 按 1H 12 月）。同日 Yosu 两船以 45 天计价、$6.00 溢价成交。日本终端用户 1H 仅剩约 2 个需求；韩国还差 7–8 个现货但 并不着急 ——买家预期 70-min 进一步恶化，且两大内销卖家的 1 月本地量将复刻 12 月水平，Onsan 一带在本地 LVN 销售后料再度过剩。交易商中的激进抛售，把韩国 70-min 预期重置到 30 天定价 MOPJ+low-teens 。周四新加坡一笔 1 月 1–18 整月计价的采购据传接近其 30 天等值——以 low-$20's 折扣 成交，远低于 CFR 长约谈判开始时的水平。亚洲炼厂收率向石脑油倾斜，令新加坡 gas-nap 放宽至 $10.00/bbl 、汽油一个月月差走平。 Fig 1 · 东京数字（周均 $/ton）：CFR 石脑油 43–47 周 1036→1088→1005→899→831，Inter-month 月差与 Brent×7.5 裂解同步下行 | Tokyo Numbers, $/ton — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p1 环烷基与品质溢价 ：1H 1 月环烷基对 MOPJ 溢价走软。A-Grade 的下跌完全归因于 70-min 走低；出乎意料的是，中馏分裂解价差走弱 并未影响 Skikda 的价差 。C-Grade 与 HVN 则在基础回调之上叠加了品质折价扩大。 splitter 进料集中补库 ：韩国 1H 1 月 splitter 进料需求在首周大部分落实——Daesan 锁定 20 kt Skikda（MOPJ+$55.00/ton） 、3 船 Duqm（$32.00）、2 船 SOMO（$35.00）、Milazzo 与另一套利货源各 1 船（$32.00）；次日 Yosu 以 2 船 Skikda（来自某大公司的 新小型长约计划 ，$47.00）与 A/C Grade 期权（$29.00/$22.00）补足——A/C 期权在谈判中又跌了 $7.00–$8.00。亚洲人公认 Yosu 批次代表最新 Skikda 价值，而 B/C 以全部成交均值最具代表性。尽管 Daesan 已大量接货，激进抛售仍持续——这种景象 自去年夏天需求更少时以来首次出现 。Daesan 周四招标后又取消 12 月标购（原因不明）。一船 SEA 真正 HVN 定档日本 2H 12 月，据传结果不高于 MOPJ+$60.00 ，1H 1 月料走向 mid-$50's。 中国与供需平衡 ：JKT 与 SEA 的 1 月需求均上行——前者受补库与 TA（检修）减少驱动，后者受产能恢复驱动；但聚合物走弱足以削弱任何平价驱动的开工提升，上行空间有限。炼厂高开工+汽油注意力下降，使本地石脑油部分替代进口；JKT 自 9 月以来的需求增长并不完全转化为海运活动。中国 10 月后有理由维持高进口：国内供应昂贵、古雷 12 月 5 日开工、惠州裂解装置 11 月末重启；但 Ust-Luga 停运导致俄罗斯可用货源受限 ，可能阻止进口在 11 月之后进一步增长（1 月尤甚）。平衡表上，"12 月短缺"被证伪——前几个月的过剩使 12 月转为宽松；13–20 日裂解价差暴跌 $70.00/ton ，正是亚洲为"不那么短缺的 1 月"重新定价。中国 1–10 月进口累计 10.0 mmtons（同比 -27%） ，全年料略超 12.0 mm （2025 年为 16.8）；1–10 月乙烯产量 34.3 mmtons（+10.7%） 。 Fig 2 · 关键基本面平衡表（mmtons）：JKT 裂解石脑油投料 12 月 4.15→1 月 4.20，中国进口 11 月 1.15→1 月 0.70，东方缺口 12 月 1.80→1 月 1.60 | Key Fundamentals, mmtons — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p1 中东与印度 ：中东 11 月出口难以复刻 10 月的增幅，提名量指向 再度 2.60–2.65 mmtons ，但中东港口实际起航已经滞后——一艘发往日本的 LR1（Navig8 Messi）因 11 月 17 日遇袭 从名单上移除；战争风险溢价上升、AG 内局部通行延误与 STS 作业油轮可用性受限都在侵蚀实际出口。绕行霍尔木兹的陆上管道运力本已为清洁油品满负荷运转。印度平衡可能从缺口大幅摆向过剩：10 月进口创年内新高 0.50 mmtons （史上最大净缺口）后，12–1 月将回落至 仅 AG 供给、总量不超过约 0.15 mmtons 的水平。KPC 12 月 3–4 日现货 LR1 成交价约为 MOPAG-mid-teens ，QE 3–7 日的 fixture 更便宜。 Fig 3 · NEA 品质溢价（全货船，$/ton）：OSN spread 47.0→24.0→19.5，70-min 42.2→17.0→11.5，N+A 稳于 43.0→45.0（1H 1 月交付）| NEA Quality Premiums — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p2 Section 02 苏伊士以西：掉期连跌，美湾"史上最差" West of Suez — swaps slide; worst-ever USG light market 欧洲 ：NWE 石脑油掉期周一、周二、周三连跌，周四小幅回升，周五回吐约一半涨幅——交易者怀疑下跌只是暂停：未来五周看不到需求改善的迹象，而把美湾 sour-light 运往北欧的动机（钱）很足。周末结束时 没有一单 USG→NWE 的 commitment ；但 11 月 13–20 日 USG/ARA MR 运费下跌 $29/ton ，让跨大西洋运输裂解石脑油看起来颇具吸引力。欧洲多头唯一的安慰：美湾卖家把 sour-light 卖去 NEA 比卖 NWE 净回值更高——最终货去哪里，取决于船东愿不愿意让 clean tanker 离开大西洋盆地。 本周以计价基准切换分界 ：周初裂解石脑油按 12 月计价成交，周中后转向 11 月计价，南北溢价因基准不同而迥异。已知来源 65-min 以 12 月交付/12 月计价成交 +$12.00/ton （±$1.00），小批量（barge/coaster）补足了许多需求，溢价一度高达 +$14.00–$15.00 ；周四、周五一船 70-min 以 B/L+5（11 月计价）成交 +$7.00–$8.00 。周五下午 11 月掉期高出 12 月 $7.00——两种基准大体等价。欧洲大陆南岸本周 无蒸汽裂解石脑油成交 ；C&F Lavera 的 +$9.00–$11.00 只是小批量报价（运套利不经济），地中海卖家宁愿以 MR/LR 把船货发往海外或 NWE。高品质汽油调和石脑油 Week 47 难寻买家：一船北海天然汽油以 +$30.00 卖给调和商，调和商转售时却拿不到 +$30.00。HVN 溢价下降，sour heavy 卖到 +$15.00 。 Fig 4 · NWE 石脑油裂解（$/bbl，伦敦时间 17:00）：11 月 -5.05→-7.70、12 月 -4.50→-6.20、1Q -5.35→-5.75、2Q -7.20→-7.30 | NWE Naphtha Cracks — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p3 Fig 5 · NWE 数字（周均 $/ton，42–47 周 966→953→1003→887→844→769）：All-in naphtha、Brent×8.9、裂解×8.9 与 70-min 溢价 | NWE Numbers — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p3 纽约港 ：Week 47 迎来一些轻质低辛烷值船货——此前一周卖家无货可示，本周南美、西非与欧洲货源齐现，在本土低辛烷值组分几近断供时支撑纽约汽油调和。USG 企业用 Colonial Pipeline 管容输运半成品调和油； 油罐车运力受限 抑制宾州 Marcellus 天然汽油发货。阿根廷轻石脑油混合物重新现身，以 12 月 RBOB-$0.48/gallon 成交；贸易商意外推介一船智利 Concepcion（Bio Bio 炼厂）船货；Bonny 天然汽油报 -0.38 周五仍未售；Fos LVN 寻价类似阿根廷货也未售；Marcellus 报 -0.40（FOB 新泽西水域码头）未售，市场估值 low minus-$0.50's。周末时 NWE HVN 看起来卖纽约的净回值优于 ARA 驳船——但那只是基于"12 月 -0.36"的名义假设，并无实际成交。 美湾"史上最差" ：参与者称 Week 47 的美湾轻石脑油市场是其经历过最差的。轻质标杆——11 月 Enterprise Belvieu C5+——10 月高得不可持续：10 月 9 日达 前月 WTI 结算价的 99.0% 、10 月 23 日达 前月 RBOB 结算价的 74.7% ，此后回落但仍不够。最后几天卖家不得不大幅折价出售 sour-light 驳船货。11 月 20 日周五流动性尚存时标杆最高成交 $1.77/gallon（$714/ton） ，收于较 11 月 13 日下跌 $0.145/gallon（$58/ton，-7.6%） ；12 月 RBOB 结算同期跌 $0.1187（-4.5%），标杆从 RBOB-$0.7064 弱化至 RBOB-$0.7327（占结算价比 73.1%→70.7%）；12 月 WTI 跌 $4.58/bbl（-5.2%），标杆占原油结算价比从 90.8% 沉至 88.5% ——相当长时间以来最低，但仍不足以让 sour-light 在驳船市场或 Explorer 注入贸易中获得溢价。水运高硫 LVN 低至 -$0.08/gallon ；sour C5+ 周五拿不到 -0.03，估值 -0.05–-0.04；Explorer 注入最近成交不优于 -0.04–-0.03 ；sweet-light 收于 -0.03 买盘 / +0.03 卖盘，料难越过 0.00。输往南美的稀释剂需求支撑美湾重石脑油：高硫品种周末卖到约 12 月 RBOB-$0.60 ，低硫品种靠汽油调和兴趣略好于一船 -0.53 的成交。 Fig 7 · 美湾溢价（$/gallon，waterborne，delivered）：sour light (-0.05–-0.04)、sweet light (-0.01)–0.00、C5+ injects (-0.04–-0.03)、reforming HVN (-0.60–-0.59)、blending HVN (-0.54–-0.53) | US Gulf Coast Premiums — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p4 Section 03 市场分析：NEA 溢价是西→东套利之门的关键砝码 Market Analysis — NEA premiums keep West-to-East arbs workable Week 45 的市场分析曾展示西方品质溢价如何调控裂解石脑油套利；本期更进一步： 把 Chiba、Yosu 对 MOPJ 的溢价（即实际成交所体现的）加入套利等式 ，比较把船货运往东方（NEA）与留在西方的净回值，判断哪个出口更划算。以 USG sour-light 为例："USG Arb Sensitivity"红线=德州 sour-light 本地驳船净回值与 Yosu LR1 交付净回值之差；蓝线在红线上再剔除 Yosu 溢价的影响（只用 JOSN 作为交付价）。 Fig 8 · 美湾套利敏感性 LR1（$/ton，'25 年 1 月–'26 年 10 月）：红线=JOSN+Yosu 溢价-标杆+溢价，蓝线=仅 JOSN-标杆+溢价 | USG Arb Sensitivity, LR1 — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p4 LR1 口径（'25 年 1 月–'26 年 10 月，共 22 个月） ：若交付价只用 JOSN，sour-light 卖 Yosu LR1 净回值优于休斯顿地区驳船客户的月份为 13 个；若交付时能拿到 JOSN+Yosu 溢价，LR1 船货净回值胜出 19 个月 。约四分之一的时间里， Yosu 溢价本身就是套利之门开合的决定因素 。22 个月中溢价均值 $21.62/ton （'25 年 $6.40；'26 年 1–10 月 $39.61），把 LR1 套利可行的时间占比从 59% 提升到 86% 。 Fig 9 · 美湾套利敏感性 MR（$/ton）：组织 MR 船期比 LR1 更容易，sour-light 套利门在 2 月 28 日伊朗冲突升级前从未大幅开合 | USG Arb Sensitivity, MR — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p5 MR 口径 ：'26 年 2 月 28 日伊朗冲突激化之前的 14 个月里，套利门从未大幅开合。不计溢价，卖 Yosu MR 净回值优于 Ship-Channel 驳船的月份仅 5/14，均值低 $3.12/ton； 计入溢价后 11/14 个月胜出，均值高 $3.34 。3–6 月 '26 因东方过度反应（竭力吸引西方货源替代中东损失、又吸来太多）而失去参考性。7–10 月回归常态后溢价的作用清晰化：Yosu 那几个月并没从 USG 吸走多少裂解石脑油（东行货多去日本、新加坡），JOSN 单独定价使 Ship-Channel 处置在全部 4 个月都优于套利； 溢价均值 $10.93，把 MR 套利从 0/4 提升到 3/4 个月占优 ；同期 Chiba 溢价均值 $19.58，同样把套利从 0/4 拉到 3/4。 Fig 10 · 地中海套利敏感性（$/ton）：红线=JOSN+Chiba 溢价-掉期+65/70-min 溢价；蓝线剔除 Chiba 溢价 | Med Arb Sensitivity — Source: NIS, Naphtha International K206, p5 地中海口径 ：NEA 边际石蜡基石脑油来自 USG，而匹配东方需求的主要西方套利来自欧洲（尤其地中海）。'25 年 1 月–'26 年 10 月的大多数月份，JOSN 单独定价就足以让石蜡基 FRN 以 LR1 东行日本、净回值优于 MR 西行 ARA（LR2 套利通常可行，直到今夏 LR2 运价飙升）。Chiba 溢价在 22 个月中只有 4 个月真正决定套利门开合，但它可能在未来变得重要： LR1 运价已升得很高，'26 年前 10 个月溢价只打开过一次 LR1 套利门 。10 月单月：JOSN 单独使 Chiba 净回值比 ARA 低 $4.69/ton；加上溢价后 Chiba 净回值反超 $24.67 ——足以逆转的溢价也让 Med→日本 MR 套利相当可观。 Section 04 净回值与套利价差：压价未能关闭套利窗口 Netbacks — Eastern price-slashing leaves arb gates open 东方发现西来的石脑油已超过早-'27所需，于是 "示意性"（gestured）地 试图抑制流入——Naphtha International 强调只是"示意"：借助 Brent 下跌，含溢价、并按新加坡 16:30 与伦敦 17:00 之间 Brent 波动调整后的 70-min C&F Chiba 一周砍价 $88/ton （11 月 13→20 日），但 没有关闭 Med→NEA 套利门 ——JOSN 与 Chiba 溢价仍高到足以让地中海卖家把石蜡基 FRN 运往 NEA 赚钱。含溢价的 70-min C&F 鹿特丹同期下跌 $86 。运费没帮东方的忙：Med/NEA LR1 运费一周仅降 $21/ton、MR（红海航线）降 $16，而 Med/ARA MR 降了 $20——于是 20 日日本对西地中海的净回值 按 LR1 计比 ARA 高 $73（与 13 日持平） 、按 MR 计高 $54（比 13 日多 $5）。 USG→NEA 套利门同样大开 ：sour-light 含水运折扣、按休斯顿 13:30 调整后一周下跌 $81/ton ；USG/NEA LR1 运费降 $14、MR 降 $16。把 sour-light 送往 Chiba 而非卖休斯顿驳船市场的激励，从 13 日的 $51/ton 升至 20 日的 $65（LR1） 、从 $58 升至 $74（MR） 。 Fig 11 · 净回值比较（$/ton，FOB 装货港，经 Brent 调整至伦敦 17:00）：USG sour-light FOB $676；USAC blending 763/758、ARA cracking 719/712（Med/Red Sea）、NEA cracking 80 经 Red Sea 763、AG 633 | Netbacks Comparison — International K206, p6 结论： Week 47 三地齐跌但结构分化——东方用 $88/ton 的砍价"示意"截流西方套利，可 Med→NEA、USG→NEA 的套利门依旧敞开（激励反而从 $51 扩大到 $65–$74/ton）；NEA 品质溢价（Yosu/Chiba 对 MOPJ）持续扮演套利门开合的边际砝码，在 '26 年前 10 个月平均把 LR1 套利可行概率从 59% 抬到 86%。后续关注 Week 48 CFR 结果对即期溢价的进一步确认，以及中东实际装船与俄罗斯货源恢复的节奏。 本页为原文精读笔记，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属原机构 NIS（Naphtha Information Services Pte Ltd）。原文版权归 NIS 所有。

reports.ftext: www.spglobal.com/energy Platts Oilgram News Volume 104 / Issue 220 / November 9, 2026 Inside this issue PetroChina diversifies crude supply, shipping amid Middle East disruptions: exec  Middle East disruptions reshape China's crude sourcing  Russian, South American barrels partly fill supply gap  PetroChina uses controlled fleet, pipelines to secure supplies PetroChina has tapped diversified crude supplies, controlled shipping capacity and its global trading network to maintain oil flows amid Middle East disruptions that have tightened supply and pushed up freight costs, Luo Yizhou, general manager of PetroChina International Co. Ltd., said at the 15th China International Oil and Gas Trade Congress in Shanghai on Nov. 8. The company's international trading arm accounted for 18.1% of China's crude imports over January-September 2026, making its response significant for crude flows into the world's largest importing market, Luo said. Middle East tensions this year at one point disrupted more than 12 million barrels/day of crude flows and triggered more than 16 million b/d of oil production cuts within the Gulf, according to figures cited by the executive. Freight rates on some routes surged as much as tenfold. The impact extended beyond Middle Eastern routes, as increased use of tankers for ship-to-ship transfers in the region reduced available tonnage elsewhere and pushed up freight rates globally. The disruption has also reshaped China's crude sourcing. The share of China's crude imports from the Middle East fell 12.5% year over year over January-September, while the shares from Russia and South America rose 6% and 5.2%, respectively, according to customs data cited in the speech. The shift showed Russian and South American barrels filling  Clean power push takes center stage in Antalya  Electrification pace must quadruple to hit 35% by 2035 goal  Carbon funding shortfall threatens Article 6 progress The UN Climate Change Conference opens in Antalya, Turkey, Nov. 9 against one of the most turbulent backdrops in the Paris Agreement's history, as energy market disruptions, geopolitical fractures and a widening gap between climate commitments and real-world delivery converge at a summit that has placed electrification at the heart of its agenda. COP31, running Nov. 9-20 under a joint Turkish-Australian presidency, arrives as global average temperatures have already breached the 1.5-degree-C threshold that governments pledged to defend in Paris more than a decade ago. This year's Strait of Hormuz crisis disrupted roughly a fifth of global oil and LNG trade, exposing the vulnerability of fossil fuel-dependent economies and adding urgency to the case for accelerating the energy transition. “While climate cooperation remains an area of shared interest, achieving consensus is becoming more difficult as national strategic, economic and security priorities diverge,” Sara Giordano, senior principal analyst at S&P Global Energy CERA, said in a recent note. Electrification push The centerpiece of the COP31 agenda is the “35 by 35” Global Electrification Pledge unveiled by the Turkish COP31 Presidency, which aims to raise electricity's share of global final energy consumption from just over 20% to 35% by 2035. All rights reserved. 2 Asia Pacific China extends US tariff suspension, keeps LNG at 25%, crude at 20%  24-percentage-point tariff suspension extended for two months  Separate US LNG, crude tariffs remain in place  China monitors potential US Section 301 tariff shift China will extend for two months the suspension of a 24-percentage-point additional tariff on US-origin goods while retaining a 10% reciprocal tariff, according to a Nov. 9 announcement by China's State Council Tariff Commission. The measure takes effect at 1:01 pm on Nov. 10 and applies to imports covered by the commission's 2025 Announcement No. 4. China said the extension implements the consensus reached by the US and Chinese leaders in Busan and is intended to provide a relatively stable and predictable policy environment for businesses. This means US LNG remains subject to a combined 25% additional tariff, comprising the retained 10% reciprocal levy and a separate 15% tariff imposed on US LNG in February 2025. US crude also remains subject to a combined 20% additional tariff, including the retained 10% levy and a separate 10% crude- specific tariff. Coal, however, was included in a tariff-reduction framework announced in September, although implementation remained subject to completion of domestic legal procedures, Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, reported Sept. 28. The rates refer to additional tariffs imposed as part of China's trade countermeasures and do not necessarily represent all duties or charges payable on an import. The retained 10% additional tariff also continues to apply to other covered US goods, including commercial soybeans. China separately announced tariff relief in September for a range of US agricultural products including corn, wheat, sorghum, soybean oil and meal and animal proteins, while excluding commercial soybeans, Platts reported earlier. Energy flows remain constrained Regular customs-cleared imports of US LNG into China effectively halted after Feb. 6, 2025. Individual US-origin cargoes subsequently reached Chinese terminals in July and August 2026, although the trading and logistics arrangements did not necessarily result in the LNG being cleared into China's domestic market. Chinese buyers holding flexible US FOB supply have instead been able to resell, swap or reload cargoes to manage their exposure to Chinese import tariffs, Platts reported previously. Market participants have also said that demand and cargo economics, rather than tariffs alone, would determine whether direct US LNG imports resume. US crude flows have also been constrained by the additional 20% tariff. Chinese refiners had gone about nine months without US crude imports before considering a resumption during the Middle East supply crisis in March 2026, Platts reported earlier. Trade truce extended The latest tariff extension comes after the US and China agreed to extend their broader trade truce, previously scheduled to expire on Nov. 10, until Jan. 10, 2027, giving the two sides additional time to address outstanding trade measures. The State Council Tariff Commission said Nov. 9 that China had noted repeated US statements about potentially using Section 301 tariffs to replace tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA), which had been ruled invalid. China will continue monitoring subsequent US measures and adjust its tariff countermeasures as appropriate, according to the commission. — Cindy Liang - LNG Market Specialist AKR to buy out BP’s stake in Indonesian fuel retail joint venture  Buys BP's 49.9% stake in APR for $14.2M  BP still focused on Tangguh LNG operations  Comes amid BP global portfolio rethink Indonesia's AKR Corporindo will take full ownership of fuel retailer PT Aneka Petroindo Raya (APR) after two of its subsidiaries agreed to acquire BP's 49.9% stake in the joint venture for $14.2 million, the company said Nov. 9. In an Indonesia Stock Exchange filing, AKR said its subsidiaries PT Anugerah Krida Retailindo (AKRIDA) and PT Andahanesa Abadi (ADH) had jointly agreed to acquire 11,444,565 shares held by BP Global Investments Limited, representing 49.9% of APR's issued and paid-up capital. The shares were valued at $14,221,500 under a share purchase agreement signed by the parties. AKRIDA previously held 50.1% of APR, with BP owning the remaining 49.9%. Upon completion of the transaction, AKRIDA will hold all but one share of APR, while ADH will own the remaining share, giving the AKR group full ownership of the company, it said. BP and AKR signed a joint venture agreement in April 2017 to develop a fuel retail business in Indonesia. The venture established APR, which operates under BP AKR Fuels Retail, according to the company's website. BP's divestment is part of its ongoing portfolio reshaping strategy, aimed at supporting growth and improving performance across its business, James Tehubijuluw, BP Indonesia's country head, told Platts Nov. 9. New BP CEO Meg O'Neill, who took over in April, has set out plans to create a simpler, stronger and more valuable company. “BP has agreed to divest its 49.9% interest in PT Aneka Petroindo Raya (APR) to PT Anugerah Krida Retailindo (AKR). As a result of the transaction, BP will exit the joint venture,” Tehubijuluw said. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 9, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 3 The divestment will not affect BP's other Indonesian operations, particularly its upstream business and Tangguh LNG project, Tehubijuluw said. “This decision does not change the importance of Indonesia to BP or affect BP’s Tangguh LNG operations and our growth agenda in the upstream,” he said. “Indonesia continues to be an important part of BP’s global portfolio. Tangguh remains a strategic asset within BP’s upstream portfolio in the region.” BP's divestment follows Shell's decision to transfer its fuel retail business in Indonesia to SEFAS Group, which was completed on Oct. 30. The business now operates through PT Isla Energy Indonesia and includes around 200 Shell-branded fuel stations, related fuel supply and distribution operations, and a terminal in Gresik, East Java, Platts has reported. France's TotalEnergies and Malaysia's Petronas were also active in Indonesia's fuel retail market in 2006, but eventually relinquished their operations. — Anita Nugraha China's INE crude futures volume drops 46% MOM to four-month low in Oct  Oct traded volume reaches 3.46 million lots  Delivery volume surges tenfold in October The volume of crude oil futures traded on the Shanghai International Energy Exchange declined 46.15% month over month to 3.46 million lots in October from 6.42 million lots in September, reaching a four-month low, exchange data showed Nov. 6. The INE crude oil futures contract (SC) is a physical settlement contract priced and traded in yuan, having first been listed in March 2018. One lot is equivalent to 1,000 barrels. Following suit, the total traded volume for the front-month November SC futures contract was at 606,556 lots in October, decreasing 74.52% from the 2.38 million lots that the then front- month October SC futures contract had recorded in September, the exchange data showed. The INE crude futures contract comprises crudes of mostly medium, sour quality, including grades such as Dubai, Upper Zakum, Murban, Oman, Qatar Marine, Basrah Light, Basrah Medium, Tupi, Buzios, Djeno and Shengli. These are delivered to various storage facilities across coastal China, such as Zhoushan, Dalian and Shandong. “The overall trading volume was contracting over the month as activity of short-term speculative capital declined,” said a source with a futures company. October also saw fewer trading days in China due to the Golden Week holiday. Crude throughput at China's state-owned refineries faces further downward pressure in November as high feedstock costs and weakening margins prompt some plants to consider voluntary run cuts on top of scheduled maintenance, Platts reported earlier. December cash Dubai assessments averaged $110.73/barrel in October, down from an average of $113.711/b for front-month November cash Dubai in September, while the Dubai cash-futures spread — a measure of the market structure — averaged $8.10/b in October, down from $21.60/b in September, data from Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, showed. Meanwhile, total open interest for the futures contract was 63,195 lots Oct. 30, up 1.02% from 62,556 lots at the end of September. Contrastingly, the open interest for the front-month November SC futures was at 1,295 lots as of Oct. 30, down 34.60% from the front-month October SC futures at 1980 lots Sept. 30. The crude oil delivery volume in October was at 1,980 lots, or 1,980,000 barrels, a tenfold rise from that delivered over September. The fuel oil stockpiles, which had slipped to a two-week low in the week ended Oct. 28, were now at their highest since Sept. 23, when they stood at 19.78 million barrels, the Enterprise Singapore data compiled by Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, showed. This week’s stocks, however, were 21.8% lower than the corresponding week in 2025, according to the data. The weekly residual fuel stocks in Singapore have averaged about 20.6 million barrels so far in 2026, compared with a weekly average of 22.8 million barrels in 2025, and an average ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 9, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 4 of 19.7 million barrels in 2024, according to the Enterprise Singapore data. Singapore’s fuel oil exports fell 29% from the preceding week to about 328,265 mt in the week ended Nov. 4, with shipments to China dropping for a second straight week to 111,005 mt, down nearly 20% from the preceding week, the data showed. Although there were no fuel oil exports to Sri Lanka in the latest week, the city-state’s fuel oil exports to Bangladesh more than doubled week over week to 49,421 mt in the week ended Nov. 4, the data showed. Meanwhile, Singapore’s overall fuel oil imports slipped 12.9% week over week to 1.001 million mt in the week to Nov. 4, while inflows from suppliers within the Asian region climbed 5.7% week over week to 459,830 mt in the latest week, according to the data. The city-state’s imports from neighboring Malaysia rose about 15% week over week to 250,912 mt in the week to Nov. 4, while Singapore also imported 72,935 mt from Thailand and 15,364 mt of fuel oil from Vietnam in the latest week, compared with none from these countries in the preceding week, the data showed. Singapore also imported 78,241 mt of fuel oil from Europe in the week to Nov. 4, of which 39,854 mt came from France and the remainder from Italy. However, there were no fuel oil arrivals from Russia in the latest week, the data showed. Fuel oil imports from the Middle East fell nearly 9% from the previous week to 341,331 mt, of which 145,559 mt came from the UAE, about 109,049 mt from Iraq, 50,501 mt from Kuwait, and the rest from Oman, the data showed. Singapore's inventory data counts only stocks at onshore terminals. Enterprise Singapore describes heavy distillates as “residues,” which include cracked and straight run fuel oil and low sulfur waxy residue. In the downstream market, Singapore bunker premiums for the low and high fuel oil grades fell amid more aggressive selling, on the back of a weaker fuel oil complex in the week to Nov. 5, according to local traders. While spot inquiry flows were modest for most of the week, persistent constraints on prompt availability limited trades for H1 November deliveries, traders noted. Platts assessed the Singapore-delivered 0.5%S marine fuel bunker premium over the benchmark FOB Singapore marine fuel 0.5%S cargo assessments down 3.5% week over week at $99.70/ mt Nov. 5. Offer levels for H2 November loading LSFO ex-wharf cargoes eased to premiums of low-$40s/mt, compared with $45-$50/mt premiums seen the week before. Meanwhile, November HSFO ex-wharf offers also declined to premiums of around $60/mt in the week to Nov. 5, from prior week premiums of $65-$70/mt. Platts assessed the Singapore-delivered 380 CST HSFO bunker premium over the FOB Singapore 380 CST HSFO cargo values at $70.73/mt on Nov. 5, 18.5% lower week over week. — Koustav Samanta, Iris Leung Europe, Middle East and Africa Operations at Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline unaffected by fresh attack: SPA  Pipeline sustains attack, fire extinguished  Saudi loads 2.8 mil b/d at Yanbu in October  Capacity expansion planned beyond 7 mil b/d Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline, a key conduit linking eastern fields with the western port of Yanbu, came under attack again on Nov. 9, although there was no impact on operations, state news reported. In a statement, the Saudi Press Agency quoted an official source at the Saudi energy ministry as saying the 7 million barrel/ day pipeline was “targeted” in the Medina region, “resulting in a limited fire that was extinguished by emergency response teams.” No injuries or fatalities were reported, the official said, adding that “emergency response teams and specialized technical teams responded immediately following the attack and took the necessary measures to secure the site and ensure its safety.” It did not speculate on who was responsible for the attack. Representatives for Saudi Aramco did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Platts Nov. 9. The 1,200 km pipeline — which is connected to the huge crude processing facility in Abqaiq — represents an alternative export route for Saudi crude flows in the event of disruptions through the pivotal Strait of Hormuz, which hosted 20 million b/d of crude and products prior to the US-Iran war in February. After war broke out, the kingdom quickly rerouted flows through the East-West Piepline, but it came under attack by drones in early September, Riyadh said, resulting in a days-long shutdown. By Oct. 6, the pipeline was back pumping 5.8 million b/d, according to state media. In an earnings call on Nov. 3, meanwhile, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser told analysts that the pipeline is undergoing preliminary engineering work for a “major” expansion to take capacity to “much more” than its existing 7 million b/d. The kingdom exported 4.8 million b/d of crude oil in October, 2.8 million b/d of it from Yanbu, according to data from S&P Global Commodities at Sea. Prior to the US-Iran war, which constrained flows through Hormuz, Saudi Arabia exported around 6.8 million b/d, according to CAS. Last week, Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, reported that Saudi Aramco had lowered its December official selling price differentials for its crude grades bound for Asia, Europe, and the Mediterranean, citing a notice from the producer. Aramco set the December OSP differential for its flagship Arab Light bound for Asia at a $7/b discount to the Oman/Dubai average, declining by another $2/b from the previous month, the notice said. Super Light, Extra Light, Medium, and Heavy’s December OSP differentials also decreased by $2/b. — Charlie Mitchell ©2026 S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 5 COSCO plans 24-VLCC fleet expansion through newbuild orders, leasing deals  Chinese state-run tanker firm orders 10 VLCCs  14 VLCCs to come from six Chinese lessors  Fleet adds dual-fuel ships for emissions cuts COSCO Shipping Energy Transportation plans to add another 24 Very Large Crude Carriers to its fleet through newbuild orders and bareboat charters, the world’s largest tanker operator said on Nov. 9, betting on future growth of crude transportation amid strong market conditions. In regulatory filings, the Shanghai- and UNV2-listed company said that 10 newbuild VLCCs were contracted at two Chinese yards while unveiling plans to lease another 14 from six Chinese banks, all of them due to be delivered by the end of 2030. “The Group is responding to the trend of growing global crude oil transportation demand by adding scarce VLCC tanker capacity, expanding fleet scale and capturing market opportunities,” the Chinese state-backed company said. The large investment has come as VLCC rates have reached record highs this year, boosted by increased ship requirements as ton-mile demand grows during shipping disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz. The Platts Global VLCC Index for scrubber-fitted, eco ships jumped from $218,080/day on Feb. 27 to a record $1,195,157/day on Oct. 9 before easing back to $1,044,559/day on Nov. 8, still a historically high level. Platts is part of S&P Global Energy. Deals Through a subsidiary, COSCO Shipping Energy has spent 9.482 billion yuan ($1.42 billion) ordering 10 VLCCs from Yangzhou COSCO Shipping Heavy Industry and four from Dalian Shipbuilding Industry Co., according to the filings. Yangzhou COSCO — ultimately controlled by China COSCO Shipping, parent of COSCO Shipping Energy — will deliver four ships between August 2029 and November 2030. The other four ships are due to be delivered by Dalian Shipbuilding between September 2029 and May 2030. Separately, COSCO Shipping Energy said it plans to bareboat charter 14 newbuild VLCCs from six Chinese financial leasing companies for periods of up to 20 years. Total lease payments will be capped at 17.4 billion yuan, with the tankers expected to be delivered progressively by the end of 2030. The leasing counterparties are BOCOM Financial Leasing, ICBC Financial Leasing, ABC Financial Leasing, BOC Financial Leasing, CITIC Financial Leasing and Minsheng Financial Leasing. They will provide four, three, three, one, two and one VLCCs, respectively. “Supplementing VLCC capacity through bareboat leasing can effectively reduce overall financial costs and one-off capital investment,” COSCO Shipping Energy said. Alternative fuels Of the 14 leased VLCCs, 10 will have LNG dual-fuel propulsion, while the remaining four will be conventionally powered. Following simple retrofits, the six Yangzhou newbuilds will be able to run on LNG, while the four Dalian vessels could be powered by LNG or methanol, according to the company. The efforts to run on fuels with lower greenhouse gas emissions than conventional, oil-based fuels came as COSCO Shipping Energy “actively respond to the global shipping decarbonization trend, conform with the company’s sustainable development strategy and help improve the vessels’ competitiveness throughout their full life cycle,” the company said. “Through the addition of VLCC tanker capacity, the Group will optimize the age structure of its international tanker fleet, enhance the fleet’s intelligent and green development, and improve fleet operating efficiency,” COSCO said. — Max Lin Czech oil players to replace remaining Russian volumes in state reserves  50% of Czech stocks are Russian crude  CPC Kazakhstan blend selected for storage  Stocks support Litvinov, Kralupy plants Czech oil refinery, transportation and state storage companies are working together to replace the remaining Russian oil held in the country’s strategic stockpiles – which amounts to around half – a spokesperson for its state reserves authority told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, on Nov. 9. On Nov. 6, Czech oil refiner Orlen Unipetrol, state-owned oil pipeline company Mero, and the State Authority for Management of Strategic Reserves signed a cooperation agreement paving the way for a phase-out of Russian crude from the country’s reserves. “We currently have around half [Russian] oil in reserves for Unipetrol’s refineries,” Jakub Linka, an SSHR spokesman, said in a telephone interview, with the remainder “a Norwegian oil mix [including] Johan Sverdrup for the Litvinov refinery, and an Azeri mix for the Kralupy refinery.” He added: “The memorandum is a first step in replacing the remaining Russian oil which amounts to half, 45 days out of the European Union’s obligatory 90-day oil reserve.” Linka said a further agreement still needs to be signed by the three parties setting out the specific timelines and other details of the oil reserves switch. Orlen Unipetrol has selected a CPC Kazakhstan-type oil blend as its preferred crude to be kept in the state reserves for possible emergency use, as it can be used by both Czech refineries. The larger Litvinov refinery is capable of processing oil with a higher sulfur content, while Kralupy uses a lower sulfur mix. The three Czech oil players still have to determine how suitable the CPC blend is for long term storage, Linka added. “The evaluation could take a year or more, this will be covered by the ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 9, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 6 final agreements,” he said. The Czech Republic switched its oil supply to exclude Russian flows in March 2025 – amid a broad European shift away from Russian hydrocarbons following the Ukraine war – and now gets crude via the Trans-Alpine Pipeline, beginning at the Italian port of Trieste. The European country was previously largely reliant on Russian oil transported by the huge Druzhba pipeline system. The Litvinov refinery has an annual capacity to process 5.8 million metric tons of oil, while Kralupy is smaller at 3.3 million mt/year. — Chris Johnstone QatarEnergy takes stake in Chevron oil block offshore Namibia  Chevron's stake in PEL 82 falls to 55%  Block sits in Walvis Basin  Namibian officials eye first oil from 2030 QatarEnergy has reached an agreement to acquire 25% of an offshore exploration block in Namibia's Walvis Basin from a subsidiary of Chevron, according to a QatarEnergy statement on Nov. 9, marking its fifth acreage acquisition in the emerging oil producer. Chevron’s operated interest in Petroleum Exploration License 82 will be reduced to 55% as part of the deal, which is subject regulatory approvals, QatarEnergy said. Meanwhile, Custos Energy and state-run Namcor E&P will also each hold a 10% interest, it said. The agreement covers blocks 2112B and 2212A in Namibia's Walvis Basin, which has in recent years played second fiddle to the Orange Basin, where huge discoveries by TotalEnergies and Shell in 2022 triggered an intense competition for acreage by some of the world's largest oil companies. BP farmed into a trio of Walvis Basin blocks earlier this year, reflecting increased interest from international oil companies. “We are pleased to further strengthen our relations with Chevron through this agreement, and to expand and diversify our footprint in Namibia,” Qatari energy minister Saad al-Kaabi said in the statement. The exploration license covers about 11,444 square kilometers in water depths ranging from 350 meters to 2,300 meters, QatarEnergy said. Chevron said previously that it was considering drilling an exploration well on PEL 82 in 2026. The deal is the latest in a string of Namibia acquisitions by the Gulf national oil company. QatarEnergy already holds stakes in Shell's prolific PEL 39 block, TotalEnergies' PEL 56 — which contains the huge Venus oil discovery — and Chevron's PEL 90, where an exploration well is being lined up for late 2026. Norway's Equinor recently farmed into PEL 90 as well. Namibian officials are hoping to achieve first oil in around 2030 and estimate that the country holds over 11 billion barrels of crude oil. reports.ftext: Volume 104 / Issue 215 / November 9, 2026 (continued on page 14) Market analysis International Crude PetroChina diversifies crude supply, shipping amid Middle East disruptions: exec  Middle East disruptions reshape China's crude sourcing  Russian, South American barrels partly fill supply gap  PetroChina uses controlled fleet, pipelines to secure supplies PetroChina has tapped diversified crude supplies, controlled shipping capacity and its global trading network to maintain oil flows amid Middle East disruptions that have tightened supply and pushed up freight costs, Luo Yizhou, general manager of PetroChina International Co. Ltd., said at the 15th China International Oil and Gas Trade Congress in Shanghai on Nov. 8. The company's international trading arm accounted for 18.1% of China's crude imports over January-September 2026, making its response significant for crude flows into the world's largest importing market, Luo said. Middle East tensions this year at one point disrupted more than 12 million barrels/day of crude flows and triggered more than 16 million b/d of oil production cuts within the Gulf, according to figures cited by the executive. Freight rates on some routes surged as much as tenfold. The impact extended beyond Middle Eastern routes, as increased use of tankers for ship-to-ship transfers in the region reduced available tonnage elsewhere and pushed up freight rates globally. The disruption has also reshaped China's crude sourcing. The share of China's crude imports from the Middle East fell 12.5% year over year over January-September, while the shares from Russia and South America rose 6% and 5.2%, respectively, according to customs data cited in the speech. The shift showed Russian and South American barrels filling part of the Middle East supply gap, highlighting the importance of alternative crude sources as geopolitical risks disrupt established trade flows, Luo said. Shipping, supply flexibility PetroChina sources crude from more than 30 countries and over 100 grades, providing flexibility to redirect purchases when individual supply sources or transportation routes are disrupted. Following the outbreak of the Middle East conflict, PetroChina's international trading arm activated emergency measures and directed a fully loaded tanker in the Gulf (continued on page 3) OIL FUTURES: Crude extends decline as concerns about US-Iran escalation fade  Trump meets with Qatari prime minister  Weekly Hormuz traffic lowest since September Crude prices settled sharply lower Nov. 9 session as concerns of an imminent US-Iran escalation faded. NYMEX December WTI settled down $3.98/b (4.4%) at $86.85/b, and ICE January Brent ended the session $5.75/b (5.9%) lower at $92.57/b. “The US and Iran appear to be engaged in negotiations on several levels, while Washington has suspended its attacks for the time being,” CMC Markets analyst Andreas Lipkow said in a note Nov. 9. “However, the situation remains fragile. Isolated attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz demonstrate just how quickly tensions could escalate again. Although the geopolitical risk premium in financial markets has declined significantly, it has by no means disappeared entirely,” he added. US President Donald Trump met with Qatari Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman al-Thani on Nov. 9 in a closed-door meeting. “President Trump continues to signal no appetite for further escalation with Iran, keeping downward pressure on crude oil prices,” TD Securities analyst Ryan McKay and Bart Melek said in a Nov. 9 note. “As such, constant headlines of deal talks/progress will likely suppress upside for now, but further material downside should be limited without a concrete deal.” NYMEX December RBOB settled 12.58 cents/gallon lower at Platts Oilgram Price Report News www.spglobal.com/energy ©2026 S&P Global Inc. The window for securing vessels subsequently shortened to three to five days from a normal two to three weeks, highlighting the value of PetroChina's controlled shipping capacity during the disruption. PetroChina's controlled vessels have handled more than 100 million metric tons/year for four consecutive years, operating across more than 300 routes. The company also coordinated with partners to maintain and increase pipeline oil and gas supplies when seaborne routes were under pressure. The ability to switch between supply sources and transportation routes has become increasingly important for Chinese refiners as higher freight rates raise delivered crude costs and Middle East disruptions increase uncertainty over feedstock availability. Global trading network PetroChina's international trading business operates through hubs in Asia, Europe and the Americas, with operations spanning more than 120 countries and regions. Its trading volumes have averaged more than 500 million mt/ year over the past five years, with annual trading value exceeding $280 billion, allowing the company to reallocate supplies between regions when disruptions emerge. The trading arm also accounted for 70.7% of China's natural gas imports over January-September, while PetroChina's gas sourcing covers about 90% of global gas-producing regions, Luo said. PetroChina is also expanding trading in biofuels, carbon products and critical minerals, with its green trading volume increasing nearly eightfold over the past five years. However, oil and gas remain central to the company's supply strategy as disruptions to Middle Eastern production and shipping continue to alter crude trade flows and raise transportation costs. — Daisy Xu - Oil Market Specialist Azeri Light crude December loadings at Ceyhan rise to 511,612 b/d  15.9 million barrels scheduled to load in Dec  Socar set to load 70% of 23 cargoes Loadings of Azeri Light crude at the Turkish port of Ceyhan are scheduled to total 511,612 barrels/day in December, according to a copy of the program seen Nov. 9 by Platts, part of S&P Global Energy. A total of 15.9 million barrels is scheduled to load in December, up from 15.1 million barrels in November. The number of cargoes rose by one to 23 for the month, according to the loading program. Out of 23 cargoes, 12 were 650,000-barrel shipments, and eight were 700,000-barrel shipments. The remaining cargoes varied from 500,000 to 1.3 million barrels. Socar is set to load 70% of the cargoes in December, with the last 1.3 million-barrel cargo set to load over Dec. 30 to Jan. 1, the report showed. Mediterranean and Black Sea traders have expressed mixed views on the strength of Azeri Light differentials, amid contesting views on the availability of prompt cargoes.
