All rights reserved. 6 EC to propose 22nd Russia sanctions package before end-Nov: president  Von der Leyen says proposal due ahead of Council meeting  Previous package faced extended discussion before July approval  Sanctions require unanimous member state agreement The European Commission plans to propose its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia before a late-November meeting of the European Council, President Ursula von der Leyen said Nov. 13. “We will come forward as a Commission…with the 22nd sanction package before the next European Council,” von der Leyen told reporters Nov. 13 during an informal meeting of EU leaders in Dublin. Von der Leyen was referring to a special Council meeting scheduled for Nov. 26-27 in Brussels, an EC spokesperson told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy. The expected proposal comes some four months after member states agreed to the EU’s 21st sanctions package against Moscow in July. Among other measures, that package included a one-year freeze to the bloc’s oil price cap and a carve out allowing some continued transit of Russian LNG to third countries after an EU ban takes effect next year. Sanctions require unanimous approval from EU member states. The 21st package faced extended discussions before receiving the green light over the summer. The EU is set to ban all remaining imports of Russian LNG from Jan. 1, 2027, under a major law approved in early 2026. So far this year, the EU has brought in about 13.1 million metric tons of LNG from Russia, accounting for about 15.1% of the bloc’s overall imports, according to data from S&P Global Energy CERA. This is up from the same span last year, when Russian cargoes totalled 12.3 million mt, accounting for 13.4% of overall EU LNG imports, per CERA. Platts assessed the DES Northwest Europe LNG marker at $29.435/million British thermal unit on Nov. 12, up 6.7% day over day. — Matt Hoisch Trump extends Jones Act waiver to ease fuel transport amid conflicts  Trump extends waiver for 90 more days  Recent waiver covered 13 million barrels The Trump Administration has extended a Jones Act waiver for another 90 days, giving states additional flexibility to source products like gasoline and oil amid ongoing international conflicts, a White House official said Nov. 13. The waiver allows foreign-flagged vessels to transport refined products between US ports, bypassing the century-old maritime law that typically restricts such movements to US-built, US- flagged and US-crewed ships. The new waiver will begin Nov. 16, after the current 90-day waiver expires, the White House official said. Under the waiver that expires Nov. 15, a total of 13 million barrels of products were shipped, including 5 million barrels of gasoline, 4 million barrels of crude oil and 1 million barrels of fuel oil, the White House official said. “Since the waiver was first issued [in March], an additional 90 million barrels of products – primarily refined petroleum products – have been shipped between US ports,” the official said. “This represents a 40% increase in maritime domestic product volume shipped compared to the same period last year.” The West Coast has especially benefited, receiving 23 million barrels of additional products since the Jones Act was waived, the official said. This included 13 million barrels of gasoline and 4 million barrels of renewable fuels, the official said. “This collectively represents a 190% increase in maritime domestic product volume shipped compared to 2025 when, during the same period, 8 million barrels of products were shipped into the West Coast,” the White House official said. Houston has emerged as a dominant origin for westbound Jones Act waiver cargoes, according to US Energy Information Administration data. Tanker-and-barge shipments of crude oil and petroleum products from the US Gulf Coast to the US West Coast reached 4.43 million barrels in July, up from 1.26 million barrels in July 2025, rising roughly 252% on the year. — Kate Winston Argentina's Petróleos Sudamericanos aims to boost oil output 40% in three years  Midsize producer is targeting conventional fields  Vaca Muerta shale will follow in next growth phase  CEO says other plays could be new sources of growth Petróleos Sudamericanos, a midsize oil producer in Argentina, plans to step up production by 40% at its conventional fields over the next three years, helping to provide the cash flow for future shale projects, CEO Alfredo Bonatto said in an interview. This will take the company’s production to some 120,600 barrels/day from 86,000 b/d, he told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy. “We are gradually growing,” he said of the strategy. Petróleos Sudamericanos, now the country’s 12th-largest oil producer, is one of several smaller independent firms betting on conventional blocks for growth, as larger firms sell assets to focus on developing the giant Vaca Muerta shale play. The company plans to invest $230 million through 2031 as part of this growth strategy, which calls for drilling 20 new wells and doing workovers on 178 wells, according to a Nov. 12 presentation of its plans at Oil Day 2026 in Buenos Aires. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. reports.ftext: Volume 104 / Issue 219 / November 13, 2026 (continued on page 23) Market analysis International Crude World oil market set for Q4 surplus as Gulf supply rebounds: IEA  IEA cuts oil demand forecasts for 2026, 2027  China's consumption drops 1.3 mil b/d in Sept  Global production jumps 5.3 mil b/d since Aug The world oil market is set to flip into a fourth-quarter surplus as a faster-than-expected recovery in Middle East crude flows outpaces softer global demand, the International Energy Agency said Nov. 13, reversing an earlier warning of a year-end deficit. In its latest monthly oil market report, the Paris-based agency lowered its 2026 global oil demand projection by 90,000 barrels/ day from its October assessment to 102.3 million b/d, deepening the expected annual contraction to 2.7 million b/d compared with the 2.6 million b/d drop forecast a month earlier. Total consumption for 2027 was also revised down by 80,000 b/d month over month to 104.3 million b/d, with next year's projected 2 million b/d recovery leaving global oil use roughly 670,000 b/d below prewar 2025 levels. Combined with a 3.3 million b/d upward revision to fourth- quarter supply, the softer demand baseline is set to push global balances into an immediate overhang before a more substantial inventory build takes hold in 2027, the IEA said, signaling a reversal of last month's warning of a persistent year-end deficit. “The oil market is showing tentative signs of rebalancing, with global oil supplies surpassing demand for the first time since the outbreak of the war in Iran,” the IEA said in its latest report, titled “Straightening out.” Demand weakness China accounted for the bulk of the downward demand adjustments, with the agency cutting its 2026 and 2027 Chinese consumption estimates by 80,000 b/d each to 16.43 million b/d and 16.96 million b/d, respectively, the IEA said. Chinese oil demand contracted by 1.3 million b/d year over year in September, nearly double August's pace, as a six-year property slump and rapid electric vehicle adoption continued to erode road fuel consumption. Overall, the downgraded consumption outlook reflects ongoing disruptions to Middle Eastern exports of refined products and LPG, which remain at roughly half of prewar levels, alongside the lingering drag of elevated fuel prices, the IEA said. Platts North Sea Crude Daily Market Analysis  Buying interest emerges for December cargoes  November availabilities keep sentiment muted North Sea crude differentials rebounded slightly as some interest emerged for December-loading cargoes Nov. 13, although prompt November availabilities and the general uncertainty surrounding supply balances ahead kept sentiment widely muted. “It’s the year-end, the market has no direction, the war risk is on and off… it’s hard to trade,” a Europe-based North Sea crude trader said. “Margins are still okay but stocks are low, I think refineries are waiting to buy cheaper FOB — freight is wild.” The Platts Market on Close assessment process saw Glencore bidding for December-loading cargoes of Forties and Ekofisk, left outstanding at the London close at premiums as high as $1/ barrel over Dated Brent, having demonstrated value higher. However, prompt November-loading cargoes remained available, with Forties in particular seeking homes within a well- supplied Europe as arbitrage prospects for the grade remained unviable. “The arb freight is not cheap enough yet, and also the economics don’t work so it is hard to pull Forties to the East,” a second trader said — adding, however, that “reverse” arbitrage flows from Asia into Europe were unlikely for the December cycle. On the sour front, a well-supplied European sour crude complex continued to exert significant pressure across Norway’s Johan Sverdrup, with easing freight rates across the Atlantic Basin seeing more competing medium sour flows into Europe. “Johan Sverdrup values have been decimated because of [the Latin American crude] flow, and now they have found some sort of floor,” a third trader said. “It is a combination of lower freight allowing a lot of Latin American barrels to come to Europe at competitive prices, and also quite a lot of availabilities of Saudi barrels in December,” a fourth trader said. The recent collapse in differentials is expected to have opened arbitrage lanes into the Mediterranean for the Norwegian medium sour grade, although participants still saw flows into Asia as unlikely. A second WAF trader told Platts that the state of the market would be drastically different if it was not for the domestic refiner. “Dangote does a great job of scooping up Nigerian crude,” the second trader added. TotalEnergies then entered the day’s MOC with five bids for Nigerian crude grades Bonga, Egina, Erha and Forcados for loading dates across Dec. 15-31. China's apparent crude stocks likely rose by 15.31 million barrels in October, the largest stock build since the 54.11 million- barrel build in March, as crude imports hit a seven-month high of 9.92 million b/d, domestic production rose 2.3% year over year to 4.36 million b/d and refinery throughput declined, according to Platts' calculations based on NBS and General Administration of Customs data. Analysts and refiners attributed the increase to concentrated crude arrivals and the need to support refinery runs after commercial crude inventories had been drawn down to levels that could no longer provide additional supplies. Chinese refiners could consider restocking if crude prices fall toward $80/b, with more substantial purchases likely at about $70/b, a refining source with a state-run oil company said. For now, refiners are prioritizing processing existing high- cost barrels rather than adding expensive inventories, while using exports to help offset elevated feedstock costs, the source added. Any move by the White House could bring volatility to the oil market, while logistical uncertainties could also affect the pace of deliveries.” The company had to increase crude imports because its commercial crude stocks had been drawn down to levels that could no longer provide additional supplies, the crude procurement manager said. According to Ursa Space data, China's onshore crude inventory fell to 1.240 billion barrels as of Oct. 29 from 1.252 billion barrels as of Oct. 1. The reduction during the period was 12 million barrels, slower than the 55 million-barrel decline seen in September, according to the data. Throughput down The month-over-month throughput reduction was within expectations, as the combined crude throughput of 49 Chinese state-owned refineries was expected to fall to 8.15 million b/d in October, from 8.39 million b/d in September, Platts data showed. reports.ftext: www.spglobal.com/energy Platts Oilgram News Volume 104 / Issue 226 / November 17, 2026 Inside this issue INTERVIEW: ADNOC looks to deepen India footprint through crude, chemicals, oil storage  ADNOC supplied over 500,000 b/d of crude to India in 2025  ADNOC holds 40% share of India's LPG imports  ISPRL storage deal signals deeper energy security ties India's surging energy appetite and rapid industrial expansion are prompting Abu Dhabi National Oil Company to deepen its presence across the country's energy value chain, as the UAE producer seeks to evolve from a commodity supplier into a long- term integrated partner. In an exclusive interview with S&P Global Energy Platts, Nasser Omair Al Muhairi, acting CEO of Downstream Industry, Marketing & Trading at ADNOC, discussed the company’s strategy across crude oil, LPG, LNG, petrochemicals, storage and trading. He also addressed supply reliability amid the Strait of Hormuz risks, potential investments in Indian infrastructure and ADNOC's ambition to move beyond its traditional role as a crude and oil products supplier. How important is India to ADNOC's downstream growth strategy in Asia and which parts of the value chain offer the greatest opportunities? India is among ADNOC’s most important energy markets. In 2025, ADNOC supplied more than 500,000 barrels/day of crude to India, representing almost 10% of the country’s crude imports. Our energy partnership with India also extends into everyday life. Through ADNOC Global Trading, we account for about 40% of India's LPG imports and supplied over 600,000 metric tons in October alone, equivalent to the average monthly LPG consumption of about 86 million households. As India’s economy and industrial base continue to expand, we see  Minister announces 120,000 b/d initial flow  Rehabilitated pipeline boosts export capacity  Targets 500,000 b/d through pipeline Iraq’s Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair declared the resumption of pumping through the Iraqi federal section of the Iraq-Turkey pipeline at an initial rate of 120,000 barrels/day, the Iraq News Agency reported Nov. 17. He added that export capacity would gradually increase to 500,000 b/d. The section runs from the ITI-A station northwest of Baiji to Fishkhabur on the Turkish border, where it connects with pipelines running to the port of Ceyhan. The restart gives Baghdad an additional route for moving northern and southern crude to the Mediterranean, increasing flexibility at a time when Iraq has sought to reduce its reliance on Persian Gulf export routes disrupted by the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. The federal line had been largely out of service for years, leaving the Kurdistan Region’s pipeline, which runs parallel to the federally controlled pipeline, as the principal connection between northern Iraqi fields and the Turkish export system. The line has undergone extensive rehabilitation and testing since February, as Iraq has accelerated projects to diversify export routes. All rights reserved. 2 Asia Pacific AZEC forms 'Asia Oil Security Task Force;' works with IEA to bolster supply security  Japan proposes to work with ASEAN Regional Joint Stockpiling  To explore stockpiling in idle tanks in Japan for Asia  To establish IEA-Japan Oil Security Hub for Asia Leaders of the Asia Zero Emission Community agreed Nov. 17 on launching the “Asia Oil Security Task Force” initiative following a proposal from Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi at the AZEC leaders' meeting, Japanese government officials said, aiming to strengthen regional oil stockpiling and coordination on emergency responses. During the AZEC leaders' meeting, co-chaired by Japan and the Philippines in Manila, Takaichi also proposed the Japan-led Stockpiling Project to be coordinated with the ASEAN Regional Joint Stockpiling scheme. Under the proposal, potential cooperation to stockpile oil for Asian countries in idle tanks in Japan will be explored in coordination with initiatives such as the Philippines-led ASEAN Regional Joint Stockpiling scheme, the officials said. This cooperation could be pursued under the Partnership on Wide Energy and Resources Resilience Asia, or POWERR Asia, initiative, launched by Japan in April, using existing infrastructure, including facilities at closed refineries, the officials said. Under the proposed scheme, idle oil stockpiling infrastructure located in Japan would be refurbished, including the renovation of idle storage tanks and port berthing facilities, according to the officials. The costs associated with upgrading, maintaining and operating the infrastructure would be covered by stockpile usage fees paid by ASEAN countries, allowing those countries' oil reserves to be held using Japan's oil stockpiling infrastructure. However, ASEAN countries are envisaged as not owning the oil itself under the proposed scheme. Instead, they would pay a “stockpile usage fee” for the right to purchase oil on a priority basis in the event of an emergency, under a plan envisioned as a ticket-stockholding scheme, according to the officials. The Asia Oil Security Task Force will collaborate with the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia (ERIA) and the International Energy Agency, and will serve as a voluntary body to advance cooperation among AZEC partner countries under the AZEC Ministerial Work Program for Strengthening Oil Stockpiling, according to a joint statement by the AZEC leaders. The Asia Oil Security Task Force also supports, complements and aligns with existing regional energy cooperation mechanisms, particularly the ASEAN Framework Agreement on Petroleum Security (APSA), including through oil stockpiling for emergency preparedness, as appropriate, while avoiding duplication of efforts and respecting their respective mandates and institutional arrangements, according to the joint statement. The adoption of the AZEC Ministerial Work Program for Strengthening Oil Stockpiling at the fourth AZEC Ministerial Meeting in October by 11 AZEC partner countries — Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Cambodia, Indonesia, Japan, Lao PDR, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam — marked a step forward in developing petroleum stockpiles among ASEAN countries after years of little progress in establishing oil stockpile frameworks in the region. The joint statement comes as AZEC leaders recognized Asia's high exposure to disruptions to energy supply chains and key maritime routes, including the Strait of Hormuz, and noted the importance of joint efforts and cooperation among Asian countries, including through ASEAN-led mechanisms. “In this regard, we reaffirm our commitment to strengthen energy security and supply chain resilience, including by maintaining open and transparent energy markets and rules- based trade, recognizing the importance of international cooperation on strengthening oil stockpiling, and close coordination on energy between producing and consuming countries to build more resilient energy supply chains,” the joint statement said. Joint oil stockpiling In the Nov. 17 joint statement, AZEC leaders also welcomed the ERIA's contribution through its study on the potential for joint oil stockpiling in ASEAN. “We emphasize that initiatives on joint oil stockpiling should take into account the respective national circumstances, regulatory frameworks, infrastructure readiness, and national oil stockpiling policies of participating countries, while allowing flexibility in determining appropriate cooperation arrangements,” AZEC leaders said. The AZEC leaders' joint statement urged partner countries to strengthen their energy supply systems through appropriate policy measures, diversification of energy sources and suppliers, and constructive engagement and policy coordination. The leaders also encouraged enhanced bilateral and commercial cooperation with relevant international partners to diversify crude oil supply sources and strengthen supply arrangements, taking into account different national circumstances, market conditions, and energy security priorities, the joint statement said. These efforts should also include developing adequate oil storage infrastructure, strengthening supply chain connectivity, and improving information sharing and coordination to facilitate timely responses to potential oil supply disruptions and energy emergencies, the statement said. “We encourage AZEC partners to also pursue opportunities to structurally strengthen energy security and resilience, including through renewable energy, electrification and other measures that reduce exposure to potential future energy shocks,” the statement added. Japan-IEA initiative In a separate joint statement Nov. 17, Japan and the IEA welcomed the proposal to establish the “IEA-Japan Oil Security ©2026 S&P Global Inc. The Asian region has been particularly heavily impacted by the instability of the Strait of Hormuz, owing to its high dependence on oil and gas imported from the Gulf region, underscoring the need for concerted steps to improve oil security across the region, Japan and the IEA said in the joint statement. “The Hub will strengthen oil security across Southeast Asia and beyond, with an initial focus across three areas: (i) capacity- building support for the development of oil stockholding systems and infrastructure; (ii) enhanced analysis and information- sharing on oil markets and energy security; and (iii) examination of frameworks for emergency cooperation and coordinated responses by providing strategic and technical insights on the overall design of oil security systems, including the development and enhancement of oil stockpiling arrangements that reflect the circumstances and needs of Asian countries,” according to the joint statement. The Hub will feed into work undertaken by the Asia Oil Security Task Force, which was established at the AZEC leaders' meeting on Nov. 17 to materialize POWERR Asia in order to strengthen the resilience of Asia’s energy and resource supply through both emergency preparedness and longer-term structural measures, according to the joint statement. The Hub will be hosted by the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security in Tokyo and will draw on market analysis, policy recommendations and technical expertise from the IEA Secretariat’s headquarters in Paris and the IEA’s Regional Cooperation Centre in Singapore, the joint statement added. — Takeo Kumagai China refiners eye more fuel exports in Nov to offset higher crude costs  State refiners to largely use up fourth-batch quotas  Sinopec raises November crude runs by 9%  Gasoline exports rise; gasoil shipments restricted China's refiners are aiming to boost oil product exports toward the end of 2026 to help mitigate high crude feedstock costs, with state-owned refiners expected to largely utilize their fourth-batch export quotas as domestic supply pressures remain manageable, refinery sources said Nov. 16. A state-run refining group has increased its planned November crude throughput by about 9% to 18 million metric tons (4.4 million barrels/day), up from an earlier market estimate of 16.5 million mt (4.03 million b/d), a source close to the matter said. The higher throughput comes after Beijing allocated a larger- than-expected 5.65 million mt in fuel export quotas in the fourth batch in late October. Refiners said they have been eager to process the high-priced crude already procured for November rather than carry the barrels forward and risk further price volatility. By exporting more of the resulting products, they aim to recover part of the elevated feedstock costs. “If the crude has already been bought at a high price, the risks further down the line are difficult to predict,” an East China-based refinery source said. “Refiners would rather process it as early as possible and export the products if they can.” The incentive to export is stronger because China's regulated domestic gasoline and gasoil prices may not fully reflect sharp increases in international crude prices, thereby limiting refiners' ability to pass on higher feedstock costs to the domestic market, refiners said. Freight differentials between domestic and overseas markets also play a role in export economics. “Refiners need to balance securing domestic supply with exporting more products to recover some of the higher production costs caused by expensive crude,” a South China- based refinery source said. S&P Global Energy CERA analysts estimate that China would need to export at least 2 million b/d, or about 7.72 million mt, of clean oil products over November-December to fully use the quotas. China adjusts retail ceiling prices for gasoline and gasoil every 10 working days based on international crude price movements. Market sources said freight and insurance costs have been set at a combined $5/b in the pricing formula. Gasoline exports rise Some state refineries are already planning higher gasoline exports in November while continuing to hold back gasoil shipments, according to refinery sources. Two refineries with a second state-run refining group in Northeast China plan to increase gasoline exports in November, according to sources at the plants. One of the refineries, which has not exported gasoline in recent months, plans to resume shipments with one Medium Range tanker cargo in November. The other refinery plans to export three MR-sized gasoline cargoes, up from zero in October, while keeping jet fuel exports steady at about 140,000 mt. The scope for higher exports varies by product, with gasoline and jet fuel having more room for overseas sales as domestic gasoil supply remains relatively tight. The first state-run refining group currently allows gasoil exports only to UNV2 and UNV3, restricting shipments to other destinations to safeguard domestic supply. “There are no such restrictions on gasoline and jet fuel exports,” another South China-based refinery source said. The restrictions mean incremental exports could be skewed toward gasoline and jet fuel, allowing refiners to monetize higher output while prioritizing domestic gasoil supply. — Daisy Xu - Oil Market Specialist ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian refineries resumed in late October after a nearly two-week pause, with strikes affecting a host of refineries, including Novokuibyshev in the Samara hub, Norsi in Kstovo, Nizhny Novgorod region, Kirishi in the northwest and Volgograd in southern Russia as well as the Omsk refinery in Siberia. The renewed disruptions have brought back fuel rationing at filling stations and queues, both of which had largely disappeared in October. So far, however, it is too early to speak of a return to a full- fledged fuel crisis, Vladimir Poklad, director of Moscow-based consultancy Delovoy Profile, said in an email on Nov. 17. November demand is 5% below July's seasonal peak, while refinery throughput had recovered to around 5 million b/d by late October, well above the 3.3–3.5 million b/d needed to meet domestic demand, Poklad estimated. Most of the previously hit refineries resumed full or partial operations in October, Russia-based market sources have said. However, as strikes were scaled up, at least seven Russian regions had reintroduced fuel purchase restrictions at filling stations as of mid-November, according to regional authorities. The measures include daily caps of 30 liters per car in towns and 50 liters per car on motorways. Market sources said the fueling limits for the moment primarily affected regions where refineries have been struck. This is far below the summer peak of the crisis, when fuel purchase restrictions were in place in 88 of Russia's 89 regions, Poklad said. Moreover, the November restrictions have been concentrated mainly in regions with longer supply routes such as Zabaykalsky Krai, Krasnoyarsk Krai, and Arkhangelsk region. “These measures are aimed more at rerouting supplies and preventing panic buying than at addressing a nationwide fuel shortage,” Poklad said. Baranov also pointed to logistics as a separate source of vulnerability, warning that consistent attacks on fuel transport and distribution infrastructure in recent months could cause localized shortages even where refinery output remains sufficient. Despite the mounting pressure, analysts do not expect major market turbulence in the near term. “The baseline scenario is one of manageable supply pressures without major disruptions to fuel availability,” Poklad said. Seven-day moving averages for combined crude shipments from the Persian Gulf, Gulf of Oman, and Red Sea ports fell to 14.1 million b/d in the week ended Nov. 10, down from 17.3 million b/d a week earlier and a peak of 18.63 million b/d on Nov. 4. While the latest volumes mark a major recovery from the spring trough, when regional crude exports collapsed to as low as 5.77 million b/d on March 19 following the outbreak of US-Iran hostilities, they remain well short of pre-war norms. The recent fall came as direct shipments from Persian Gulf ports to international markets via the Strait of Hormuz reached 1.8 million b/d on Nov. 4-10, much lower from 4.9 million b/d in the prior week, according to CAS. The preliminary figures remain subject to revision as additional tanker movements and cargoes are identified. Combined crude and refined product shipments exiting via the Strait of Hormuz dropped to 10.6 million b/d in the week to Nov. 10, down from 13.9 million b/d the previous week. That leaves total oil flows through the strategic chokepoint at just 49% of the 21.53 million b/d pre-war average. The estimate combines crude and refined-product cargoes sailing directly out of the Persian Gulf through Hormuz with Gulf-origin cargoes transferred to export tankers in the Gulf of Oman. “Shipowners continue to demand a substantial premium for operating in the region,” said CAS analysts in a recent note. “Against this backdrop, preliminary November export data point to a softer start to the month.” Rerouting Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, assessed the time charter equivalent earnings for non-scrubber, non-eco VLCCs on the Ras Tanura-Ningbo route at $1,093,541 per day on Nov. 17, off the previous peak of $1,338,220/day Nov. 2 and its all-time high of $1,361,928/day Oct. 9. The International Maritime Organization has recorded 12 ship attacks so far in November, of which nine occurred during the first 10 days, as the US-Iran conflict dragged on while diplomatic talks failed to yield concrete results. Among the latest attacks, the Panama-flagged LPG tanker Tara Gas was struck in the strait on Nov. 16, the Indian government said in a statement, adding that 21 Indian seafarers were evacuated and one went missing. Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency also reported several maritime incidents involving liquefied gas and oil tankers on Nov. 17, including some allegedly hitting mines, citing various Iranian forces’ statements. Exporters have leaned heavily on ship-to-ship (STS) transfers in the Gulf of Oman to bypass the chokepoint, alongside Murban and Oman Blend loadings outside the strait and Red Sea diversions. Gulf of Oman STS crude loadings alone now account for roughly 6 million to 8 million barrels of the weekly average, a trade route that barely registered in early 2026. Latest loadings reached 7.1 million b/d in the week to Nov. 10, compared with 6.5 million b/d in the prior week, CAS data shows. He added that export capacity would gradually increase to 500,000 b/d. The section runs from the ITI-A station northwest of Baiji to Fishkhabur on the Turkish border, where it connects with pipelines running to the port of Ceyhan. The restart gives Baghdad an additional route for moving northern and southern crude to the Mediterranean, increasing flexibility at a time when Iraq has sought to reduce its reliance on Persian Gulf export routes disrupted by the ongoing crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, assessed January cash Dubai and cash Oman both at a premium of 6 cents/b to same- month Dubai futures at the market close, down 13 cents/b day over day. January cash Murban was down 10 cents/b over the same period at a premium of $3.10/b to same-month Dubai futures. During the MOC, 32 January Dubai partials of 25,000 barrels each traded. reports.ftext: www.spglobal.com/energy Platts Oilgram News Volume 104 / Issue 227 / November 18, 2026 Inside this issue Energy markets eye China-US-Russia summit, but expectations cautious  Iran key to Hormuz talks  Europe, Ukraine absent from discussions  US politics constrain Russia sanctions relief Energy markets are closely monitoring an upcoming summit between the leaders of China, the US and Russia for any potential impact on Middle East stability and energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, analysts and industry sources told Platts over Nov. 16-18. Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump are set to meet in Shenzhen on Nov. 19 for a trilateral summit. The Kremlin said at a press briefing with reporters Nov. 16, “The significance and symbolism of this meeting are hard to overestimate.” Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said Nov. 16 that stronger communication among China, Russia and the US, along with efforts to manage differences and stabilize relations, would serve the interests of all three countries and help stabilize the global situation and promote dialogue and cooperation. Trump told reporters in the US on Nov. 16 that he would discuss denuclearization, Iran, Ukraine, trade and the economy with Xi and Putin. Cautious expectations Asian analysts and industry sources expressed cautious expectations for the talks, noting the complexity of several geopolitical issues affecting energy markets.  US Midwest refining margins drop 23.5%  Tight distillate stocks support diesel cracks  ARA, Singapore inventories fall below norms Global refining margins fractured along regional lines in the week ended Nov. 13, with four of six major refining hubs posting weekly declines and only the US West Coast and Singapore bucking the trend, according to analysis from Platts on Nov. 18 The divergence was driven by localized supply disruptions, inventory draws and the relative strength of diesel economics against a backdrop of softening gasoline values. The split carries direct implications for crude trade flows and product arbitrage windows heading into the final weeks of the fourth quarter, with distillate tightness in the US providing a floor under diesel-oriented refinery configurations even as gasoline- heavy margins face mounting pressure from high run rates and building stocks. Gasoline pressures down margins The US Midwest recorded the steepest weekly decline, with its equal-weight average margin based on four representative crudes falling $8.56/b, or 23.5%, to $27.89/b from $36.45/b the prior week, according to the data from S&P Global Energy. Gasoline economics weakened as Midwest stocks rebuilt and Group 3 premium suboctane slipped below futures, while refineries ran at 94.9% of utilization for the week ended Nov. 13, according to EIA data REFINERY MARGIN TRACKER: Global refining margins split as US, Europe diverge from Asia (continued on page 15) (continued on page 14) South Korea eyes bigger African crude role as shipments set for record high........... 2 Idemitsu to receive Brazilian crude at Aichi as Japan's first intake since conflict. ...... 2 Sanctioned VLCCs could return to mainstream trades, complicating outlook: Heidmar CEO..................................................... 3 Bahrain’s Sitra refinery expects to run above 100% capacity by year-end............... 4 Neo Next+ agrees to buy EnQuest's UK oil, gas portfolio................................ 5 Nigeria's Heritage Energy targets 100,000 b/d oil output................................ 6 Norway's Equinor says hit by IT cyber-attack, production unaffected................... 6 ADNOC Gas aims to boost production to 17.7 Bcf/d in coming years: CEO............... 7 US commercial crude stocks hit 6-week high as SPR drawdowns accelerate........... 7 Argentina oil output heads toward 1M b/d; heavy crude imports may rise............... 8 Presidio acquires Permian Basin assets under a $360 million deal...................... 9 PDVSA reports fire in a wastewater pit at Petropiar oil facility.......................... 10 ©2026 S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 2 Asia Pacific South Korea eyes bigger African crude role as shipments set for record high  Seoul seeks closer African ties on trade, crude, resources  African crude intake more than doubles to 149,000 b/d  Equatorial Guinea's Alen, Alba fill DFC, LSC supply gap African crude suppliers are expected to remain key to South Korean refiners' feedstock diversification amid disruptions to tanker flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with shipments of ultra- light, light and medium sweet grades from Algeria, Nigeria and Equatorial Guinea poised to reach a record annual high in 2026. South Korea, Asia’s third-largest crude oil buyer, is seeking closer trade and investment ties with African countries to secure stable supplies of crude oil, natural gas and critical minerals as geopolitical uncertainty accelerates the restructuring of global resource supply chains, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources said in a statement Nov. 17. At the 2026 Korea-Africa Trade and Industry Cooperation Forum in Seoul on Nov. 17, government officials, African diplomats, business representatives and experts discussed Africa’s growing importance as a trade partner and a source of strategic energy and mineral resources, according to the trade ministry. “The talks focused on ensuring stable supplies of crude oil and other resources from Africa, while also expanding the continent’s energy and logistics infrastructure,” the trade ministry said. South Korean refiners have secured well over 90% of their monthly crude feedstock requirements so far this year, with supply diversification and increased reliance on non-Middle Eastern crude, including African grades, playing a major role, feedstock managers at three major refiners based in Ulsan, Seosan and Yeosu told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, during market discussions Nov. 17-18. Although South Korea has secured higher volumes of light and medium sour crude from the UAE and Oman so far this year, sourcing ultra-light grades such as deodorized field condensate (DFC) and low-sulfur condensate (LSC) from the Middle East has been challenging. Imports of Alen and Alba condensate from Equatorial Guinea have helped fill the gap, the Seosan and Ulsan- based refinery feedstock managers told Platts. South Korea’s crude and condensate imports from Africa are on course to reach a record annual high in 2026, after shipments in the first nine months more than doubled year over year to 149,000 b/d, the latest data from state-run Korea National Oil Corp. showed Oct. 27. Algeria was South Korea's biggest African crude supplier over January-September, supplying 17.02 million barrels, driven by purchases of light sweet Saharan Blend crude, while African suppliers accounted for 5.6% of South Korea’s total crude imports so far this year, up from 2.2% in 2025, according to KNOC data. Although sweet-sour crude arbitrage economics and freight rates largely determine Asian refiners’ appetite for African and Mediterranean grades in each trading cycle, diversification efforts have prompted refiners to closely monitor spot cargoes offered by African suppliers, the three refinery feedstock managers said. Platts assessed the front-month Cash Brent-Dubai spread at an average of minus 83 cents/b in the fourth quarter to date, compared with minus $1.73/b in the third quarter and plus $1.58/b in the second quarter. A negative Brent-Dubai spread makes various sweet crude grades produced in the North Sea, Africa and the Mediterranean that are linked to the European benchmark more economical for Asian refiners than Dubai-linked grades. Closer South Korea-Africa cooperation is also intended to promote bilateral trade and investment as protectionism, geopolitical tensions and the restructuring of global supply chains heighten concerns over energy and resource security, the trade ministry said. — Gawoon Philip Vahn Idemitsu to receive Brazilian crude at Aichi as Japan's first intake since conflict  Brazilian barrels to arrive after 40-day voyage  950,000 barrels of medium sweet crude to arrive: Idemitsu  Medium-sweet Tupi crude, several other Brazilian grades popular Idemitsu Kosan Co. Ltd., the second-largest Japanese refiner, is set to receive a tanker carrying Brazilian crude oil at the 163,000 barrels/day Aichi refinery in the Ise Bay as early as Nov. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 18, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 3 20, a senior official at the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry said Nov. 18, as Japan steps up its supply diversification efforts. The expected arrival of the Brazilian barrels marks the first arrival of Brazilian crude in Japan since the conflict in the Middle East, the official said at a press briefing, declining to elaborate on the grade and volume to be received. This would mark the first import of Brazilian crude oil by a company with a business presence in Japan since 2002, METI said in an emailed statement. The Brazilian crude cargo is being transported to Aichi, central Japan, after a 40-day voyage from the South American country, according to a METI briefing document. A spokesperson for Idemitsu Kosan told Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, that the refiner will receive 950,000 barrels of medium sweet Brazilian crude oil, marking its first purchase of Brazilian barrels as part of its efforts to diversify its procurement sources. The arrival of the Brazilian crude cargo marks the 16th country Japan has imported crude oil from outside the Strait of Hormuz since the outbreak of conflict in the Middle East, following an intake of Argentine crude oil in September, according to the METI briefing document. Japan took a rare 10,960 b/d of Argentine Medanito crude in September, according to METI data. Tupi crude Medium-sweet Tupi crude, along with several other Brazilian export grades, has been popular among refiners in China, Thailand, Indonesia and South Korea. It would not surprise the market to see Japanese refiners take Brazilian cargoes and establish a regular trade flow, as they have been making significant efforts to diversify their feedstock sources, a trading manager at a major Japanese integrated trading house based in Singapore told Platts. Among other Brazilian crude trading activity in Asia, Indonesia’s Pertamina purchased Tupi crude for October- November arrival through a tender. Trading activity for Brazilian crude cargoes scheduled for February arrival in Asia is expected to continue this week. Tupi was last heard traded at a premium of about $18/b to March ICE Brent, delivered ex-ship (DES) Shandong. Platts assessed Tupi crude at a premium of $7.22/b against Dated Brent on a DES Qingdao basis on Nov. 17, trending lower since reaching a record-high premium of $23.52/b Sept. 21. — Takeo Kumagai, Gawoon Philip Vahn and Leon Wong Sanctioned VLCCs could return to mainstream trades, complicating outlook: Heidmar CEO  Buyers seek US clearance for sanctioned ships  CEO notes uncertain 2027 oil demand outlook  VLCC rates drop from October's record highs Buyers are pursuing sanctioned tankers for potential return to mainstream trading through US approvals, complicating expectations that older shadow fleet vessels will exit the market, Heidmar Maritime Holdings CEO Pankaj Khanna said Nov. 17. The activity is concentrated in VLCCs and remains limited, as tanker operators weigh the outlook for vessel supply against uncertain oil demand and adjustments to trading routes, Khanna said at the Xinde Marine Forum in UNV2. “The shadow fleet is coming back into the mainstream fleet. Nobody expected that,” said Khanna. Khanna said prospective buyers were approaching owners of sanctioned vessels, including Chinese owners, to seek clearance from the US Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control to trade the ships. “This [the potential return of sanctioned vessels] is happening on the margin, mostly in the VLCC sector,” he said. The move challenged earlier expectations that shadow fleet vessels would eventually be pushed out of the market, he said. OFAC had listed an Oct. 28 statement of licensing policy on the purchases of blocked vessels on its website. Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, could not find the listing when checked Nov. 18. The US Treasury Department did not immediately respond to a request for clarification on the policy status Nov. 18. A Treasury official had said the department could consider authorizing purchases by legitimate buyers and removing vessel sanctions on a case-by-case basis to restore ships to commercial service. There are already precedents for vessel sales followed by delisting. In an Oct. 8 statement, Treasury said it had removed the Hakuna Matata and Pinocchio from its sanctions list following their sale to nonsanctioned/US-aligned operators, allowing them to reintegrate into legitimate maritime operations. Aging fleet, uncertain demand Nonetheless, Khanna expected the age of most of the shadow fleet to eventually drive vessels out. In a scenario involving a Russia-Ukraine peace agreement, Russian trade could shift back toward younger ships, encouraging smaller owners to scrap older tonnage that had already generated substantial returns, he said. Subdued oil demand and easing geopolitical risks could reduce voyage distances that have supported tanker earnings, just as new ships enter service, he noted. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 18, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 4 “So, I’m afraid for oil demand in 2027 and what that will be, whether it will be stable or will decline,” Khanna said. The International Energy Agency lowered its 2027 global oil demand projection to 104.3 million barrels/day, at a projected 2 million b/d year-over-year recovery but still roughly 670,000 b/d below prewar 2025 levels, according to its latest monthly oil market report released Nov. 13. VLCC freight rates have retreated from record highs. The Platts VLCC index, for non-scrubber-fitted and non-eco vessels, was assessed at $814,585/day Nov. 17, up $14,686/d from the day prior, but down from its all-time high of $1,181,046/day Oct. 9. It has been below the $1 million/day mark since Nov. 10. Delivery risks At the Capital Link UNV2 Maritime Forum earlier Nov. 17, Khanna said an easing of conflicts and reopening of trade routes could coincide with a substantial delivery wave. He viewed deliveries in 2028-29 as a greater concern than those in 2027. “I think the confluence of that [easing of conflicts] combined with the delivery of the order books is scary,” he said. There could also be support for tanker demand as cargo owners diversify supply sources rather than return to the previous dependence on the Middle East, while lower oil prices could encourage inventory rebuilding, Khanna told the Xinde panel. The balance among those factors, new deliveries and the retirement or return of older vessels left the outlook uncertain, he said. “The only thing we can prepare for is a scenario where markets will be super volatile.” — Mia Pei Europe, Middle East and Africa Bahrain’s Sitra refinery expects to run above 100% capacity by year-end  Refinery operations currently at 80%: Bapco CEO  GCC markets now taking 80% of refinery’s output  Insurance costs adding $56/b for product exports Bapco’s Sitra refinery in Bahrain is set to operate at over 100% capacity by the end of the year, CEO Mark Thomas said on stage at the Middle East Gas Conference Nov. 18. Currently operations are around 80%, he said, as Bapco continues to ramp operations back up after refinery attacks and months of disruptions that cut off the country’s only export route via the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain, wholly reliant on the Strait of Hormuz for access to markets beyond the region, exported 85% of its refined products beyond the strait in February, Thomas said. “Now 80% of our product is consumed within the [Gulf Cooperation Council],” Thomas said. “We’re selling diesel to Iraq. We’re selling fuel to Saudi Arabia. Our whole marketing complexion has changed in the last six months. It will change again in the coming months as well as the strait opens up.” In February, Bahrain exported 413,000 metric tons of gasoil and diesel, plummeting to 36,000 mt in March after the onset of the war, data from S&P Global Commodities at Sea show. By October, those volumes had rebounded to 170,000 mt. Jet fuel and kerosene exports stood at 87,000 mt in October, still below pre-war volumes, which in February stood at 279,000 mt, CAS data show. Bapco has for years been working to expand capacity at the Sitra refinery to 415,000 barrels per day (20.75 million mt/year), and Thomas said that 27 of the 32 new processing units “were up and running” just before war broke out. He declined to comment on how many processing units are currently running. There were six direct attacks on the refinery during the regional war that broke out at the end of February, with the refinery shutting down for “a very short period of time,” Thomas said. As operations have ramped up, many products have found new markets in nearby countries, but Thomas said that for naphtha and LPG there is limited demand within the GCC, so they must be exported. Naphtha is being exported via the Strait of Hormuz, but LPG is difficult to transport and Bapco has been working with regional neighbors “to find homes for LPG within the GCC over the last few months.” This has created a new pricing structure for products traded within the GCC nations with ports inside the Strait of Hormuz. “There’s a huge differential between the outer Gulf and the inter-Gulf pricing,” Thomas said. “And the reason for that is not necessarily supply and demand.” He said that for every boat that is chartered to sail through the Strait of Hormuz, insurance costs $17 million for 24 hours. This insurance cost would run around an extra $8.5/barrel for a VLCC carrying 2 million barrels of crude, while for a smaller vessel carrying 300,000 barrels of refined product, the additional insurance cost would be over $56/b, which does not include the underlying freight rate to charter the vessel for its voyage. Referencing checkpoints within the Strait of Hormuz, Thomas said that it takes roughly eight hours to sail between each, making the entire journey through the narrow waterway around 24 hours. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 18, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 5 “On a cargo of 2 million barrels of crude, [the cost is] significant,” he said. “On a cargo of 300,000 barrels of diesel, it’s outrageous.” The Clean Arab Gulf-Japan 55kt LR1 rate was assessed by Platts, part of S&P Global Energy, at $204.33/mt on Nov. 17, off from a high of $237.65/mt at the end of October. Right before the war broke out, that rate was just below $50/mt. Export volumes through the strait have recovered, though the return of volumes for products has been slower than that for crude. Volumes are expected to continue to recover next year, which will prompt more changes in product flows. “Today, there’s a balance within the Gulf for most products,” Thomas said. “But as everyone repairs the refineries and the volume of export product becomes greater and greater, you’ll see greater pressure to actually be able to export.” — Lauren Holtmeier Neo Next+ agrees to buy EnQuest's UK oil, gas portfolio  Company was formed by TotalEnergies, Neo Next  EnQuest ends 16-year tenure in North Sea  Set of assets produced 31,100 boe/d in 2025 Neo Next+ will acquire the North Sea assets of its smaller rival EnQuest, cementing its role as the basin’s largest oil and gas producer and ending EnQuest’s 16-year tenure in the North Sea, it said in a statement Nov. 18. The company — the product of a tie-up between Neo Next and TotalEnergies’ UK business that was completed in March — said the agreement will add a “high-quality portfolio” of North Sea assets centered on the operated Kraken and Magnus fields, as well as the Sullom Voe terminal. Neo Next was a partnership between Spain’s Repsol and Norwegian private equity firm HitecVision. The deal also includes interests in the Greater Kittiwake Area and the Golden Eagle project northeast of Aberdeen, Neo Next+ said. The portfolio produced 31,100 barrels/day of oil equivalent in 2025, Neo Next+ said. The deal is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to regulatory approvals, and will be funded from existing debt facilities, the company said. “This transaction is another important step in Neo Next+’s strategy of Resilience, Yield and Growth. The addition of EnQuest’s UK oil and gas business further strengthens our scale and resilience in the UK North Sea, while adding production, reserves and cash flow to our portfolio,” said John Knight, the company’s executive chair. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. Any unauthorized use of this copyrighted material constitutes infringement of our intellectual property and will subject you to possible legal action. Platts Oilgram News November 18, 2026 © 2026 by S&P Global Inc. All rights reserved. 6 In its statement, Neo Next+ said the deal cemented “our position as the leading operator and producer on the UK Continental Shelf.” The company is “positioned to grow both through further M&A and through opportunities within its existing portfolio,” it added. The company, whose other assets include Penguin, the Elgin/ Franklin complex and the key Culzean gas field, said earlier this year that the Neo Next-TotalEnergies UK merger would create a 250,000 boe/d oil and gas business. The deal marks EnQuest’s exit from the UK after 16 years and leaves it to focus on a roughly 70,000 boe/d Southeast Asian upstream business. It follows a wave of exits by international oil companies from the UK North Sea, with executives citing unfavorable regulation and taxes, including the Energy Profits Levy, as well as a ban on new exploration. Among the companies looking to offload its UKCS assets is British group BP. Meanwhile, UK crude production has fallen by about two- thirds since 2009 to some 600,000 b/d, according to official government figures. — Charlie Mitchell Nigeria's Heritage Energy targets 100,000 b/d oil output  Aiming to double production  Operates Oil Mining Lease 30 Nigerian indigenous producer Heritage Energy Operational Services Ltd. announced Nov. 18 plans to embark on a fresh drilling campaign in its Niger Delta onshore oil block OML 30, with a target of more than doubling output to 100,000 barrels/day by 2030. Heritage Energy Operational Services Ltd, an affiliate of Shoreline Natural Resources Ltd. (SNRL), operates the Oil Mining Lease (OML) 30 sold by international oil companies Shell, TotalEnergies and Eni in 2013, with current output estimated at 45,000 b/d of light sweet crude oil grade, according to company data. “Heritage Energy is targeting production of 100,000 b/d per day by 2030, underpinned by a focused strategy encompassing sustained capital investment, disciplined reservoir management, technological advancement and operational excellence,” Heritage said in a statement, quoting its CEO Ado Oseragbaje. “Achieving this ambition requires an integrated approach to asset development, combining strategic investment, effective reservoir management, operational excellence and a deeper understanding of our subsurface potential,” he added. OML 30 lies onshore within the Niger Delta, in one of the most proliﬁc oil and gas provinces in the world. The acreage covers 1,097 square kilometers and includes eight producing ﬁelds, according to company data. Oil from OML 30 is transported through the major Trans- Forcados pipeline in the Western division of the Niger Delta and is operated by Heritage Energy and exported at the Forcados oil terminal. Heritage is partnered in the block by state oil company Nigerian National Petroleum Co. Ltd., which holds a 55% working interest. — Rosemary Griffin, Newsdesk-Nigeria Norway's Equinor says hit by IT cyber-attack, production unaffected  Working to 'neutralize the attack and restore full integrity'  Company confirms operations remain normal  Europe faces energy infrastructure threats Norway's state-controlled Equinor said on Nov. 18 it had gained a clearer understanding of a cyberattack on its IT systems first detected late Nov. 17, confirming the incident was not a virus and posed no risk of spreading, and that production remained unaffected. The update came as the company, one of Europe's largest gas suppliers, said work was “ongoing to neutralize the attack and restore full integrity to affected systems,” though it said it was too early to determine how long that process would take. “Equinor continues this work in dialogue with national security authorities,” it added. “Production remains unaffected.” In its initial statement late Nov. 17, Equinor said it had detected an “ongoing cyberattack” against certain IT systems and had mobilized relevant resources to neutralize it. “There are no indications that data has been stolen. The attack has not affected Equinor's operations and production,” the company said in its earlier statement. Key gas supplier Norway is a major gas supplier to the European market, with countries such as the UK, Germany, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Poland key buyers of Norwegian gas. The threat of cyberattacks, as well as physical attacks on infrastructure, remains a concern for the European gas sector. In November last year at an EU-Norway energy conference in Brussels, the EU's energy commissioner Dan Jorgensen said infrastructure was a “growing target for sabotage”. “In the coming years, our cooperation on the security of supply and the security of our infrastructure will become even more critical,” he said. “In the face of threats, we must stand strong and work together.” Rising cyber threats The energy sector faces a growing cybersecurity threat, with operational technology systems at oil and gas facilities and utilities increasingly targeted by sophisticated attackers. A recent study by Honeywell Technologies found that while only 54% of oil and gas respondents had reported a significant incident in the past 12 months, just 52% said they could restore critical systems within 24 hours, the lowest expected recovery rate among the four sectors profiled. ©2026 S&P Global Inc. According to new figures from Turkey's General Directorate of Mineral and Petroleum Affairs (MAPEG), the country's total crude imports in September rose by 10.2% from August and by 14.4% year over year to 3.133 million metric tons. Shipments from Russia, which was Turkey's largest source of crude until recently, fell by 40.2% from August and by 69.8% year over year but were still 19% up from June, when Russian imports were the lowest in over a decade. September's inflows of Russian crude comprised 505,633 mt of Russian Export Blend, imported by both Turkey's refiners — Tupras and Socar's STAR. When both refiners import the same crude grade, MAPEG provides only a single combined figure. Russian Export Blend was the only Russian grade imported, compared to August, when STAR also imported REBCO, and September 2025, when STAR also imported REBCO and CPC, and Tupras also imported Siberian light. Russian crude accounted for just 16.1% of Turkey's crude imports in September, down from 29.7% in August, marginally up from 16.0% reported in June and sharply down from 61.2% reported in September 2025, the data showed. Turkey's September imports of Iraqi crude accounted for 22.2% of total imports, up from 16.4% reported in August and 7.7% in September 2025. By volume, imports from Iraq totaled 697,892 mt, up 49.9% from August and up 232.4% year over year. Of this, 59% was Basrah Medium while 41% was Basrah Heavy, the data showed. The sharp rise in Basrah volumes coincided with an easing in the disruption of traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. According to data from Turkey's state pipeline operator Botas, flow through the Iraq-Turkey Pipeline (ITP) in September averaged 261,800 b/d, up 72% from August and 1,040% from September 2025, when flow had newly restarted under a deal between the Iraqi central government, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and producers in Iraq's Kurdistan region. Separately, Iraq’s Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair said Nov. 17 that pumping had resumed through the Iraqi federal section of the Iraq-Türkiye pipeline at an initial rate of 120,000 b/d, and that flow would gradually increase to 500,000 b/d. This section of the line handles crudes from Iraq's Kirkuk region and volumes of trucked Basra crudes. A separate section handles crude from fields in the KRG region. Under an agreement between Turkey and Iraq signed Aug. 1, flow through the line is to be increased to 1 million b/d, ahead of a new broad-based energy agreement between the two countries, to be concluded by July 27, 2027. Improved maritime conditions in the Black Sea in September coincided with Turkey's imports of crude from Kazakhstan rising by 48.1% from August and 37.4% year over year to 370,066 mt, about 11.8% of total imports. All imports were CPC grade, imported by both Tupras and STAR. With uncertainty over Russian sanctions and the continuing possibility of disruption to shipping in both the Black Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, Turkey's two refiners continued to operate broad crude slates, importing 19 grades from 15 countries in September, up from 17 grades from 14 countries in August. Imports rose from Saudi Arabia, Libya, Norway, the US, Italy, Guyana and Angola, with Turkey also recording its first imports from Syria in over a decade, about 59,912 mt of RMELIAN imported by STAR. The two refiners imported 505,633 mt of Saudi Arab light, about 16.1% of total imports, up 70.5% from August. Ithaca’s 2026 turnarounds were concluded “ahead of schedule in 166 days versus 274 planned,” the company’s CEO Luciano Vasques said during a call with investors Nov. 18. Overall, Ithaca’s production in the first nine months of 2026 was around 125,000 boe/d, with an output mix comprising 52% liquids and 48% gas, the company said. Ithaca has updated its production guidance for the year from 120,000-130,000 boe/d to 123,000-127,000 boe/d. Rosebank expectations Ithaca’s executive chairman Yaniv Friedman noted “material progress” at Rosebank ahead of the field’s first production expected in the period between January and June of 2027. The regulatory approval is expected by the end of 2026, the company said. Rosebank, operated by the Equinor-Shell joint venture Adura, is awaiting final approval from Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh. The debate over whether to grant final go-ahead is fracturing the ruling Labour Party, according to media reports. Dozens of MPs are expected to soon present a letter opposing Rosebank’s approval to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Despite the regulatory uncertainty, the project is on track to start up soon, Ithaca’s executives said during the call with investors. Ithaca holds a 20% non-operated interest in the field. “We are basically looking at the very last parts of the mechanical completion to be achieved, and then, in parallel, the handover of systems to go to commission for the startup and the operation readiness,” Ithaca’s CEO said. “At this moment, we are relatively comfortable that the project being forwarded according to the highest standards,” Vasques added. Rosebank production is expected to peak in 2028, according to Ithaca’s CEO. Petronas also adjusted the price differentials for its secondary crude grades relative to its main crude basket. The Miri Light differential to the MCO OSP was set at a discount of $3.65/b for December-loading cargoes, compared with a discount of $4.04/b for November, according to the notice. The company began publishing the price differential for Miri Light crude against the MCO OSP for cargoes loading from October 2025 onward, with the grade remaining in the basket that forms the MCO OSP. The MCO OSP basket comprises the flagship grades, including Labuan, Miri Light, Kikeh and Kimanis crudes. The Tapis differential to the MCO OSP was set at a discount of $8.46/b for December-loading cargoes, compared with a discount of $7.96/b for November, according to the notice. The Dulang and Cendor grades were set at premiums of $2.66/b and $2.95/b, respectively, to the MCO OSP for December- loading cargoes, compared with premiums of $2.74/b and $2.98/b to the MCO OSP for November. The Malaysian crude oil OSP differential takes into account a number of factors, such as the average premium or discount to Platts Dated Brent crude assessments in physical spot sales of Labuan, Miri Light, Kikeh and Kimanis grades loading during the month. Petronas also considers assessments of those grades by price information providers over a specific period, as well as buyers' views on trades and their recommendations on the value of the grades. reports.stext: Vortexa 亚洲市场焦点 2026-11-23 · 中文总结 CRUDE · PRODUCTS · FREIGHT｜原油 / 成品油 / 运费 中国主导 TMX 增量流向，运费走低支撑需求 China dominates incremental TMX flows; lower freight to underpin demand 报告： Vortexa · Asia Market Spotlight ｜发布日期： 2026-11-23 ｜编制： Wanying Zhang （Freight Analyst，Vortexa 分析团队指导） 数据快照：11 月数据分别截取 1–15 / 1–18 / 1–20 日（分页不同）；运费与存量数据最后观察点为 11 月 18–20 日 本页为第三方报告的中文研究摘要，观点与数据版权归 Vortexa 所有；仅供研究参考，不构成投资建议。 目录 Contents 核心观点 Key Takeaway TMX 增量流向中国：地炼入场，运费回落支撑采购 日本：多元化退潮，中东原油回归，出口蓄势过冬 埃及（Highlight）：“气转油”发电推升燃料油进口 中间馏分油：亚洲与 MEG 出口走高，输欧流量重经曼德海峡（BEM） 亚洲炼厂提石脑油收率、让渡汽油，填补海湾缺口 西非→中国：Suezmax 强势拉大 VLCC–Suezmax 价差 新加坡燃料油浮仓：周环比 -26% 报告附注与免责声明 Key Takeaway · 核心观点 原油：区域需求变化重塑贸易流向；成品油：流向与收率随利润、运费调整 原油市场 On crude —— 区域需求变化正在重塑贸易流向： 中国承接 TMX 增量产量的绝大部分 ：地炼（Teapots）批量入场，运费回落有望延续采购动能； 日本原油来源多元化退潮 ：中东原油回归，成品油出口为“强劲冬季”做好准备； 埃及“气转燃料油”发电 ：LNG 成本上行，推升燃料油进口需求（原文 Highlight）。 成品油 On products —— 出口流向与炼厂收率随利润与运费调整： 中间馏分油出口上升 ：亚洲与中东湾（MEG）货源流向广义阿拉伯海与欧洲，输欧流量大多重经曼德海峡（BEM）； 石脑油收率提升、汽油让位 ：重整利润收窄 + 海湾供应缺口延续； Suezmax 航次强劲 ：拉大西非（Waf）→中国 VLCC–Suezmax 运费价差。 Section 01 · Crude Flows TMX 增量流向中国：地炼入场，运费回落支撑采购 China captures most of TMX's incremental production as teapots step in, with easing freight likely to sustain demand momentum 出口总量 ：Trans Mountain 海上终端（TMX）自 2024 年 5 月放量以来，月度出口基本运行在 300–500 kb/d 区间；2026 年 9 月创出约 575 kb/d 的峰值，11 月（1–18 日快照）仍处约 550 kb/d 附近的高位。 目的地结构 ：中国是最大接收国，美国、韩国次之，新加坡/印度/日本/马来西亚/文莱零星参与。 中国接收方 ：中石化（Sinopec）与中石油（PetroChina）构成基本盘，ZPC、CNOOC/SinoChem 参与； 2026 年 10 月起地炼（Teapots）批量入场 ——10 月总量冲至约 400 kb/d 以上，11 月（1–18 日）地炼份额仍显著。 运费小窗 ：温哥华→日照 Aframax 运价自 2026 年 10 月下旬约 33 $/b 的峰值快速回落至 11 月中的约 4–5 $/b ，回到年内低位。 结论： TMX 增量持续释放 + 西海岸–中国小船运费大幅回落，双重利好下中国（尤其地炼）的 TMX 采购动能有望延续。 Fig 1 · TMX 出口目的地构成（左）｜中国 TMX 进口接收方结构 + 温哥华–日照 Aframax 运费（右） | Trans Mountain Marine Terminal crude exports by destination country (bd)；China's TMX crude imports by receiver (kbd) and Vancouver-Rizhao Aframax freight ($/b, side window) — Source: Vortexa（Nov-26 数据为 1–18 日；Nov-25 小窗数据为 1–30 日） Section 02 · Japan 日本：多元化退潮，中东原油回归，成品油出口蓄势过冬 Japan's diversification fades as Middle East crude returns; product exports set for a strong winter 原油进口 ：月均 ~2.2–2.4 mb/d。2025 年起日本一度压降中东依赖、转向北美等来源（多元化），中东占比从年初 ~90%+ 一路回落， 2026 年 5–9 月一度跌至 ~60% 上下 ；随后中东货源（含经埃及 Sidi Kerir 中转的沙特原油）回归， 10–11 月占比回升至 ~78–80% ，总进口修复至 ~2.3 mb/d（2026 年 6 月曾异常低至 ~0.65 mb/d）。 成品油出口 ：运输燃料（汽柴油 + 航煤）冬季旺季特征显著——上一轮冬季（2025-10 → 2026-01）从 ~220 kb/d 升至 ~330 kb/d 峰值；2026 年 4–6 月淡季低谷仅 ~65–95 kb/d；7 月起持续回升，10 月 ~250 kb/d， 11 月（1–15 日）~285 kb/d，已逼近上一轮冬季高点（图中虚线 ~290 kb/d） 。 结论： 中东原油回归 + 出口持续抬升，日本成品油出口大概率迎来一个“强劲冬季”。 Fig 2 · 日本原油进口来源结构与中东占比（左）｜运输燃料出口分品种（右） | Japan crude/condensate imports by origin region (mbd, LHS) and share of imports from Middle East (%, RHS)；Japan transport fuel exports by product (bd) — Source: Vortexa（Nov-26 数据为 1–15 日；中东口径含经 Sidi Kerir 中转的沙特原油） Section 03 · Egypt 原文 Highlight 埃及：LNG 成本高企，“气转油”发电推升燃料油进口 Gas-to-fuel oil switching for power generation drives fuel oil import demand in Egypt amid rising LNG costs (Highlight) LNG 侧（成本推手） ：埃及 LNG 进口（28 日均线）2026 年夏季冲至 ~21 mtpa 的历史同期极高水位，随后快速回落，11 月中已降至 ~8 mtpa——但仍约为 2016–25 同期均值（~2–4 mtpa）的两倍，气电经济性持续承压。 燃料油侧（切换结果） ：重质成品油进口 2026 年 9 月因夏季用电高峰冲至 ~220 kb/d 峰值，9 月底–10 月中回落后自 10 月下旬再度快速拉升， 11 月 18 日升至 ~140 kb/d ，远高于 2016–25 同期均值（~50–60 kb/d），并逼近 2025 年同期水平。 结论： “高 LNG 价格 → 电力部门气转燃料油 → 燃料油进口放量”的传导仍在进行时；只要冬季 LNG 价格维持强势，埃及燃料油进口需求有望维持高位。 Fig 3 · 埃及重质成品油进口（左）与 LNG 进口（右），均为 28 日均线 | Egypt dirty product imports (bd, 28-day moving average)；Egypt LNG imports (mtpa, 28-day moving average) — Source: Vortexa（最后数据点：11 月 18 日） Section 04 · Middle Distillate 中间馏分油：亚洲与 MEG 出口走高，输欧流量重经曼德海峡（BEM） Rising middle distillate exports from Asia and MEG head to Wider Arabian Sea and Europe, most flows to Europe transit via BEM 总量与流向（左图） ：亚洲 + 中东湾中间馏分油出口中，广义东南亚+东北亚（WSEA+WNEA）仍为最大流向（~2.2–2.6 mb/d 高位波动）； 广义阿拉伯海（WArS）自 2026 年 7 月起明显抬升 ，10 月 ~1.4 mb/d；西北欧+地中海（WNWE+WMed）在 2026 年 1–6 月一度塌陷至近零， 7 月起快速修复至 ~0.75–1.0 mb/d （图中红圈）；北美东海岸+南大西洋 ~0.2–0.35 mb/d；美洲西海岸量级很小。 输欧路径（右图） ：2023 年底红海危机后，亚洲/MEG→欧洲中间馏分油几乎全部绕行好望角（COGH 线 2024–25 年初高达 ~1.0–1.4 mb/d，BEM 柱归零）；2025 年下半年起 BEM（曼德海峡）流量恢复， 2026 年 7–11 月回升至 ~0.6–0.75 mb/d，COGH 同期萎缩至 ~0.1–0.15 mb/d ——输欧流量重新以 BEM（苏伊士方向）为主。 结论： 出口总量上升 + 欧洲流向修复 + 红海通行常态化，三者叠加令亚欧中间馏分油运输需求（吨海里）同步受益。 Fig 4 · 亚洲与中东湾中间馏分油出口按目的地区域（左）｜输欧经 BEM（柱）与 COGH（线）流量（右） | Asia and Middle East Gulf middle distillate exports by destination – wider shipping region (mbd)；Asia and MEG middle distillate transits to Wider Europe via BEM (bars) and via COGH (line) by waypoint entry date (mbd) — Source: Vortexa（Nov-26 数据为 1–15 日） Section 05 · Naphtha / Gasoline 亚洲炼厂提石脑油收率、让渡汽油，填补海湾供应缺口 Asian refiners boost naphtha yields at the cost of gasoline as reformer margins narrow and Gulf supply shortfall persists 海湾缺口（右图） ：中东（除伊朗）对东北亚石脑油出口 2025-06 → 2026-02 维持 ~0.9–1.1 mb/d 高位； 2026 年 3 月起断崖式下跌至 ~0.2 mb/d 以下 ，随后逐月修复——9 月 ~0.62 mb/d、10 月 ~0.49 mb/d， 仍较 2 月水平低约 515 kb/d （原图标注 “-515kbd vs Feb 26”）；11 月（1–18 日）~0.39 mb/d。 全球同比（左图） ：全球对东北亚石脑油出口同比变化在 2026 年 3–11 月持续为负，4 月与 8 月两度探至约 -1.0 ~ -1.1 mb/d 深度；中东是最大拖累项，俄罗斯阶段性减量，亚洲自身的小幅增量对冲有限。 炼厂行为 ：重整（reformer）利润收窄令汽油经济性下降，叠加海湾石脑油缺口延续——亚洲炼厂选择 提高石脑油收率、压低汽油收率 ，以增产对冲缺口。 结论： “海湾缺口 + 亚洲高收率”格局短期难解，东北亚石脑油进口依赖维持高位，利好石脑油计价与跨区套利流量。 Fig 5 · 全球对东北亚石脑油出口同比变化（左）｜中东（除伊朗）对东北亚石脑油出口（右） | Year-on-Year change in global naphtha export to Northeast Asia (bpd)；Naphtha exports from Middle East (excluding Iran) to Northeast Asia (bpd) — Source: Vortexa（Nov-26 数据为 1–18 日） Section 06 · Freight 西非→中国：Suezmax 强势拉大 VLCC–Suezmax 运费价差 Strong Suezmax voyages drive VLCC-Suezmax freight spread from Waf to China 航次量（左图） ：西非→中国原油/凝析油海运 ~0.45–0.78 航次/日（2025 年），2026 年 5–9 月回落至 ~0.3–0.45 的年内低位； 10 月强劲反弹至 ~0.81 航次/日 ，其中 Suezmax/LR3 ~0.55、占比罕见超过 VLCC；11 月（1–20 日）~0.65，Suezmax 仍占约 1/3。 运价（右图） ：VLCC 与 Suezmax（西非→中国）运价 8 月起同步飙升， 10 月 7 日前后见顶（Suezmax ~45 $/b、VLCC ~32 $/b） ；随后回落，11 月 20 日 VLCC ~13 $/b、Suezmax ~15 $/b。模型预测（虚线 + 阴影带）：12 月中 VLCC 降至 ~7–9 $/b、Suezmax ~10–11 $/b。 价差逻辑 ：Suezmax 航次需求异常强劲使 VLCC–Suezmax 价差走阔至峰值 ~13 $/b；随着运价整体回落，VLCC 相对经济性将重新显现。 结论： 短期 Suezmax 强势支撑价差；中期运价中枢回落，有利于压低中国进口西非原油的到岸成本，与 Section 01 的 TMX 采购逻辑互为印证。 Fig 6 · 西非→中国出口航次按船型（左）｜VLCC 与 Suezmax 运费及预测（右） | West Africa seaborne crude/condensate exports to China by vessel class (voyage count per day)；West Africa to China freight on VLCC and Suezmax with forecast ($/barrel) — Source: Vortexa（左图 Nov-26 为 1–20 日；右图最后数据点 11 月 20 日） Section 07 · Floating Storage 新加坡燃料油浮仓：周环比 -26% Singapore fuel oil floating storage highlights 周度要点 ：新加坡燃料油浮仓库存环比 -26.0% ——LSFO 降至 373 kt ；混合燃料油（Fuel oil mix）-15.0% 至 316 kt ；HSFO +2.0% 至 464 kt 。 水平 ：浮仓总库存（不含 Linggi）自 2026 年 1 月 ~3.5 mt 高位持续回落至 ~1.2 mt 附近，接近 2024 年中的低位区间；浮仓容量维持在 ~5.7–6.3 mt（图中红线）。 明细变化 ：18 艘浮仓船合计容量 5,738 kt、在册填充 1,150 kt（填充率 20.0%），环比 -405 kt 。增库集中在 HARMONY STAR（+168 kt，填充 74%）、CS DEVELOPMENT（+132 kt）、AQUARIUS STAR（+88 kt，新进入）；减库以 GRACE STAR（-247 kt）、CS BRILLIANCE（-189 kt）、OCEAN STAR（-156 kt，清空）、CS PROSPERITY（-135 kt）、SA CAPRICORN（-125 kt）为主。 Fig 头版：中石油多元化原油供应与中东变局 PetroChina Diversifies Crude Supply, Shipping amid Middle East Disruptions 中石油国际事业公司（PetroChina International）总经理罗亦周 11 月 8 日在上海举行的第十五届中国国际油气贸易大会上表示，面对收紧供应、推高运费的中东动荡，公司通过 多元化油源、自有运力与全球贸易网络 维持了石油流。该公司国际贸易板块占 2026 年 1-9 月中国原油进口的 18.1% ，其应对对中国这一全球最大进口市场意义重大。 动荡量级 ：年内中东紧张局势一度扰乱超过 1200 万桶/日 原油流量，引发湾区内逾 1600 万桶/日 石油减产（其引用的数据）；部分航线运费一度暴涨 十倍 。区域内船对船过驳（STS）占用运力，导致全球其他航线运价同步走高。 中国采购结构重塑 ：1-9 月中国自中东原油进口份额同比降 12.5% ，俄罗斯、南美份额分别升 6% 、 5.2% （海关数据）。俄油与南美原油部分填补中东缺口。 运力与网络 ：中东冲突爆发后，公司启动应急机制，指示湾内满载油轮加速通过霍尔木兹，订船窗口从正常的 2-3 周缩至 3-5 天 ；自有船队连续四年年处理量超 1 亿吨 、运营逾 300 条航线；货源覆盖 30 多个国家、100 多个油种。贸易量过去五年年均超 5 亿吨，年贸易额超 2800 亿美元 ，业务覆盖 120 多个国家和地区。 配套背景：中美延长贸易休战至 2027 年 1 月 10 日，中国将 24 个百分点加征关税暂停期延长两个月，但美国原油仍适用合计 20% 加征关税（LNG 为 25%）——美国原油流入中国依旧受限。 高运费抬升到岸原料成本、地缘扰动放大油源不确定性， 在供应源与运输路线之间灵活切换的能力已成为中国炼厂的核心竞争力 （原文观点）。 图 1 · 基准现货油价一个月走势：Dated Brent 与 Platts AGS 自 10 月高位同步回落至 $90 一线 | Benchmark Platts spot crude prices — Source: S&P Global Energy（Oilgram News 头版 p1） SECTION 02
