reports.ftext: For precious metals, 2027 increasingly looks like 2022: a rising Fed policy n rate weighs on private investor demand, but structural central bank buying keeps a firm bid under gold. We therefore see near-term downside risk and elevated volatility as the Fed continues to hike, but still see gold prices grinding higher to $4,650/toz by end-2027 on continued central bank purchases. Once the Fed starts cutting, we expect Western ETF demand to recover, supporting a stronger gold rally to $5,600/toz by end-2028, with significant upside risk to our base case if macro-policy hedge demand were to return. The same 2022 setup should favor gold over silver. Fed hikes weigh on private n investment demand for both metals, but only gold benefits from the structural central bank bid. We therefore expect gold to outglitter silver in 2027, barring another silver liquidity squeeze, which we think is difficult to sustain during a Fed hiking cycle when silver ETF demand is under pressure. For platinum and palladium, persistent US tariff uncertainty should keep n supply fragmented and volatility elevated, but does not necessarily imply higher prices in 2027. Fed hikes should weigh on investment demand — particularly for platinum which has a larger investment component than palladium, while rising EV penetration remains a structural auto-demand headwind. Platinum faces greater pressure from Europe’s more diesel-heavy fleet transitioning toward EVs, while palladium autocatalyst demand should decline more gradually as hybrids gain share and the EV transition proceeds more slowly in the more gasoline-heavy US market. In this 2027 Outlook, we use a Q&A format to discuss our precious metals n views, the key risks and the implications for investors: We cover the upside and downside risks to our gold forecasts, why gold did not hedge the 2026 Hormuz supply shock, how the opportunity differs by investor horizon, why we expect central bank buying to remain structural, the risks around China central bank buying and potential official-sector selling. We then turn to why we expect gold to outperform silver through the Fed hiking cycle, and why continued supply fragmentation should keep platinum and palladium prices volatile without Lina Thomas +44(20)7051-3062 | lina.thomas@gs.com Goldman Sachs International Daan Struyven +1(212)357-4172 | daan.struyven@gs.com Goldman Sachs & Co. The authors would like to thank Samuel Jönsson — an intern on our commodities research team — for his extensive contributions to this report. 16 November 2026 2 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst 2027 Outlook: It Is 2022 Again Gold: Structural Central Bank Support Through a Cyclical Rate Headwind Please see our Gold Market Primer for our framework and how we think about the gold market. Q1. What is your gold price forecast for 2027 and beyond? We remain constructive on gold longer term on structurally strong central bank buying, including from China’s central bank, but see a more challenging near-term setup given the hawkish Fed outlook. Our economists expect a third 25bp Fed hike in March 2027 following a second hike expected in December 2026, weighing on rate-sensitive Western ETF demand. We nevertheless expect continued central bank buying to lift gold prices to $4,650 by end-2027, up 19% from spot and up 13% from the October average (Exhibit 1, Exhibit 2). The Fed’s recent hawkish shift and a rising federal funds rate should also keep investor “debasement concerns” contained. We therefore assume macro-policy hedge demand for gold – reflected in call-option demand – declines toward its historical average (Exhibit 3). We expect private investor demand (via rate-sensitive Western ETF demand)1 to eventually recover as four 25p Fed cuts between November 2027 and September 2028 reduce the funds rate to its terminal rate of 3.25-3.5%, removing the rate constraint on gold prices and supporting a rise to $5,600/toz by end-2028 (Exhibit 1). 1 The boost to ETF holdings from Fed policy rate cuts tends to be gradual and not anticipatory, with flows only turning once rates are actually lowered. One 25bp cut results in ~60 tonnes ETF demand spread out over 6 months. Exhibit 1: We Forecast Gold at $4,650/toz by End-2027 and $5,600/toz by End-2028 Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 3 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst We think that the 2027 setup resembles 2022 (Exhibit 4): central banks provide a strong structural bid, but a higher federal funds rate weigh on investor positioning, driving a more modest pace of gold price increases on net. Exhibit 2: We Retain Our Longer-Term Constructive View on Structurally Strong Central Bank Demand – Which Drives Most of the Price Upside We Forecast by End-2027 We start from the October average of $4,100/toz, and view the more recent price weakness as largely driven by speculative positioning and therefore likely to prove temporary. Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research Exhibit 3: We Expect Macro-Policy Hedge Demand for Gold — Reflected in Call-Option Demand and Likely a Key Amplifier of the 2025/Early-2026 Rally, to Decline Further Toward Historical Levels Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 4 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Q2. What are the risks to your gold forecast? We see further near-term downside risk from a more hawkish Fed. In a scenario with four hikes and a higher terminal rate (Exhibit 6), we estimate gold at $4585/toz by end-2027 (red dashed line in Exhibit 5). A larger ETF unwind could push prices lower still. Gold ETF holdings have risen substantially over the past three years, reflecting lower rates, a normal upward trend as investor wealth grows (which our rates-implied autoregressive ETF model captures), and potentially a boost from the recent debasement trade. We expect two additional Fed rate hikes to unwind the latter, but cannot cleanly separate it from the structural wealth trend. As a conservative lower bound, we therefore assume all ETF holdings above the level implied by rates alone to unwind, implying another 300 tonnes of selling and gold at $4265/toz by end-2027 (grey dashed line in Exhibit 5, Exhibit 7). Exhibit 4: The Current Setup Resembles 2022: Central Banks Provide a Strong Structural Bid, But Higher Rates Weigh on Investor Positioning. Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 5 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Exhibit 5: A Higher Terminal Rate and ETF Sell Off Leaves Downside Risk to Our Base Case of $4,650/toz by End-2027 Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research Exhibit 6: Our US Economists Expect One Hike in December 2026 and Another One in March 2027, With Further Downside Risk to Our Gold Price Forecast From an Additonal Hike and Higher Terminal Rate Market pricing as of November 15 Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 6 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst There is also tactical downside risk around our fair-value forecast. Our forecasts capture the slower-moving drivers of gold prices, namely Western ETF and central bank demand, but speculative positioning can push prices temporarily away from that fair value. Speculative positioning on COMEX is already low at the 45th percentile, and we expect it to recover in our base case. That said, higher oil prices could trigger further systematic CTA selling, while sharp equity drawdowns (for instance related to uncertainty about the AI cycle) could initially pull gold lower as margin calls and broader deleveraging force investors to raise cash (Exhibit 8). Longer term, we see significant upside beyond our base case if macro-policy hedge Exhibit 7: A More Hawkish Fed Could — In an Extreme Scenario — Drive a 300-Tonne ETF Gold Unwind Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research Exhibit 8: On an Intra-Day Basis, Higher Oil Prices Weigh on Gold Through Systematic Selling, While Sharp Equity Drawdowns Initially Weigh Through Deleveraging Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 7 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst demand returns once the Fed starts cutting. Perceived fiscal sustainability concerns across Western economies, potentially reinforced by higher military spending and rising debt burdens in energy-importing countries, might revive that macro-policy hedge demand if investors were also to become concerned about how DM central banks would respond. Once falling rates remove the cap on the gold rally, a potential revival of fiscal sustainability concerns could drive substantial upside beyond our base case of $5600/toz by end-2028. Q3. Gold did not rally during the 2026 Hormuz shock despite higher inflation. Has gold’s role as an inflation hedge or safe haven changed? No, in our view. We have long argued that gold is not a universal stagflation hedge because the source of inflation matters. There are two distinct stagflationary regimes in which equity-bond portfolios tend to perform poorly, and gold behaves differently across them. The first regime is one of growing market concerns about institutional credibility. When markets doubt the central bank’s willingness or ability to contain inflation, inflation may run high, and both bonds and equities sell off. The 1970s are the classic case: US fiscal expansion and Fed subordination let inflation run out of control, and gold surged as investors sought value outside the system. The second is when supply disruptions drive both weaker growth and higher prices, as in 2022 when Russia, then supplying ~40% of Europe’s gas, cut flows, and commodities — as the disrupted input —were among the few assets with positive real returns. Like in 2022, gold typically underperforms initially in supply disruption episodes. Supply‑driven inflation raises the risk of tighter monetary policy, higher yields increase the opportunity cost of holding gold and weigh on ETF demand, and potential equity market drawdowns trigger margin‑related liquidations. The 2026 Hormuz shock fits this second regime, as the inflation shock came from disrupted commodity supply. Q4. What do you recommend investors? For CTAs and macro hedge funds, the next 3-6 months may remain challenging: our n base case of a rising funds rate, highly uncertain energy prices, volatility around inflation and labor-market data, and tight drawdown limits make it difficult to maintain long positions. Potentially higher oil prices could add to that pressure through systematic selling, while sharp equity drawdowns could initially pull gold lower as margin calls and broader deleveraging force investors to raise cash. For longer-horizon investors seeking exposure to rising central bank demand and/or n protection against macro policy tail risks (i.e. gold as a “debasement” hedge), however, the current correction in gold prices may offer a more attractive entry point. Structural central bank demand remains supportive, while private wealth and other long-term investors may value gold as insurance against DM fiscal sustainability risks2, even though their materialization is not our base case. Q5. Central bank demand is a key pillar of your gold outlook. Why do you view this 2 Particularly if investors were also to become concerned about how DM central banks would respond. 16 November 2026 8 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst demand as structural and expect buying to continue? Our view of structurally strong central bank demand drives most of the price upside we forecast by end-2027 (60 tonnes/month through 2026-28 vs. a 17 tonnes/month pre-2022 average. While the seasonally adjusted 3MMA fell to 51 tonnes/month in September from 85 tonnes/month in August, we expect buying to have recovered as gold prices subsequently stabilized and therefore put more weight on the stronger preceding months; Exhibit 9).3 Central banks—particularly in emerging markets—have increased the pace of gold purchases roughly fivefold since 2022, following the freezing of Russian reserves. We view this as a structural shift in reserve management behavior, and we do not expect a near-term reversal. Our base case assumes that the current trend in official sector accumulation continues for another three years. Our rationale is that EM central banks remain significantly underweight gold compared to their DM counterparts, while the motivations for diversifying away from G7 reserve currencies, including geopolitical and financial risk, likely remain in place. For example, we estimate that China—the largest buyer—holds around 11.8% of its reserves in gold, compared to ~80% for the US, Germany, France, and Italy (Exhibit 11). The global average is above 20%, which we view as a plausible medium-term target for large EM central banks, based on historical precedent, current positioning, and our conversations with EM central bank reserve managers. For instance, Russia increased its gold share 3 Our September central bank nowcast fell to 31 tonnes, below our expectations. However, this is consistent with our finding that central bank buying tends to slow temporarily after sharp and volatile gold price increases before recovering once prices stabilize. Given the subsequent pullback in gold, we expect buying to recover in our October reading and therefore put more weight on the stronger preceding three months than on September alone. Separately, central bank gold holdings in custody at the Bank of England rose sharply in September (+ 82 tonnes) by more than we can explain through implied UK net monetary gold imports (17 tonnes) or NY Fed custodial (0 tonnes), pointing to additional London OTC purchases being stored in custody at the Bank of England that are not captured by our nowcast of central bank buying. Exhibit 9: Our GS Central Bank Gold Purchases Nowcast Fell to 51 Tonnes/Month in September on a 3-Month Seasonally Adjusted Basis, From 85 Tonnes/Month in August (vs. a Pre‑2022 Average of 17 Tonnes) Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 9 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst from 8% to 20% between 2014 and 2020, and repatriated its gold holdings ahead of sanctions. If the largest official buyer—China—were targeting an allocation of 20%, and maintained an average pace of ~20 tonnes per month (in line with their 12MMA) (Exhibit 10), we estimate it would take approximately three years to reach a 20% gold share. Our estimate also accounts for the fact that sustained global central bank buying (at 60 tonnes/month) would likely raise gold prices over time — thereby increasing the notional value of existing holdings and helping reach allocation targets more quickly (see Appendix for details).4 A recent World Gold Council survey supports our view: a record 45% of the 76 central banks surveyed between February and May 2026 expect to increase their own gold reserves over the next 12 months – the highest share since the survey began in 2018 – while ~90% expect global reserves to rise with the remainder expecting broadly stable holdings. 4 A broader gold rally driven by private-investor demand for gold as a macro-policy hedge could shorten the horizon by lifting prices beyond what central bank buying at 60 tonnes/month alone would imply. Exhibit 10: China Was the Largest Identifiable Buyer in September at 20 Tonnes Source: PBOC, Goldman Sachs Group Inc. 16 November 2026 10 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Q6. Could China’s gold allocation ultimately exceed your 20% plausible target? Yes. We see risks to our estimate of China’s 20% gold allocation target as skewed to the upside because larger gold reserves could support RMB tion. The path toward a more important international currency broadly has three steps: increasing its use in third-country trade, increasing its role in international debt markets and, ultimately, establishing it in other countries’ reserves. While the first two steps are already underway, the final step is typically the hardest for any emerging reserve currency, as reserve managers seek diversification from the existing reserve system while also considering the composition of assets underpinning the alternative. History suggests gold can help bridge this transition: as a neutral reserve asset that does not depend on any issuer’s or political alignment, gold can strengthen confidence in an international currency. Large gold holdings helped underpin confidence in the USD as it overtook the GBP as the dominant reserve currency after World War II, reinforcing the notion that the currency was “as good as gold.” Whether or not an emerging currency ultimately achieves dominant reserve status, gold accumulation can therefore form part of the strategy, suggesting China’s desired gold allocation could ultimately exceed 20%. Q7. There have been reports that Türkiye’s central bank has sold significant amount of reserves since the onset of the Middle East conflict. Could central bank gold sales broaden? We think broader central bank gold selling is unlikely — with our nowcast instead showing a pickup in central bank purchases since May — while even Türkiye’s reported decline likely overstates outright sales. Türkiye’s reserve reporting is unusual because gold swaps can appear as declines in reported gold reserves even when the gold has not been outright sold, potentially accounting for part of the 129-tonne decline at the onset of the Middle East conflict and its subsequent rapid rebound (Exhibit 12). Exhibit 11: China’s Estimated 11.8% Gold Allocation Leaves Significant Room to Reach a Plausible 20% Target Source: IMF, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 11 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst More fundamentally, Türkiye is an outlier: as an EM central bank, it faces potential FX liquidity needs, while its unusually high gold allocation of more than 60% of FX reserves makes gold (swaps) a more natural source of that liquidity than for most EM reserve managers, which typically hold significantly less than 20% in gold. Only a small group of countries share this profile: Kyrgyzstan, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan also have unusually high gold allocations, while Russia and Venezuela face more idiosyncratic constraints on their other reserve assets, similarly making gold a more natural source of liquidity. We therefore view these countries as outliers where gold swaps or sales are more plausible, rather than as a signal of broader EM central bank selling. We are skeptical about concerns that Gulf countries might also sell gold going forward. Gulf countries hold significantly lower gold shares in their reserves. Gold accounts for roughly 4% of reserves in the UAE, 8% in Saudi Arabia, 5% in Oman, and around 24% in Qatar, compared to more than 60% of Türkiye ’s FX reserves, an unusually high share for an EM economy (Exhibit 13). Gulf economies typically operate dollar pegs, implying that FX intervention is more likely to occur through US Treasury liquidation rather than gold sales. The Gulf’s reserve structure reduces the likelihood that Gulf central banks would need to liquidate gold for FX management purposes. Exhibit 12: Türkiye’s Central Bank Data Show a Pickup in Gold Reserves After a 129-Tonne Decline at the Start of the Middle East Conflict Source: Central Bank of the Republic of Turkiye, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 12 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Q8. Could DM central banks with large legacy gold holdings become sellers? We view that risk as less likely now. If anything, interest in gold and reserve security is broadening beyond EM central banks. DM central banks have largely remained on the sidelines of the buying wave since 2022, partly because they already hold substantial gold reserves for historical reasons, typically diversified across domestic and foreign custody locations, notably the Bank of England and the New York Fed, to manage jurisdictional, political and physical risks. Concerns about geopolitical instability were among the reasons some European central banks moved part of their gold holdings to New York during the Cold War. But DM central bank feedback suggests that the debate is increasingly shifting from whether to own gold to where to store it: for instance, France and the Netherlands have recently reportedly moved gold holdings away from New York. The greater focus on reserve security suggests DM reserve managers are increasingly considering the tail risks that give gold its strategic value in the first place, reinforcing the case for retaining rather than selling gold. Silver: The Squeeze Is Over, and the Fed Is Still Hiking Q9. Silver had an extraordinary start to the year — peaking above $120/toz —, with extreme price volatility. Do you expect that to repeat in 2027? Not in our base case. The 2025/26 silver rally reflected an unusual combination of rising investor demand and tight London liquidity that we do not expect to happen through a Fed hiking cycle (Exhibit 14). Exhibit 13: Türkiye’s Gold Share in FX Reserves Is Significantly Higher Than in Gulf Countries Source: IFS, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 13 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Speculation around US trade policy, with silver on the critical minerals list and therefore theoretically eligible for tariffs despite its April 2025 exemption, encouraged pre-positioning of metal into the US during 2025, drawing inventories out of London, where global benchmark prices are set. As London inventories thinned, strong investor flows — supported by Fed cuts, silver’s catch-up to gold trade and spillovers from the debasement trade — absorbed an increasing share of the remaining available metal and ultimately triggered a liquidity squeeze (Exhibit 15). While 1,000 tonnes of weekly net silver demand would typically lift prices by around 2%, we estimate that price sensitivity rose to roughly 7% during the squeeze. When investor demand subsequently weakened, tightness eased and prices fell sharply. Exhibit 14: Silver Peaked in Early 2026 as Rising Investor Demand Collided With Tight London Liquidity Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 14 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst We think a repeat of the 2025/26 squeeze is unlikely in 2027: Even if renewed tariff concerns were to pull silver from London into the US again, Fed hikes through early 2027 should suppress ETF demand, removing the second leg of the 2025/26 squeeze. Once the Fed returns to easing, recovering ETF demand could lift silver prices again, but another London liquidity squeeze would likely require renewed tariff concerns to simultaneously restart US inventory building. Q10. Is the gold-silver ratio still relevant to watch? With the ratio back near the top of its historical range, should silver outperform gold again? No, we think gold may outglitter silver again in 2027, at least through the Fed hiking cycle. Just like gold — investment demand is the main driver of silver prices. Historically, the private investment flows move in tandem across gold and silver markets (Exhibit 16), keeping the gold-silver ratio within a broad 45-80 range (Exhibit 17). Exhibit 15: Tariff Concerns Drew Silver to the US, Draining London Inventories; Surging Investor Demand Then Absorbed Remaining Silver, Creating a Impact on Prices Source: Bloomberg, LBMA, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 15 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst But since 2022, gold has decoupled as central bank buying surged, lifting gold prices even without private investment inflows. Silver, which lacks that central bank bid, lagged. The 2025/26 London silver liquidity squeeze temporarily reversed that divergence, pushing silver sharply higher and the ratio toward the bottom of its historical range. As that squeeze unwound, the gold-silver ratio moved back toward the top of the range, but we don’t see that as a signal for renewed silver outperformance. Fed hikes should weigh on private investment demand for both metals, but gold retains the structural bid from central banks. With another silver liquidity squeeze unlikely during the hiking cycle (see Q9), we expect gold to outglitter silver again in 2027, at least until the Fed returns Exhibit 16: Silver and Gold’s Main Driver — Private Investment Flows — Move in Tandem... Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research Exhibit 17: ...Keeping the Gold-Silver Price Ratio Within a Broad 45-80 Range Until Gold Decoupled in 2022 on Central Bank Gold Purchases Gray shading denotes US recessions; red shading denotes the London silver liquidity squeeze. Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 16 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst to easing. Platinum and Palladium: Still Fragmented Q11. Platinum and palladium remain under Section 232 investigation for US tariffs. What does that mean for the outlook? We think the main risk is continued supply fragmentation and volatility from persistent US tariff uncertainty (Exhibit 18), but see outright US tariffs on platinum and palladium as unlikely. Platinum and palladium are critical inputs, particularly for the automotive sector, but global supply is exceptionally concentrated: Southern Africa accounts for roughly 82%/46% of platinum/palladium supply and Russia another 11%/39% — creating significant disruption risk. Reducing reliance on foreign critical mineral supply and rebuilding domestic capacity appear to have become increasingly important US policy objectives. In theory, tariffs are a way to achieve this policy objective: make imported minerals more expensive, protect domestic producers and ultimately incentivize investment in US mines, smelters and refineries. In practice, the PGM supply response is limited. US domestic mine production is limited, scaling output is technically and geologically challenging, and new mines and refineries take many years to permit build and bring online. Because tariffs can change much faster than production capacity can be built, the resulting policy uncertainty can undermine the long-term investment they are intended to encourage. But the risk of tariffs still achieves a national-security objective by pulling metal inventories into the US without requiring large-scale government purchases or immediately raising costs for downstream consumers. The result is lower liquidity outside the US — and thus price volatility — even if global inventories remain comfortable on paper. Exhibit 18: US Tariff Risk Since 2025 Has Driven Platinum and Palladium Supply Fragmentation, Increasing Volatility and Squeeze Risk Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research 16 November 2026 17 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Q12. Does ongoing fragmented supply mean higher platinum and palladium prices in 2027? Not necessarily. Supply fragmentation keeps volatility risk elevated, but the 2027 demand backdrop is more mixed. Fed hikes should weigh on investment demand, particularly for platinum, which has a larger investment component than palladium. The EV transition should also continue to reduce PGM demand, although the impact may differ between the two metals. Platinum faces the greater European EV headwind, but also more upside from defense spending. Europe has historically been more diesel-heavy, making its vehicle fleet relatively more platinum-intensive. Rising EV penetration therefore weighs particularly on platinum demand. Our auto analysts reported BEV sales in Europe up 66% yoy in August 2026, while implied ICE sales fell 10% yoy. However, military vehicles remain heavily diesel-based, making higher defense spending a potential offset. Palladium has relatively more support from hybrids and the slower US EV transition. Gasoline vehicles are more palladium-intensive, and because HEVs are mostly gasoline-engine vehicles, hybrid growth supports palladium demand. In the US, BEV sales fell 45% yoy in 3Q26, while hybrid sales rose 27% yoy in 3Q26. This suggests gasoline-linked catalyst demand may persist for longer as hybrids gain share and BEV adoption slows. 16 November 2026 18 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Appendix To estimate how long it would take for China to reach a given gold reserve share (e.g. 20%), we solve numerically for the number of months n such that: P(n) x Q(n) = targeted gold share x total reserves (incl. gold reserves P(n) x Q(n)) where: Q(n) = current gold holdings + n x average monthly additions n P(n) = current gold price x (1 + (2% *global central bank demand/100))^n n We assume a 60 tonnes/month of global central bank demand and apply our rule of thumb that every 100 tonnes/month raises the gold price by ~2%. 16 November 2026 19 Goldman Sachs Precious Analyst Disclosure Appendix Reg AC We, Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven, hereby certify that all of the views expressed in this report accurately reflect our personal views, which have not been influenced by considerations of the firm’s business or client relationships. 快评三句话：去杠杆兑现、历史上属常见模式、逆转可期但偏慢 风险兑现： 上周高盛已提示"股市驱动去杠杆"的战术性下行风险（tactical downside risk），本周兑现——与 AI 周期（AI cycle）不确定性 相关的股市急跌触发追加保证金（margin calls）与大范围去杠杆（broad deleveraging），成为黄金周度下跌 8.0%（8% w/w） 的重要推手；动量转弱随后引发 CTA 趋势基金追加卖出 ，放大了跌幅。 常见模式： 黄金在股市抛售初期下跌是常见模式（common pattern）——黄金 高流动性 使其成为风险资产急跌时的"现金来源"（source of cash）；若不确定性持续，价格通常随后回升。2008 年金融危机（GFC）、2020 年 3 月新冠疫情冲击（Covid shock）、2025 年 4 月"解放日"抛售（Liberation Day sell-off）均是先例。 前瞻： 预计下行压力 终将逆转，但年末附近节奏可能更慢 ：部分对冲基金不愿在年末前重建风险敞口；叠加市场预期的 12 月美联储（Fed）加息 ，为推迟重建黄金多头提供了另一重理由——尽管投机仓位（speculative positioning）已经偏低。 Section 01 事件复盘：AI 不确定性触发股市急跌与黄金去杠杆 The Shock: Equity-Driven Deleveraging Hits Gold 这是一份发布于 2026-11-23 11:12AM GMT 的一页式快评（Precious Comment），属于高盛大宗商品研究（Commodities Research）系列。作者开篇即点明： 上周报告提示的战术性下行风险本周已经兑现（materialized） 。 传导逻辑链 Transmission chain 触发源： 与 AI 周期不确定性 （uncertainty over the AI cycle）相关的股市急剧回撤（sharp equity drawdown）； 流动性冲击： 股市急跌触发 追加保证金通知（margin calls） ，投资者被迫筹措现金，进而引发 更大范围的去杠杆 （broader deleveraging）； 黄金被卖出： 黄金因流动性极佳而首当其冲被变现，成为金价周度下跌 8.0% w/w 的重要推手（contributing to）； 第二波放大： 价格下跌使 动量（momentum）转弱 ，触发 CTA（趋势跟踪基金）追加卖出 （additional CTA selling），进一步放大跌幅（amplifying the move）。 要点： 本次下跌的驱动是"流动性挤出 + 动量放大"的交易层面机制，而非黄金基本面恶化的信号——原文用词是"contributing to"（促成），即去杠杆是 8.0% w/w 跌幅的重要成因之一，动量与 CTA 卖盘则负责放大。 图 1 · 原文快评版面：标题、三段要点与作者栏 | Precious Comment: Gold Caught in Broad Deleveraging, p.1 — Source: Goldman Sachs Commodities Research（2026-11-23） Section 02 历史规律：黄金在股市抛售初期下跌是常见模式 A Common Pattern in Equity Sell-Offs 高盛强调， 金价在股市抛售初期下跌是常见模式（common pattern） ，其机制在于黄金的 流动性 ：在风险资产急跌、投资者急需现金时，黄金因极易变现而成为" 现金来源 （source of cash）"，遭到先卖。 先跌后回的路径 Down first, recover later 关键的条件分支是： 若不确定性持续存在（if uncertainty persists），价格通常随后回升（typically recover） 。也就是说，去杠杆引发的初始下跌是"技术性"的，而当冲击的不确定性延续时，黄金的避险属性会重新接管定价。 时期 事件（原文例证） 原文含义 2008 全球金融危机 GFC（Global Financial Crisis） 三者均为"黄金先跌、随后随不确定性持续而回升"路径的历史例证（as seen during …, among others） 2020 年 3 月 新冠疫情冲击 Covid shock（March 2020） 2025 年 4 月 "解放日"抛售 Liberation Day sell-off（April 2025） 含义： 把本次 8.0% w/w 的下跌放进历史框架看，它更像 GFC、Covid shock、Liberation Day 的重演——去杠杆期的初始下跌并不否定黄金的中期逻辑，不确定性若延续，价格历史上均出现修复。 Section 03 前瞻展望：压力终将逆转，但年末节奏偏慢 Outlook: Reversal Expected, More Slowly into Year-End 高盛对方向的判断明确： 预计下行压力最终会逆转（eventually reverse） ；但对节奏给出保留—— 年末附近逆转可能更慢（more slowly around year-end） 。理由有二： 对冲基金年末行为： 部分对冲基金可能不愿在年末前重建风险敞口（reluctant to rebuild risk into year-end），压制多头回补的力度； 12 月美联储加息预期： 市场预期的 December Fed hike 为"推迟重建黄金多头"提供了另一个理由——尽管 投机仓位已经偏低 （lower speculative positioning，本应利于回补）。 推论： 金价修复的节奏瓶颈不在基本面而在资金面——年末风控 + 加息落地前，反弹可能延后；一旦这两重约束解除（跨年之后、加息靴子落地），叠加已偏低的投机仓位与延续的不确定性，下行压力逆转的条件将更齐备。 LLC Precious Comment: Gold Caught in Broad Deleveraging 23 November 2026 | 11:12AM GMT Last week, we flagged tactical downside risk from potential equity-driven n deleveraging, and that risk has now materialized. The sharp equity drawdown — linked to the uncertainty over the AI cycle — triggered margin calls and broader deleveraging, contributing to gold’s 8% w/w decline. Weaker momentum subsequently triggered additional CTA selling, amplifying the move. Gold prices falling initially during equity sell-offs is a common pattern. Gold’s n liquidity makes it a source of cash during sharp risk-asset sell-offs, causing an initial decline before prices typically recover if uncertainty persists, as seen during the 2008 GFC, March 2020 Covid shock and April 2025 Liberation Day sell-off, among others. We expect the downward pressure to eventually reverse, but potentially more n slowly around year-end. Some hedge funds may be reluctant to rebuild risk into year-end, while the expected December Fed hike provides another reason to delay rebuilding gold longs despite lower speculative positioning. reports.stext: 铁矿石：下调 2027 年预测至约 90 美元/吨，CMRG 价值漏损或达 100 亿美元 GOLDMAN SACHS · 全球金属与采矿 · 铁矿石 铁矿石：下调 2027 年预测至约 90 美元/吨，CMRG 价值漏损或达 100 亿美元 Global Metals & Mining: Iron Ore — Cutting Our 2027 Forecast to ~US$90/t, CMRG Value Leakage Could Reach US$10bn 机构 ：Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research · 分析师 ：Paul Young / Matt Greene / Chris Bulgin / Riccardo D'Agata 等 · 日期 ：2026-11-14 12:08AM AEDT · 页数 ：37 页 本页为第三方研究报告的中文精读摘要，图表截取自原报告 PDF，版权归原机构所有。 目录 CONTENTS 价格预测：下调 2027 年至 92 美元/吨 CMRG：谈判、折扣与价值漏损 成本曲线：更高、但仍有支撑 库存与供需跟踪 覆盖公司影响、评级与估值 KEY POINTS 核心观点 铁矿石跌破 90 美元/吨 （2024 年以来首次）； 4Q26 预测下调至 93 美元 、未来数月下行风险至 85-90 美元； 2027 年预测由 96 下调至 92 美元/吨 （VA 共识 96，有下行风险）。 市场转向平衡：中国/全球钢产量同比 -3%/-2% 、澳巴发运改善、 Simandou 放量（当前约 23 Mtpa → 2028 年 >100 Mtpa）、CMRG 集采影响持续。 CMRG 折扣（GSe 有效值）：BHP 约 2.7% （4 月）、RIO 约 2.1% （10 月、多年期至 2028/5，保留 PBF 营销权）、Anglo 约 2.3% ；FMG/Hancock 年杪期限谈判中，FMG 未售库存 4Mt+4-5Mt、或减产 Cloud Break（约 30 Mtpa）；港口圈存 10-15Mt SSF。 价值漏损：五大上市矿商合计约 11 亿美元 EBITDA/年 、10 年 NPV(5%) 约 88 亿美元 （报告标题称可达 100 亿美元）；FMG 占其 2027 EBITDA 约 7.8%。 成本支撑：品位调整后 90 分位约 95 美元/吨 （两年 +20%），>300Mt（约 20% 海运供应）在 90 美元以下现金负成本 → 85 美元强支撑 ；未调整口径 90 分位约 110-111 美元。 长期价格维持 2030 年 85 美元（实际）/95-100 名义 ：矿山枯竭约 10 亿吨/十年、品位下降约 50Mt、2030 年可竞争海运市场约 20 亿吨。 评级：BHP.AX/RIO.AX、RIO.LN、CIA 买入 （PT 64.1/170.7/£78.0/C$2.8）；MIN、DRR 中性 （A$48.0/A$4.2）；FMG 卖出 （US$12.2，FY27 FCF 约 -5 亿美元、需借款分红）；AAL 不评级。 股价隐含价格（NAV=股价）：MIN 96 / FMG 94 / CIA 82 / BHP 80 / DRR 77 / RIO 75 美元（实际）——RIO/BHP 现价隐含价格低于 GS 预测，被视为低估。 Section 01 价格预测：下调 2027 年至 92 美元/吨 Iron Ore Price Outlook: 2027 Cut to ~US$92/t 铁矿石价格持续去估值，近期 跌破 90 美元/吨——2024 年以来首次 。下跌反映市场转向平衡：中国/全球钢产量同比 -3%/-2% （至 9 月底）、澳巴大矿山发运改善、西非 Simandou 新供应放量，以及中国矿产资源集团（CMRG）集中采购带来的持续动态。 高盛将 4Q26 61% Fe 预测下调至 93 美元/吨 ，未来几个月存在下探 85-90 美元 的风险——理由是中国钢产量与钢厂利润率疲弱（钢价弱、焦煤贵）、约 160Mt 的高位港口库存、以及年末海运发运强劲预期；12 月钢厂补库至中国新年前（2 月初）的季节性反弹预计短命。 2027 年预测由 96 下调至 92 美元/吨 ：Simandou 发运爬坡（当前约 23 Mtpa，2028 年 ramp 至 >100 Mtpa）叠加中国钢产量再降 2-3%，而澳巴发运仅温和增长；VA 共识 2027 约 96 美元，存在下行风险。 成本支撑与长期价格： 品位调整后 90 分位边际成本约 95 美元/吨 （两年升逾 20%）；90 美元以下现金负成本供应 >300Mt（约 20% 海运供应）→ 85 美元附近有强成本支撑 ；巴西/印度等高成本产商已开始减产。长期（2030）基准价维持 85 美元/吨（实际）／95-100 名义 ：矿山枯竭约 10 亿吨/十年、品位下降（约 50Mt 影响）构成结构性支撑，2030 年可竞争海运市场规模仍约 20 亿吨。 Fig 1 · GS 铁矿石价格与运费基准假设：61% Fe 2026/2027/2028 分别为 100/92/94 美元/吨（2027 由 96 下调至 92），长期 85（实际）/99（名义） | GS base case iron ore price and freight assumptions — Source: Platts, Company data, Goldman Sachs GIR（Exhibit 1, p5，截至 2026-11-12 定价） Fig 2 · GSe 预测 vs Visible Alpha 共识与远期曲线：2027 年 GSe 92 vs VA 共识 96（-5%）、远期 89；澳-中运费 GSe 高出共识 13%-26% | GSe iron ore price and bulk freight forecasts vs. Cons & Forward curve — Source: Goldman Sachs GIR, Visible Alpha, FactSet（Exhibit 2, p5） Fig 3 · 海运铁矿石及球团矿价格（CIF 中国）：61% Fe 近期跌破 90 美元/吨（2024 年以来首次） | Seaborne iron ore and pellet prices (CIF China) — Source: Goldman Sachs GIR, Bloomberg（Exhibit 24, p16） Fig 4 · 中国钢产量（年化）：2026 年同比约 -3%（至 9 月底），全球约 -2%，驱动铁矿石转向平衡 | China Steel Production (annualised) — Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 29, p17） Fig 5 · 几内亚 Simandou 发运（年化）：当前约 23 Mtpa，高盛预计 2028 年 ramp 至 >100 Mtpa | Guinea (Simandou) iron ore shipments (Mtpa annualised) — Source: Goldman Sachs GIR, Global Trade Tracker（Exhibit 23, p15） Section 02 CMRG：谈判、折扣与价值漏损 CMRG Negotiations, Discounts and Value Leakage CMRG 集中海运铁矿采购（主要面向澳洲矿山）并推动定价权回归境内：其集中采购已覆盖 过半数中国钢厂 ，以托管人/代理/长协谈判者身份运作，并推动在 Platts 指数之外引入人民币计价的 PRAs（COREX、Mysteel、Argus、Fastmarkets）。 已达成条款（GSe 估计）： BHP 4 月落定，部分品种对部分指数 1.8-2.2% 代理费/折扣， 有效折扣约 2.7% ；Anglo 8 月就 Minas Rio 与 Kumba 落定约 2.3% ；RIO 10 月据报道多年期（至 2028 年 5 月）、名义 1.75%，保留 flagship Pilbara Blend Fines 的营销权与部分溢价， 有效折扣约 2.1% 。 FMG 与 Hancock 谈判中 （FMG 自 6 月开始、获年杪期限）；FMG 披露 CMRG 相关未售库存 9 月底约 4Mt 、10 月预计再增 4-5Mt ，若谈判拖沓可能减产（高盛认为最可能是高成本的 Cloud Break，约 30 Mtpa，主产 SSF）。交易员反馈：中国港口约 10-15Mt FMG 低品 56-57% Fe SSF 被圈存，一旦成交可能流向市场；CMRG 对 SSF/Fortune Fines 目标约 3% 折扣 （叠加现有约 20% 的 ViU 折扣）。 价值漏损测算： 按 85-90 美元 IODEX，五大上市矿商（BHP、RIO、AAL、FMG、MIN）合计每年 EBITDA 漏损约 11 亿美元 ，10 年累计 NPV(5%) 约 88 亿美元 （报告标题："可达 100 亿美元"）。分企业：BHP 约 3.8 亿美元/年（占 2027 EBITDA 1.2%）、RIO 约 3.0 亿（1.1%）、FMG 约 3.7 亿（7.8%）、MIN 约 0.6 亿（3.8%）、AAL 约 0.2 亿。 Fig 6 · CMRG '已达成'条款估计：BHP 有效折扣 ~2.7%（4 月）、RIO ~2.1%（10 月，至 2028 年 5 月）、Anglo ~2.3%，FMG 未成交（年杪期限）；合计约 11 亿美元 EBITDA/年 | We compare our estimates of 'agreed' terms — Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 3, p6，GSe 估计值） Fig 7 · CMRG 价值漏损测算：按 90 美元 IODEX，五大上市矿商合计每年 EBITDA 漏损约 11 亿美元，10 年 NPV(5%) 约 88 亿美元 | ~US$1.1bn pa of value leakage over 10 years, NPV (at 5%) of US$8-9bn, at US$85-90/t IODEX — Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 4, p7） Fig 8 · FMG 品牌粉矿港口库存：无 CMRG 协议下 SSF 等低品库存再度攀升（9 月底约 4Mt、10 月预计再增 4-5Mt） | FMG branded fines stockpile (Mt) — Source: Mysteel, Data compiled by Goldman Sachs GIR（Exhibit 35, p18） Fig 9 · FMG 港口库存（分品牌）在 CMRG 未决期间持续增长 | FMG stockpiles growing without a CMRG resolution — Source: Mysteel, Data compiled by Goldman Sachs GIR（Exhibit 36, p18） Section 03 成本曲线：更高、但仍有支撑 2026 Cost Curves: Higher, Yet Supportive 2026 年品位调整后全口径成本曲线（C1+权利金+SIB 资本开支、中国 CIF、含国产矿）显示： 90 分位边际成本约 95 美元/吨 、95 分位约 100、75 分位约 81； 超过 200Mt 供应在 95 美元/吨（61% Fe 当量）以下现金亏损 。未作品位调整口径下 90 分位约 110-111 美元/吨 ，较 2024 年的约 95 上升，主因现场成本与运费上涨——不过近期油价回落带动运费下行，成本曲线重心有所下移。 Fig 10 · 2026 年全球海运铁矿石成本曲线（品位调整、全口径）：90 分位边际成本约 95 美元/吨，>200Mt 供应在 95 美元以下现金亏损 | 2026 global contestable grade adjusted seaborne iron ore cost curve — Source: Company data, S&P Global Market Intelligence, MySteel, GS GIR（Exhibit 13, p12） Fig 11 · 未作品位调整的成本曲线：90 分位约 110-111 美元/吨，较 2024 年的约 95 上升（现场成本与运费上涨） | Unadjusted grade basis cost curve, 90th percentile ~US$110/t — Source: Company data, S&P Global Market Intelligence, MySteel, GS GIR（Exhibit 14, p13） Section 04 库存与供需跟踪 Inventory and Flow Tracking 中国港口库存总量约 160Mt 处于高位（约 5 周消耗量），按来源地以巴西、澳洲矿为主；RIO/BHP 品牌粉矿港存 10 月起自高位回落。FMG 品牌低品粉（SSF 等）在 CMRG 未决期间持续累积——这既是谈判压力的体现，也是协议达成后的潜在供应释放（10-15Mt 圈存量）。 Fig 12 · 中国港口铁矿石库存按来源地：总量约 160Mt 高位（巴西/澳洲为主） | Chinese iron ore port stocks by supply source (Mt) — Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 37, p18） Fig 13 · 中国港口 RIO/BHP 品牌粉矿库存（15 港样本）：10 月以来回落但仍处高位 | China port inventories - RIO & BHP fines — Source: Mysteel, Goldman Sachs GIR（Exhibit 34, p18） Section 05 覆盖公司影响、评级与估值 Coverage Impact, Ratings and Valuations 基于更低的 4Q26/2027/2028 价格预测并计入未来约十年的 CMRG 折扣，高盛下调全球铁矿石板块盈利、NAV 与目标价： BHP 与 RIO 2027-29 EBITDA 下调 2-4% （其中约 1 个百分点来自 CMRG 折扣）；铁矿石约占两者中期 EBITDA 的 40%。 分企业要点 BHP： PT 64.1 美元（-2%），AX 买入、LN 中性；铜约占中期 EBITDA 50-55%，任何大幅回撤视为 BHP.AX/RIO 买入机会。RIO.AX 约 6.5x NTM EBITDA、0.8x NAV，略折价于 BHP.AX（约 7x / 0.9x NAV）。 RIO： PT 170.7 美元（AX，-3%）/ £78.0（LN），维持买入；EBITDA 低于 VA 共识 >10%（BHP 约 -5%）。本半年跑输 BHP 约 10%（铁矿石去估值、铝 1H27 转过剩预期、50 亿美元资产出售信心低迷）；2026-30 铜当量产量增长约 2%/年优于 BHP（无增长，FY27 见底），但 2030-35 BHP 约 3%/年 vs RIO 基本无增长。两者 2027 年 FCF 收益率仅 4-5%。 FMG（卖出）： FY27/28 EBITDA -3%/-11%，FY27 低于共识约 20%；NAV/PT -6%/-8% 至 12.2 美元（约 20% 下行空间）；FY27 FCF 约 -5 亿美元 、1H FY27 亏损，本半年度需 借款支付股息 ；若年杪前未达成协议可能减产 Cloud Break；长期 Pilbara 产能替换与 >45 亿美元/年资本开支（含 Belinga、Alta Copper）继续压制 FCF 与分红。 MIN（中性）： 不直接与 CMRG 谈判（Baosteel 持 Onslow 约 20% 权益并拥有至多约 60% 提货权），但 Onslow/Pilbara hub 实现价预计随 FMG 低品折价联动；FY27/28 EBITDA -3%/-5%，PT 48.0 澳元（-4%）。 CIA（买入）： 主要售予贸易商与中国/日本/中东/欧洲钢厂直供，不经 CMRG；FY28/29 EBITDA -8~10%，PT 2.8 加元（-3%）；现价约 0.5x 修订后 NAV（约 4.0 加元）；Bloom Lake 十年投入 >60 亿加元 vs 当前 EV 仅约 25 亿加元——价值显著但短期风险大（现货价下 NTM FCF 约 -1 亿加元）。 DRR（中性）： 通过 BHP Mining Area C 权利金传导低基准价与 CMRG 折扣；新宣布 7400 万美元收购 Santa Cruz 铜项目约 1.65% 权利金（尚未交割、未入基准）；PT 4.2 澳元。 Anglo（不评级）： 中期 EBITDA -1~6%、EPS -1~9%（铁矿石价格/运费下调 + Quellaveco 铜矿小幅产量修正）。 股价已计入多少？ NAV=股价 反推的 61% Fe 实际价格： MIN 96 / FMG 94 / CIA 82 / BHP 80 / DRR 77 / RIO 75 美元/吨 ——RIO/BHP 现价隐含价格低于 GS 2027 预测（92）与长期价格（85 实际），高盛认为两者被低估，但提示 2027 年共识 EBITDA 有下修风险。 Fig 14 · 澳洲矿商 NAV/盈利/目标价调整：BHP PT 64.1（-2%）、RIO 170.7（-3%）、FMG 12.2（-8%）、CIA 2.8（-3%）、DRR 4.2（-2%）、MIN 48.0（-4%） | NAV, earnings and PT changes (Aus Miners) — Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 5, p8） Fig 15 · 2027 年 FCF 收益率（GSe vs 现货价）：BHP/RIO 约 4-6%，FMG 约 -4%，CIA 约 -43%（现货口径） | FCF yield (%) - 2027 — Source: Visible Alpha Consensus Data, Goldman Sachs GIR（Exhibit 8, p11） Fig 16 · 股价已计入的铁矿石价格（NAV=股价 反推，61% Fe 实际）：MIN 96 / FMG 94 / CIA 82 / BHP 80 / DRR 77 / RIO 75 美元/吨 | What's priced in to our coverage: goal seeking commodity price so that NAV = share price — Source: Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 12, p11） 原文：Global Metals & Mining — Iron Ore; cutting our 2027 forecast to ~US$90/t, CMRG value leakage could reach US$10bn（Goldman Sachs Equity Research, 2026-11-14）。 Samantha Dart / Daan Struyven · 日期 ：2026-11-12 10:19PM GMT · 页数 ：7 页 本页为第三方研究报告的中文精读摘要，图表截取自原报告 PDF，版权归原机构所有。 目录 CONTENTS 报告核心：中期选举后的铜价框架 风险一：AI 仓位与数据中心暂停令 风险二：美国关税与囤库假设 KEY POINTS 核心观点 维持 2027 年铜价 15,400 美元/吨 预测不变（较现货约 13% 上行），提示中期选举后两大下行风险： AI 相关仓位 与 美国关税 。 LME 铜价一个月内下跌约 7% 至 13,588 美元/吨 ，主因民主党横扫后 AI 股票波动；但洋山进口溢价升破 200 美元/吨 历史新高、美国以外库存处季节性低位——基本面并未松动。 AI 风险主要经由仓位传导：COMEX+LME 净多头占比从 9 月底约 21% 降至 约 9% ，低于 2027 年假设的 16%；仓位维持现状则 2027 年均价约 14,600 美元/吨 。 数据中心暂停令属 延迟风险 ：在建容量足以覆盖 2028 年前需求；即便德州在建项目全部推迟 6 个月，仅约 50kt 需求移出 2027 年，价格影响至多约 -100 美元/吨（至 15,300 美元/吨）。 关税预期有限：COMEX-LME 价差仅隐含 2027 年 1 月约 1% 关税；若 2027 年约 400kt 美国囤库完全停止，均价约 14,500 美元/吨 。 关税风险未消除：232 条款决定权在总统，立法回滚需两党支持；民主党未必优先反对精炼铜关税。 铜自 2025 年底以来与 GS AI 数据中心篮子联动，若股市提前定价 AI 资本开支见顶，仓位可能继续受抑。 Section 01 报告核心：中期选举后的铜价框架 Core View: Copper Framework After the US Midterms 高盛商品研究维持 2027 年 LME 铜价 15,400 美元/吨 的预测不变（较现货约有 13% 的上行空间），但明确提示中期选举（民主党横扫，"蓝色浪潮"）之后的两大下行风险： AI 相关的投资者仓位 与 美国关税 。该预测建立在两大收紧力量之上：潜在关税落地前美国持续的补库行为、中国的废铜短缺，以及处于高位的投资者仓位——而中期选举恰恰将第一项与第三项驱动力置于风险之中。 过去一个月 LME 铜价下跌约 7% 至 13,588 美元/吨 ，主要受民主党横扫后 AI 相关股票波动的拖累。但高盛强调，实体基本面依然紧张：中国洋山铜进口溢价已升至 超过 200 美元/吨的历史新高 ，主要反映中国及美国以外地区金属可获得性有限、库存处于季节性低位。 结论： 本轮调整是 仓位驱动 而非基本面松动，physical 紧张格局未变，回调反而提升了铜的对冲与配置价值。 Fig 1 · 中国洋山铜进口溢价飙升至近年区间之上，突破 200 美元/吨历史新高 | China Copper Import Premium Has Surged Well Above Its Range of Recent Years — Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Oilgram 原报告 Exhibit 1, p2） Fig 2 · 美国以外可视阴极铜库存接近季节性低位，2026 年（红线）显著低于 2019-23 区间 | Ex-US Visible Copper Inventories Are Near Seasonal Lows — Source: Wind, Bloomberg, SMM, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 2, p3） Section 02 风险一：AI 仓位与数据中心暂停令 Risk 1: AI Positioning and Data Center Moratoria 仓位已经跌破预测假设 COMEX 与 LME 合计净多头占未平仓合约（OI）比重已从 9 月底的约 21% 降至 约 9% ，显著低于高盛 2027 年所假设的 16%。若仓位停留在当前水平，模型隐含 2027 年铜价均价约 14,600 美元/吨 （低于 15,400 的基准预测）。自 2025 年底以来铜价与 GS AI 数据中心股票篮子（以半导体、电气设备等 AI 基础设施供应商为主）高度联动——若股市提前定价 AI 资本开支周期见顶，即便数据中心建设仍在推进，铜的仓位也可能持续低迷。 暂停令是延迟风险，对未来两年影响有限 高盛经济学家预计德州、佐治亚、密歇根的民主党州长将实施 短期、有条件的 新数据中心暂停令，且主要影响新项目而非在建项目。在建容量已足以覆盖 2028 年前的美国数据中心新增铜需求预测。极端情形下——假设德州全部在建项目（约占 2027 年在建铜需求 100kt）推迟 6 个月——也仅约 50kt 需求移出 2027 年，对 2027 年价格预测的影响至多约 -100 美元/吨（降至约 15,300 美元/吨）。 2029 年起风险更大 ，因为届时预测更依赖尚未开工的项目，但 Aterio 标记为"高可能性"的已公告项目管道仍远高于预测假设。 Fig 3 · LME+COMEX 净管理资金仓位占 OI 比重跌破 2027 年假设的 16%（虚线），同期 LME 铜价回落 | Copper Positioning Has Fallen Below Our 2027 Assumption — Source: Bloomberg, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 3, p3） Fig 4 · 在建数据中心容量足以覆盖 2028 年前的美国数据中心铜需求预测（红菱形为 GS 预测） | Capacity Under Construction Covers Our US Data Center Copper Demand Forecast Through 2028 — Source: Aterio, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 4, p4） Fig 5 · 德克萨斯占 2027 年在建数据中心铜需求约 100kt（深蓝柱），为州级暂停令风险敞口最大的地区 | Texas Accounts for Around 100kt of Under-Construction Copper Demand in 2027 — Source: Aterio, Goldman Sachs Global Investment Research（Exhibit 5, p4） Section 03 风险二：美国关税与囤库假设 Risk 2: US Tariffs and the Stockbuilding Assumption COMEX-LME 价差目前仅隐含 2027 年 1 月约 1% 的关税、2028 年 1 月约 6-7% ，表明市场对近期关税的预期有限。高盛 2027 年预测中假设美国 2027 年约有 400kt 的超额库存累积 ；若美国囤库完全停止，估算 2027 年均价将降至约 14,500 美元/吨 ——若今年累积的美国库存大部分回流至世界其他地区，还有进一步下行空间。 但民主党横扫并不消除关税风险： 232 条款（Section 232）下的关税决定权在总统，通过立法回滚需要两党共同支持，而民主党在接下来的谈判中未必会优先反对精炼铜关税。 原文：Base Metals Comment — Blue Wave, Copper Ripples（Goldman Sachs Commodities Research, 2026-11-12）。 仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议，观点归属原机构。

reports.stext: 没那么糟，但"超级挤压"仍在继续 | HSBC 商品经济评论 HSBC · 商品 没那么糟，但"超级挤压"仍在继续 Commodity Economic Comment — Less bad, but the 'super-squeeze' continues 机构 HSBC（Global Investment Research · Economics, Global） ｜ 日期 2026-11-16 ｜ 页数 5 ｜ 经济学家 Paul Bloxham（澳新及全球商品首席经济学家）· Jamie Culling 本页为第三方研报的中文精读整理，观点归属原机构，仅供研究参考。市场数据截至 2026-11-11 收盘。 目录 Contents 核心观点 Key takeaways 行情回顾：中期选举后的去险化回落 The post-midterm de-escalation selloff 剧情反复：油价再度反弹 The reversal 尚未消除的五大上行风险 Five upside risks 天然气与成品油：挤压最紧的环节 Gas & refined products 结论 Conclusion Section 00 核心观点 Key takeaways 行情： 2026 年商品市场大起大落——彭博商品现货指数（BCOM）10 日滚动历史波动率（年化）年内均值 18% （2025 年为 12%）。近几周价格急跌与美国中期选举时点重合：特朗普关于伊朗谈判"进展顺利""不急于达成"、进一步空袭"极不可能"的表态被解读为美以再度开战概率下降，油价领跌。 位置： BCOM 现货指数年内仍 +17% ，但已自 9 月中旬峰值回落 10% ，跌幅集中在 11 月上旬；布伦特从 10 月 30 日约 US$117/b （4 月以来高点）跌至 11 月 10 日 US$90/b 下方，回吐了 10 月地缘风险溢价的大部分。 但剧情反复： 11 月 13 日特朗普称"我们不需要与伊朗达成协议"、伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书称不会交出"哪怕一个原子"的浓缩核材料，布伦特又反弹至约 US$95/b （较低点 +7%）。 供应侧风险仍支撑商品价格。 五大上行风险未消： ①中东冲突未结束且外溢（霍尔木兹→曼德海峡、胡塞袭击沙特设施）；②多类商品库存已降至低位，缓冲垫变薄；③运费与保险成本高企（中东-亚洲原油运费 >US$30/b ，年初不足 US$3/b）；④厄尔尼诺、燃料成本与化肥供应扰动推升农产品；⑤支撑 AI 繁荣的金属（如铜）仍供不应求。 结论： 价格回落对全球通胀是好消息，但 供应挤压尚未结束 ——供应侧风险继续为商品市场托底，价格将维持高位。 Section 01 行情回顾：中期选举后的去险化回落 The post-midterm de-escalation selloff 过去几周商品价格急跌与美国中期选举时点重合，直接导火索是特朗普与华盛顿的表态：11 月 1 日称与伊朗谈判"进展顺利""不急于达成"（Axios），11 月 10 日又称进一步空袭"极不可能"（Bloomberg）——市场将其解读为 美以再次进攻的概率下降 。布伦特在 10 月 30 日升至约 US$117/b（4 月以来最高）后，11 月 10 日跌破 US$90/b，基本回吐了 10 月的地缘风险溢价。本轮急跌与 5-6 月如出一辙：彼时美伊谅解备忘录（MoU）前后商品指数下跌 15% ，随后关系再度恶化、价格又强劲反弹。 Fig 1 · 油价回落（日线，US$/b）：Oman/Dubai/WTI/Brent 四基准——10 月底布伦特升至约 US$117/b 后跌回 US$90/b 下方，近日再反弹至约 US$95/b | 1. Oil prices have pulled back … — Source: Bloomberg; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Section 02 剧情反复：油价再度反弹 The reversal: oil is bid again 就在本报告发布前几天，油价重新上涨：布伦特回升至约 US$95/b（较低点 +7%） 。触发因素是 11 月 13 日特朗普"我们不需要与伊朗达成协议"的表态，以及伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书"不会交出哪怕一个原子（浓缩核材料）"的强硬回应。 风险仍处高位，供应侧风险继续支撑商品价格。 Section 03 尚未消除的五大上行风险 Five upside risks that remain 冲突未结束： 袭击仍在继续，前进路径高度不确定；冲突已从霍尔木兹海峡外溢至曼德海峡（Bab el-Mandeb），胡塞武装近期袭击沙特基础设施。海湾原油供应虽有超预期恢复，但 HSBC 石油团队（Kim Fustier 等）认为这已是" 能指望的最好状态 "——物流紧张、运费急升，供应并未回到"正常"。 库存见底风险： 库存消耗是冲突中断下供应链得以运转、价格未冲更高极值的关键。上周美国商业原油库存 +4.7mb，但战略储备（SPR）进一步下降 -2.6mb 。"油罐底"还有多远是市场焦点；且库存迟早需要回补——届时将同步抬升需求与油价。 航运与保险成本： 中东湾-亚洲原油运费已升破 US$30/b （年初不足 US$3/b）；"暗渡"（dark transits）与船对船转运增加复杂性，航程拉长至约 23 天——超过最优时长的一倍。 农产品与天气： 厄尔尼诺加强、燃料成本高企、化肥供应扰动叠加俄乌战争。印度遭遇十余年最弱季风，稻米供应前景受损、米价自低点上涨 45% ；菲律宾农产品产出因台风收缩，泰国洪涝、越南缺水凸显天气风险；巴西 1-9 月化肥需求下滑 11% ，将对农产品产生滞后而巨大的影响。 AI 金属短缺： 支撑 AI 繁荣的部分金属（包括铜）仍然供不应求。 Fig 2 · 航运成本（周度指数）：上海出口集装箱运价指数 2026 年再度大幅走高，运力绕行与保险成本推升商品到岸价 | 4. … while shipping and insurance costs are elevated too — Source: LSEG Datastream; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Fig 3 · ENSO 强度概率（%）：本轮厄尔尼诺强度已破纪录，10-12 月至次年 6-8 月概率分布持续偏向暖水相位 | 5. The current El Niño has already broken records … — Source: NOAA; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Fig 4 · FAO 粮食价格指数（2010 年代均值=100）：名义与实际指数均处历史高位，天气风险仍在推升农产品 | 6. … with weather posing a key risk for agri-commodities — Source: UN FAO; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Section 04 天然气与成品油：挤压最紧的环节 Gas & refined products: the tightest links 海湾地区 天然气与成品油供应并未像原油一样改善 。欧洲天然气价格年内上涨 228% ；欧洲储气"峰值填充率"降至十余年最低、未达目标，北半球冬季供应风险上升。HSBC 团队已大幅上调欧洲天然气价格预测，并提示 2027 年夏季回补将非常吃紧 （"Winter squeeze, summer strain"）。成品油方面，裂解价差与炼厂毛利维持高位，俄罗斯柴油基础设施受损令柴油市场雪上加霜。 Fig 5 · 天然气价格（US$/MMBtu）：欧洲 TTF、亚洲 JKM 与美国 Henry Hub（右轴）——2026 年欧洲气价大涨，年内 +228% | 2. … but natural gas prices are still high — Source: Bloomberg; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Fig 6 · 美国柴油裂解价差（US$/b）：US Diesel-WTI 与 Nymex 1 月裂解价差仍处高位，俄罗斯炼能受损加剧成品油挤压 | 3. Diesel crack spreads and refined products prices are still elevated … — Source: Bloomberg; HSBC（HSBC, p3） Section 05 结论 Conclusion 商品价格回落从全球通胀角度看是好消息，但 供应侧风险仍然很高 ：冲突未了、库存见底、运费保险高企、天气扰动化肥与农产品、AI 相关金属供给紧张。HSBC 的判断是—— 供应侧风险继续在商品市场下方形成托底，价格将保持高位；"没那么糟"，但"超级挤压"仍在继续。 一句话： 地缘降温带来的下跌是"情绪修复"而非"挤压终结"——库存回补需求、运输成本与农产品天气溢价将在供给实质性恢复前持续托底商品价格。 本页由研报阅读工具自动整理生成，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属 HSBC 原报告（2026-11-16，Paul Bloxham & Jamie Culling）。 原文版权归 HSBC 所有。

Issuer of report: HSBC Bank Australia Limited View HSBC Global Investment Research at: https://www.research.hsbc.com This year has brought many twists and turns in commodity markets, with the Middle East conflict playing a key role. The rolling 10-day historical volatility (annualised) of the daily Bloomberg Commodity Spot index averaged 18% year-to-date 2026, up from 12% in 2025. A key development over the past few weeks has been the sharp fall in commodity prices, coinciding with the timing of the US midterm elections. Part of this reflects comments by President Trump and the US administration in recent weeks, which, just prior to the mid-terms were that negotiations with Iran are "going fine" and not "in much of a hurry" (Axios, 1 November 2026) and subsequently suggested a greater willingness to negotiate with Iran, and that further US strikes are “highly unlikely” (Bloomberg, 10 November 2026). These comments were perceived as lowering the likelihood of a renewed US-Israeli offensive. In response, the Bloomberg spot price index has fallen sharply. While commodity prices, on this index, are still up 17% year-to-date, they have now fallen 10% from the mid-September peak, with much of the decline happening in early November. The pullback in commodity prices has been led by lower crude oil prices. The Brent oil benchmark had risen to around USD117/b on 30 October, its highest since April, before pulling back to below USD90/b on 10 November. This unwound most of the geopolitical risk-driven rally from October. Oil prices and, indeed, the broader commodity complex, have been highly sensitive to geopolitical developments this year. For instance, the steep decline in the Bloomberg spot index over the past few weeks echoes that in May and June, when commodity prices fell by 15%, coinciding with the US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding, before relations soured again and commodity prices rebounded. However, these recent developments have not eliminated the risk of a renewed escalation. ◆ Commodity prices have fallen significantly in recent weeks, led by oil, as the Middle East conflict has de-escalated after the US midterms. However, many upside risks to prices remain. First, the Middle East conflict is not over, with attacks continuing and considerable uncertainty about the pathway forward. Second, inventories of many materials have fallen to low levels, leaving less available supply to protect against further disruptions. Third, sharply higher shipping and insurance costs are supporting commodity prices. Fourth, El Niño effects, sharply higher fuel costs and disruptions to fertiliser supply are all still having effects on driving a rise in agricultural product prices. Finally, some of the metals that support the AI boom, including copper, remain in short supply. It all seems less bad, with prices down from recent peaks, but the supply squeeze is not over yet. 16 November 2026 Paul Bloxham Chief Economist, Australia, New Zealand & Global Commodities HSBC Bank Australia Limited paulbloxham@hsbc.com.au +61 2 9255 2635 Jamie Culling Economist, Australia, NZ & Global Commodities HSBC Bank Australia Limited jamie.culling@hsbc.com.au +61 2 9006 5042 Commodity Economic Comment Economics Global Less bad, but the 'super-squeeze' continues 2 Economics ● Global 16 November 2026 Indeed, oil prices have risen again in the past few days – with the brent oil benchmark is back up to around USD95/b, a rise of 7% from the trough. This coincided with comments from President Trump, who noted “we don’t need a deal with Iran” and from Iran’s Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, who noted Iran will not remove “a single atom” of enriched nuclear material (Bloomberg, 13 November 2026). As we see it, risks are still elevated and we see supply-side risks as still supporting commodity prices. The Middle East conflict is not over yet. Further disruptions to commodities supplies are still possible, particularly given the broadening in the conflict beyond the Strait of Hormuz, to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and with the recent Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s infrastructure (see Tensions mounting, 26 October 2026). As our colleague, Kim Fustier, and team, have noted, this may be ‘as good as it gets’ for crude oil markets – while Middle East crude oil supply recovered by more than expected, it is not back to ‘normal’, with strain on logistics and the sharp rise in freight rates too (see Oil markets: Gulf recovery: As good as it gets?, 6 November 2026). For oil, and refined oil products, inventories need to be rebuilt. Inventory drawdowns have been the key factor that has kept global supply chains functioning in the face of the conflict-related disruptions and kept prices from rising to higher extremes. Although last week's figures showed US commercial crude stocks rose by 4.7mb last week, the US's strategic petroleum reserves fell further, down by 2.6mb the same week. A key focus for markets is the question about how much lower oil inventories can fall (see Escalation and the ‘tank bottom’ question, 14 September 2026). Another factor that is likely to support oil prices, is that, at some point, inventories will need to be rebuilt – which will also underpin demand and oil prices. Another key factor keeping prices higher of late, has also been elevated insurance and shipping costs. The cost of crude oil freight from the Middle East Gulf to Asia has risen sharply, now above USD30/b, compared to under USD3/b at the start of the year. So- called ‘dark transits’ and ship-to-ship transfers have also increased the complexity of the journey, which now takes around 23 days, more-than double the optimal time. The supply of other commodities from the Gulf region has also not seen the same improvement as crude. This includes both natural gas, and refined products (see Natural gas inventories in focus, 28 October 2026). European natural gas prices are up 228% year-to- date. Natural gas inventories in Europe rose to their lowest ‘peak fill’ level in more than a decade, missing the target, and posing supply risks heading into the Northern Hemisphere winter months. Our colleagues recently revised their forecasts for European natural gas prices sharply higher, highlighting that 2027’s refills now look challenging (see Gas markets: Raising forecasts: Winter squeeze, summer strain, 12 November 2026). Refined product prices and ‘crack spreads’ have also remained elevated, reflecting significantly tighter markets, with damage to Russia’s diesel infrastructure also adding to the squeeze (see Diesel and refined product prices rise again, 21 August 2026). Inclement weather, the strengthening El Niño, previous fertiliser constraints and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war are also ongoing supply-side challenges for agricultural commodities. While weaker demand and a stronger USD has weighed on US grains export demand, this is not the story elsewhere. India, for instance, is seeing its weakest monsoon in over a decade, hampering the outlook for rice supplies, spurring a further rise in rice prices, which are now up 45% from their trough. Agricultural output has contracted in the Philippines, hamper by typhoons. Recent flooding in Thailand and water shortages in Vietnam have also highlighted the weather risks. A sharp fall in fertiliser demand in Brazil – our colleague Sriharsha Pappu estimates Brazilian fertiliser demand fell by 11% in January–September 2026 – is likely to have a delayed, but outsized, impact on agricultural commodities too. So, while the decline in commodity prices may be better news from a global inflation point of view, risks around the supply-side remain high. We see supply-side risks continuing to place a floor under commodity markets, keeping prices elevated. 3 Economics ● Global 16 November 2026 1. 日 · James Steel（首席贵金属分析师）· 4 页 · AI 中文精读 · 观点归属 HSBC，仅供研究参考 目录 CONTENTS 核心观点 Key Points 数据警报：CPI 与就业数据影响金价 Data Alert 10 月 CPI：关键的测试 A Close Scrutiny 策略观点：贵金属配置 Strategy View 关键点位与近期报告 Key Levels KEY POINTS 核心观点 CPI 与非农是金价最有影响力的宏观数据 ：本报告图示过去 12 个月度 CPI 公布值相对预期的偏差及金价其后 15 个交易日的反应；历史公布大多接近预期。 2025 年末–2026 年初 ：通胀缓和（但仍高）伴随金价走高，因其支持降息论据；对伊朗打击后通胀抬头+能源价格高企令货币政策持续收紧，金价随之转弱。 11 月 10 日公布的 10 月 CPI 备受关注 ：此前一周非农异常强劲。HSBC 美国经济学家 Ryan Wang 预测环比 +0.2% （略低于预期）；因去年政府停摆，本次无同比数据。 情形推演 ：CPI 高于预期→黄金涨势至少遭遇温和逆风；低于预期→有助维持涨势。 策略观点 ：预计 FOMC 2027 年加息幅度将 不及市场预期 ，对黄金构成长期支撑；白银仍易受高科技需求疲弱冲击——保留选择性白银敞口；PGM 仅在能容忍催化剂滞后与高波动的前提下逐步建仓；白色金属走势仍依赖黄金。 关键点位 ：黄金现价 $4,110/oz （阻力 $4,193 / $4,303 / $4,444，200 日均线 $4,457.8，支撑 $4,029 / $4,000 / $3,869）；白银现价 $52.86/oz （阻力 $54.77 / $56.36 / $58.60，200 日均线 $68.69，支撑 $52.00 / $50.90 / $48.53）。 Section 01 数据警报：CPI 与就业数据影响金价 Data Alert: CPI and Jobs Data Can Influence Gold 美国月度非农就业（NFP）与 CPI 是对黄金最具影响力的数据点。本报告图表展示了最近 12 次 CPI 公布值相对预期的偏差，以及金价在其后 15 个交易日的表现。总体看，公布值大多贴近预期。 通胀缓和期（2025 年末–2026 年初） ：通胀回落（但绝对水平仍高）伴随金价上涨，因为它们强化了降息论据。 通胀再起（伊朗遭袭后） ：通胀升级叠加油价走高，货币政策为压制持续性通胀压力而收紧，触发金价走弱。 Fig 1 · 金价对美国 CPI 公布的反应：近 12 次 CPI 实际值 vs 预期（左轴）及公布后 15 日金价表现（右轴） | Gold reaction to US CPI releases — Source: LSEG Datastream, HSBC Section 02 10 月 CPI：关键的测试 The 10 November CPI: A Close Scrutiny 定于 11 月 10 日公布的 10 月 CPI 可能比以往更受密切审视——因为它紧随上周晚些时候 异常强劲的就业数据 之后。HSBC 美国经济学家 Ryan Wang 预测 10 月 CPI 环比增长 +0.2% ，略低于市场预期；由于去年政府停摆的影响，本次发布 没有同比数据 。 情形推演： 若 CPI 高于预期，黄金涨势将至少遭遇温和逆风；若低于预期，则有助于维持涨势。 Section 03 策略观点：贵金属配置 Strategy View: Precious Metals Positioning 黄金 ：我们预计 FOMC 2027 年加息幅度将不及当前市场预期——这对黄金构成 更长期的支撑 。 白银 ：仍易受高科技（光伏/电子）需求疲弱的影响；建议 保留选择性的白银敞口 。 PGM（铂族金属） ：仅在投资者能够容忍催化剂滞后（delayed catalysts）与更高波动的情况下， 逐步建仓 。 白色金属整体 ：走势仍高度依赖黄金的动向。 Section 04 关键点位与近期报告 Key Levels and Recent View HSBC Global Investment Research at: https://www.research.hsbc.com ◆ Data alert: High US CPI following recent strong jobs data could present headwinds to gold; weak data may aid bullion CPI and jobs data can influence gold The US monthly non-farm payroll and Consumer Price Index releases are among the most influential data points for gold. Our chart illustrates the last 12 monthly CPI releases compared to expectations, as well as gold’s reaction for the following 15 days. The releases have generally been close to expectations. Moderating (but still high) inflation towards the end of 2025 and early 2026 were accompanied by higher gold, as they supported the argument for rate cuts. Escalating inflation in the aftermath of strikes on Iran and higher energy prices triggered gold weakness as monetary policy tightened in response to persistent inflationary pressures. The October CPI due on 10 November may be even more closely scrutinized than usual, coming after exceptionally strong jobs data late last week. Ryan Wang, HSBC’s US economist, forecasts m-o-m growth at 0.2%, slightly below expectations. There is no annualized figure due to the government shutdown last year. If the CPI comes in above expectations, we would except the gold rally to run into at least modest headwinds. A low release could help maintain the rally. Gold reaction to US CPI releases Source: LSEG Datastream, HSBC Strategy view: Our expectation that the FOMC will fall short of current market expectations of rate hikes in 2027 is longer-term gold supportive. Silver remains vulnerable to high-tech demand weakness. Retain selective silver exposure and build PGM positions gradually only where investors can tolerate delayed catalysts and higher volatility. The white metals also remain dependent on gold moves. reports.stext: 中国金属活动追踪：极紧的实货铜市对冲AI/股市风险 J.P. MORGAN · 中国金属 · 周度追踪 中国金属活动追踪：极紧的实货铜市对冲AI/股市风险，10日钢产量环比+8% China Metals Activity Tracker: Very tight China physical copper market mitigates AI/equity market risks; latest 10-day China steel output +8% vs previous 10 days 机构： J.P. Morgan（Europe Equity Research） | 日期： 2026-11-16（数据截至 11月13日当周） | 页数： 14 | 团队： Dominic O'Kane（欧洲金属与钢铁）、Patrick Jones、Gregory Shearer（全球商品研究）、Lyndon Fagan、Bill Peterson 本页为第三方研报的中文精读摘要，仅供研究参考，不构成投资建议；全部观点与数据归属原机构（J.P. Morgan）。 目录 Contents 核心观点 KEY POINTS 铜：显性库存仅47kt，洋山溢价飙破$250/t 铝：库存降至十年来同期最低 锌：去库强于季节性 钢铁：10日产量环比+8%，钢厂仍亏损 铁矿石：价格跌破$90/t，港口库存156Mt 宏观流动性与结论 Key Points 核心观点 KEY POINTS 基本金属继续去库： 上周铝 -32kt （连续两周约32kt去库）与锌 -4kt 的去库强于季节性；铜 -11kt 大致符合季节性。 铝库存十年最低： 中国铝显性库存自4月以来累计去化约 1Mt ，降至约 490kt ，为 十年来同期最低 。 实货铜极紧： 中国铜显性库存仅约 47-50kt ；LME 铜回落至约 $13,400/t ，但洋山铜溢价一个月内飙升逾 200% 至 >$250/t ——实货紧张为价格提供强支撑。 JPM 商品研究观点： 中国的实货紧张 缓解了滑向 ~$11,000/t 的下行风险 （此前两周科技/AI 股抛售带动金属回调）；同时需警惕更鹰派的美联储与更强的美元。 钢铁产量回升： 11月10日止10天中国日均粗钢产量年化 887Mt ，同比 +3% 、较前一旬 +8% ；官方产量仍运行于5年区间底部。 铁矿走弱： 铁矿价格周五跌破 $90/t ；澳中运费一周 -$3/t（FOB 约 $77/t），巴西-中国运费仅降 $0.25/t（FOB $54/t，年内低位）。 宏观偏弱、政策发力： 10月新增人民币贷款 录得有记录以来首次10月负增长 ；央行启动一系列稳市场措施，包括创纪录的 1,500亿元 公开市场国债买入。 Section 01 铜：显性库存仅47kt，洋山溢价飙破$250/t Copper: visible stocks ~47kt, Yangshan premium >$250/t 截至11月13日当周，中国铜显性库存（SHFE+保税）再去库约 11kt，总量降至 47kt ——远低于5年均值（同期约100-200kt），处于2017年有数据以来的极端低位。LME 铜价两周来受科技/AI 抛售拖累回落至约 $13,400/t ，但极低的国内可取库存使实货买盘必须支付更高溢价： 洋山铜溢价过去一个月上涨逾 200% 至 >$250/t ，与 LME 价格走势罕见背离，是实货紧张的最直接信号。 要点： JPM 商品研究认为，中国实货紧张"缓解了滑向 ~$11,000/t 的下行风险"；若 AI/股市抛售延续，价格波动将被低库存放大而非单边下行。 图 1 · 中国铜显性库存周度变化（SHFE+保税，kt，按春节后周数）：上周-11kt，符合季节性 | Figure 3: Weekly change in China visible copper inventory — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities（原文 p3） 图 2 · 中国铜显性库存总量（kt）：47kt，远低于5年区间 | Figure 4: Total China visible copper inventory, week ended 13 Nov'26 — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities（原文 p3） 图 3 · 洋山铜溢价 vs LME 现货铜（$/t）：溢价一个月飙升逾200%至>$250/t | Figure 9: China Yangshan Copper Premium vs LME Copper Spot — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p5） 图 4 · 中国铜显性库存长期走势（SHFE+保税，kt，2017年以来）：当前为极端低位 | Figure 17: Chinese visible copper inventory, week ended 13 Nov — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities（原文 p7） Section 02 铝：库存降至十年来同期最低 Aluminium: lowest seasonal inventory in a decade 铝连续两周录得约 32kt 的去库，强于季节性。中国铝显性库存（SHFE+区域仓库）自4月峰值以来累计去化约 1Mt ，降至 ~490kt ，为 十年来同期最低水平 。去库持续 + 库存绝对水平极低，意味着国内铝实货市场同样趋紧。 图 5 · 中国铝显性库存周度变化（kt）：连续两周约-32kt去库，强于季节性 | Figure 5: Weekly change in China visible aluminium inventory — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities（原文 p3） 图 6 · 中国铝显性库存总量（kt）：489kt，五年来最低季节性水平 | Figure 6: Total China visible aluminium inventory, week ended 13 Nov'26 — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities（原文 p4） Section 03 锌：去库强于季节性 Zinc: destocking stronger vs seasonal trend 锌上周去库 4kt ，同样强于季节性；总库存 179kt 仍是2022年以来同期最高，但已较年内峰值明显回落。锌是三个基本金属中库存相对最充裕的品种，紧张程度排序大致为：铜 ≫ 铝 > 锌。 图 7 · 中国锌显性库存总量（kt）：179kt，2022年以来同期最高但显著低于年内峰值 | Figure 8: Total China visible zinc inventory, week ended 13 Nov'26 — Source: SHFE, CRU, SMM, J.P. Morgan Commodities Research（原文 p4） Section 04 钢铁：10日产量环比+8%，钢厂仍亏损 Steel: 10-day output +8% vs prior period, margins loss-making 11月10日止10天，中国日均粗钢产量年化 887Mt ，同比 +3% 、较10月31日止前一旬 +8% ——供应端边际抬升，但官方产量仍运行在5年区间底部。需求侧宏观信号偏弱（10月出口自9月高点回落、新增贷款创纪录10月负增长），钢厂利润延续亏损：螺纹与热卷 margin 仍为负值、近几周随煤价与矿价企稳而保持稳定。钢材总库存 27.7Mt ，环比 -1%、同比 -2%。 图 8 · 中国粗钢产量（kt，日度）：11月10日止10天年化887Mt，+3% YoY | Figure 1: China steel production 10 days to 10 Nov — Source: CISA, Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p1） 图 9 · 中国钢厂利润（元/吨）：螺纹与热卷利润仍处亏损区间 | Figure 11: China steel mill margins remain loss-making — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P., J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p5） 图 10 · 中国钢材库存（Mt）：27.7Mt，环比-1%、同比-2% | Figure 12: China steel inventory at 27.7Mt week ending 13 Nov — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates, Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p6） Section 05 铁矿石：价格跌破$90/t，港口库存156Mt Iron ore: price <$90/t, port stocks ~156Mt 铁矿石价格上周五跌破 $90/t ，主因运费走弱：澳-中运费一周下跌 $3/t ，澳大利亚 62% FOB 约 $77/t ；巴西-中国运费仅降 $0.25/t，巴西 62% FOB $54/t ，续创年内低位。供应端：9月全球铁矿发运环比 -3%、同比 -7% （澳大利亚 -2% MoM / +4% YoY，巴西 -9% MoM / -8% YoY）。中国港口库存约 156Mt ，两周累库 +4Mt，符合季节性累库趋势。 图 11 · 62% 铁矿价格：CFR 与澳/巴西 FOB（$/t）：CFR跌破$90/t，巴西FOB $54/t 年内低位 | Figure 2: Australia FOB Iron Ore price stable whilst Brazil FOB down — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates, Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p2） 图 12 · 中国港口铁矿石库存（Mt）：约156Mt，两周+4Mt、符合季节性 | Figure 13: Iron Ore inventory at China ports ~156Mt — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates, Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p6） Section 06 宏观流动性与结论 Macro liquidity & conclusions 宏观面：10月新增人民币贷款低于预期，出现 有记录以来首次10月负增长 ；央行近期启动一系列市场稳定措施，包括通过公开市场国债买入注入创纪录的 1,500亿元 。10月出口自9月高位回落。 结论： 本周核心矛盾是"金融属性走弱 vs 实货属性极紧"——AI/股市抛售与美元走强压制价格（LME 铜 ~$13,400/t），但铜 47kt、铝 490kt 的极端低库存与 >$250/t 的洋山溢价构成强实货支撑，中国紧张缓解了滑向 ~$11,000/t 的尾部风险。后续关注：美联储路径、国内政策加码力度与冬储节奏。 仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议，观点归属原机构。原文版权归 J.P. Morgan 所有，本页为其中文精读笔记。

Morgan · 栏目 Global Markets Strategy · 报告日期 2026-11-24 · 原文 50 页 · AI 中文精读 · 观点归属 J.P. Morgan 核心主题：Unwind incomplete in base metals, closer to a bottom in precious（基本金属解仓未完，贵金属渐近底部） 本文为对原报告的中文摘编与图表引用，仅供研究参考，不构成投资建议；全部观点与数据归属 J.P. Morgan Global Commodities Research / Global FX Strategy。 目录 Contents 核心观点与价格预测一览 Key Takeaways 基本金属总览 Base Metals Summary 贵金属总览 Precious Metals Summary 铜 Copper：错位溢价的解仓 Dislocation unwind 铝 Aluminum：成本曲线的引力 Gravity of cost curve 镍 Nickel：库存重压下的区间震荡 Rangebound 锌 Zinc：精矿紧张支撑 2027 Tight concentrate 金与银 Gold & Silver：能源与美联储主导 Energy & the Fed 铂与钯 Platinum & Palladium：ETF 决定分化 ETF the differentiator 贵金属衍生品 2027 展望 Derivatives 价格预测总表 Price Forecasts Key Takeaways · 核心观点 基本金属解仓未完，贵金属渐近底部 Unwind incomplete in base metals, closer to a bottom in precious 基本金属： 一轮 空头化解仓（bearish unwind） 正在基本金属中展开并将延续至 1H27——矿供受限的背景下，铜价仍将走向 $11,000/mt ：2027 年美国 flips to destocking（转向去库存），终于给除美国平衡松绑，更充分地解开因美国超额进口/囤积而累积的"错位溢价"。铜价下行意味着铝价下沉时阻力更小，成本曲线与印尼主导的过剩（2028 年过剩 >2 mmt）将把铝拉向 $2,500/mt （YE27）。锌虽有铜的拖累，精矿紧张仍支撑 2027 均价约 $3,400/mt ；镍独走自身周期，高库存令价格 2027/28 在 $15,500–$16,500/mt 区间贴着成本支撑磨底。 贵金属： 能源、通胀与美联储（Fed）今年阻断了贵金属牛市。更低原油价格 + 美联储自 1Q27 起暂停（1H28 两次降息）将最终驱动金价于 4Q27 回升至 $4,500/oz ，白银夺回 mid-$50s ；2H27 铂金投资需求增强将令市场转向短缺，强化金带动的反弹至 $1,800/oz ；钯金受过剩压制，2027 年围绕 $1,000–$1,200/oz 。 贵金属波动率： 金价波动率在上周冲高后应开始正常化，但只是部分——今年实现波动异常强势或将延续。倾向通过 Delta 对冲的 比率看跌价差（ratio put spreads） fade 重新变贵的下行偏斜，同时对仍脆弱的现货环境保持谨慎；金价深调后，通过 卖出低 XAU/USD–EUR/USD 相关性的双数字期权（dual digitals） 大幅折价保留黄金上行敞口。 品种 4Q26F 2026 均值 2027 均值 2028 均值 方向 铜 LME cash 13,500 13,444 11,750 11,625 ▼ 走向 $11,000，1H27 后企稳（2027 较 10 Morgan（原文 Figure 59 · p38） 上周抛售中断了此前的正常化： 实现波动骤升、短端隐含大幅重定价、曲线倒挂，smile 重新摆向下行保护（risk reversal 再度买 put）。但波动响应不及 1 月冲击——更像是既有高位机制内的 又一次冲击 ，而非新机制的开启。展望：随着冲击溢价消退，前端波动将从当前水平回撤，但 1Q27 只是 部分正常化 ——仓位在抛售前已处 YTD 低位、gamma 全年韧性十足、反复的实现冲击令隐含无法持续回到 2026 年前的低位机制；倒挂曲线将趋平，而非前端快速回落。 下行偏斜比 ATM 更脆弱 ：若现货企稳，put 的重新富贵最难维持；但方向性不明 ≠ 低波动——黄金已连续一年多保持高波动资产属性。 交易观点 Trade ideas 1 · Fade 下行偏斜（Delta 对冲比率价差）： 3M 25D put/ATM vol 比率急升、逼近上半年峰值（图 20），下行保护重新富贵。JPM 偏好 Delta 对冲的 3M ATM/25D 1×1.5 ratio put spread @$90.20 （mid $88.20，spot ref 3670）——用低行权 put 的昂贵融资贴近现价的下行凸性，无需直白做空 ATM vol。注意该结构留下裸露的下行尾部； 卖 3M XAU/USD 3250 put one-touch @37.5% （mid 33%）在流动性允许时是封顶损失的替代。 2 · 折价买入黄金上行（双数字期权）： 金价已回吐至 2025 年 9 月水平（今年一度 >5,000）；分析师基准情形仅温和上行，但深调让"廉价参与更强反弹"变得有吸引力。卖出 low-40s 的 XAU/USD–EUR/USD 相关性可对独立黄金上行大幅折价——买入 3M 双数字 [XAU/USD 收盘 +4% 且 EUR/USD <1.09] @14.3% （mid 10.7%，spot refs 3670 / 1.0890，图 21），等价结构约 7.3% mid、显著低于更便宜的单边数字期权，同时契合 JPM 策略师的看空 EUR 观点。 图 20 · XAU 3M 25D put / ATM vol 比率 | Figure 64: XAU OTM puts are approaching the peak levels from the 1H — 比率逼近上半年高点，下行偏斜富贵。 Source: J.P. Morgan（原文 Figure 64 · p43） 图 21 · 3M XAU/USD Call vs 美元交叉盘 Dual Digitals 的折价比较 | Figure 65: Selling low XAU/EUR correlation steeply discounts gold topside exposure — XAU/USD+EUR/USD 组合在同类跨资产组合中折价居前。 Source: J.P. Morgan（原文 Figure 65 · p44） 结论： 2027 年的基准是"仍处高位机制内的正常化"，而非回归早年的低位波动。倾向 fade 重新变贵的下行偏斜（比率价差 / one-touch），同时用低相关的双数字期权廉价保留黄金上行杠杆。 Section 10 · 价格预测总表 JPM 金属价格预测（季度与年度均值） JPM metals price forecasts — Quarterly and annual averages 基本金属为 LME cash（US$/mt），贵金属为 spot（US$/oz）。A=实际，其余为 JPM 预测（2026-11-24 更新）。 品种 1Q26A 2Q26A 3Q26A 4Q26F 1Q27 2Q27 3Q27 4Q27 1Q28 2Q28 3Q28 4Q28 2025 2026 2027 2028 铝 3,198 3,562 3,229 3,115 2,775 2,700 2,600 2,500 2,500 2,450 2,400 2,375 2,631 3,276 2,644 2,431 铜 12,824 13,352 14,100 13,500 11,750 11,250 11,750 12,250 12,000 11,750 11,500 11,250 9,947 13,444 11,750 11,625 镍 17,338 18,090 16,562 15,500 16,500 16,000 15,700 16,000 16,200 16,100 16,000 15,600 15,164 16,872 16,050 15,975 锌 3,237 3,464 3,825 3,750 3,450 3,360 3,450 3,400 3,400 3,350 3,300 3,200 2,867 3,569 3,415 3,313 黄金 4,873 4,508 4,300 3,900 3,750 3,950 4,200 4,500 4,800 5,000 5,150 5,300 3,440 4,395 4,100 5,063 白银 83.7 73.1 62.5 50.4 45.5 48.5 52.0 56.0 60.0 62.0 64.0 65.0 40.1 67.4 50.5 62.8 铂金 2,204 1,916 1,700 1,490 1,440 1,600 1,700 1,800 2,000 2,050 2,100 2,130 1,282 1,828 1,635 2,070 钯金 1,706 1,409 1,300 1,000 1,000 1,100 1,150 1,200 1,250 1,200 1,150 1,200 1,151 1,354 1,113 1,200 路径速读： 铜 1Q27 见底 $11,750 后温和回稳；铝单边下行至 2028；镍全年横盘；锌前高后低；金 1Q27 $3,750 触底后逐季上行、2028 年创新高；银随金但 2H27 起弹性更大；铂 2H27 起加速；钯低位徘徊。 免责声明：本文为 J.P. reports.stext: 铜全球供应追踪：三季度偏弱，2027-28 增长在途 J.P. MORGAN · 铜 · 供应追踪 铜全球供应追踪：三季度偏弱，2027-28 增长在途 Global Supply Tracker: Sep'Qtr soft ahead of strong supply growth into 2027 & 2028 机构： J.P. Morgan（Asia Pacific Equity Research） | 日期： 2026-11-10 | 页数： 12 | 团队： Lyndon Fagan（澳洲金属与矿业主管）、Jonathon Sharp、Branko Skocic、Zane Guo、Gregory Shearer（基础金属与贵金属策略主管）等 本页为第三方研报的中文精读摘要，仅供研究参考，不构成投资建议；全部观点与数据归属原机构（J.P. Morgan / Morgan Stanley）。 目录 Contents 核心观点 KEY POINTS 数据集与三季度回顾 2026 与 2027 增减 TOP5 头部矿山与国别结构 全球供需平衡表 覆盖公司估值一览 Key Points 核心观点 KEY POINTS 数据集覆盖广： J.P. Morgan 全球金属与采矿团队覆盖 25 家 上市铜矿公司、 100+ 座矿山 、 27 个国家 ，约占 全球铜供应的 54% ；本协作笔记汇总各公司季报产量与预测。 三季度偏弱： 9 月季度产量环比 -1.3%（-43kt） ，较 2025 年 6 月季度高点低约 180kt ；团队预计 12 月季度将 强力反弹约 +150kt ，智利从近期降雨影响中恢复。 2027-28 供应增长强劲： 上市矿企口径 2026 年产量 -261kt ，2027 年 +987kt ，2028 年再 +1,089kt （2026 年全球矿山供应约 24.3Mt）。 增量龙头： 2027 年 Grasberg +171kt 最大、Collahuasi +151kt 次之；2028 年增长由 Cobre Panama 驱动（假设 2027 年年中重启）。 全球供需（Greg Shearer 模型）： 2027/2028 年矿山供应增长 1.43Mt / 1.57Mt （2026 年仅 +530kt）；上市矿企数据集约占 2027 年全球供应增长的 70% 。 小幅过剩格局： 平衡表显示 2026E +382kt 、2027F 收窄至 +92kt 、2028F 走阔至 +254kt ；铜价风险与 关税结果 挂钩。 评级倾向： 澳洲 OW BHP / Rio Tinto / Glencore / Sandfire / Capstone（Capstone 上行空间 73%）；EMEA OW Antofagasta（+27%）、UW Lundin Mining。 Section 01 数据集与三季度回顾 Dataset & Sep'Qtr review 本报告为 J.P. Morgan 首份 全球铜供应追踪（Global Supply Tracker） 协作笔记：把全球团队覆盖的上市矿企季报产量数据汇总为单一数据库，用于跟踪关键趋势。覆盖组合产量约占全球矿山供应的 54%，因此其增减节奏对全球供应具有较强代表性。 9 月季度回顾： 合计产量环比下降 1.3%（约 -43kt），距 2025 年 6 月季度高点仍低约 180kt，主因智利降雨扰动与部分矿山品位下降。团队预计 12 月季度环比反弹约 +150kt ，其中智利在降雨影响消退后恢复最为明显。 年度路径： 2026 年是减产年（-261kt），但数据库显示 2027 年逐季环比抬升、2028 年延续增长——上市矿企产量 2027 年 +987kt、2028 年 +1,089kt。 图 1 · 覆盖矿企季度铜产量（kt）：2026 蓝色、2027 黄色、2028 绿色逐季抬升 | Figure 1: Quarterly copper production (kt): 100+ mines under global JPM equity coverage — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p1） 图 2 · 上市矿企年度产量与同比变化：2026 -261kt → 2027 +987kt → 2028 +1,089kt | Figure 2: Annual copper production and YoY change (~54% of world supply) — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p2） Section 02 2026 与 2027 增减 TOP5 Top 5 changes in 2026 & 2027 分矿山看增减贡献： 2026 年 最大增量来自 Julong（巨龙铜矿，+106kt）、Antamina（+85kt）、Oyu Tolgoi（+65kt）；最大拖累是 Escondida（-171kt）、Kamoa-Kakula（-110kt）、Grasberg（-87kt）。 2027 年 格局切换：Grasberg（+171kt）与 Collahuasi（+151kt）领涨，Zhunuo（+65kt）、Oyu Tolgoi（+61kt）、Cobre Panama（+60kt，假设年中重启）跟进；减量集中在 Escondida（-148kt）、Antamina（-60kt）、Olympic Dam（-32kt）。 图 3 · 2026 同比增幅 TOP5：Julong +106kt、Antamina +85kt、Oyu Tolgoi +65kt | Figure 3: 2026 YoY top 5 copper supply increases — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p2） 图 4 · 2026 同比降幅 TOP5：Escondida -171kt、Kamoa-Kakula -110kt、Grasberg -87kt | Figure 4: 2026 YoY top 5 copper supply decreases — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p2） 图 5 · 2027 同比增幅 TOP5：Grasberg +171kt、Collahuasi +151kt、Zhunuo +65kt | Figure 5: 2027 YoY top 5 copper supply increases — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p2） 图 6 · 2027 同比降幅 TOP5：Escondida -148kt、Antamina -60kt、Olympic Dam -32kt | Figure 6: 2027 YoY top 5 copper supply decreases — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p2） Section 03 头部矿山与国别结构 Top mines & country mix 前十大矿山中， Escondida 从 2026 年 1,136kt 降至 2028 年 951kt（品位下滑），而 Grasberg （374kt→681kt）、 Collahuasi （396kt→582kt）、Oyu Tolgoi（410kt→498kt）在 2028 年显著放量，TFM（525kt→575kt）稳步爬坡。 国别结构上，覆盖矿企产量集中于 智利（25%） 、 秘鲁（16%） 与 刚果（金）（12%） ，其后为美国、中国（各 7%），赞比亚、墨西哥、蒙古各 4%，印尼、澳大利亚各 3%。 图 7 · 前十大矿山 2026 vs 2028 产量（kt）：Grasberg、Collahuasi 放量，Escondida 回落 | Figure 7: Top 10 mines in covered equities: 2026 vs 2028 — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p3） 图 8 · 覆盖矿企产量国别分布：智利 25%、秘鲁 16%、刚果（金）12% | Figure 9: Copper Production by Country - listed miners — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p4） Section 04 全球供需平衡表 Global S/D balance JPM 大宗商品研究（Greg Shearer 团队）全球供需平衡表：矿山产量 2026E 24,287kt → 2027F 25,717kt → 2028F 27,285kt；精炼铜用量 27,481kt → 28,315kt → 29,194kt。 全球平衡（经政府收售调整后）2026E +382kt、2027F +92kt、2028F +254kt ——2027 年过剩收窄至接近平衡，2028 年重新走阔。 结论： 矿端增长集中兑现于 2027-28 年（+1.43Mt / +1.57Mt），全球维持小幅过剩、但 2027F 趋紧；铜价的主要下行风险来自美国关税政策路径的不确定性，而非矿端短缺。 图 9 · JPM 全球铜供需平衡表（千吨）：2026E +382kt / 2027F +92kt / 2028F +254kt | Figure 8: JPM Commodities Research copper supply and demand balance by region — Source: J.P. Morgan Global Commodity Research（原文 p3） Section 05 覆盖公司估值一览 Coverage valuation snapshot 覆盖组合估值（Table 1，2026-11-10）：澳洲方面 BHP（OW，目标价 A$72，上行 20%）、Rio Tinto（OW，+38%）、Glencore（OW，+35%）、Capstone（OW，+73%）、Sandfire（OW，+17%）、South32（Neutral）；EMEA 方面 Antofagasta（OW，+27%）、Glencore LN（OW，+42%）、Anglo American（Neutral）、First Quantum（Neutral）、Lundin Mining（UW）、KGHM（Neutral）。组合 2027E 平均 EV/EBITDA 约 6.3x、股息率约 2.8%。 仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议，观点归属原机构。原文版权归 J.P. Morgan / Morgan Stanley 所有，本页为其中文精读笔记。

reports.stext: 铜仪表盘：九成显性库存困于美国，实货紧张与情绪转弱并存 J.P. MORGAN · 铜 · 仪表盘 铜仪表盘：九成显性库存困于美国，实货紧张与情绪转弱并存 Copper Dashboard: Physical tightness persists with 90% of visible inventories in the US, but sentiment weakens 机构： J.P. Morgan（Global Equity Research） | 日期： 2026-11-11 | 页数： 32 | 团队： Lyndon Fagan（澳洲金属与矿业主管）、Gregory Shearer（基础与贵金属策略）、Patrick Jones（EMEA）等 | 行业观点： 覆盖个股 OW CSC/BHP/RIO/GLC/SFR、FCX、Antofagasta；UW Lundin 本页为第三方研报的中文精读摘要，仅供研究参考，不构成投资建议；全部观点与数据归属原机构（J.P. Morgan / Morgan Stanley）。 目录 Contents 核心观点 KEY POINTS 库存：总量新高、结构极化 价差与套息交易逆转 情绪与宏观：投机退潮、PMI 仍强 冶炼与现货溢价 远期曲线与供应跟踪 Key Points 核心观点 KEY POINTS 价格区间震荡： LME 铜近三个月徘徊于 ~$14,000-14,800/t（$6.35-6.70/lb） ；美国关税威胁未散，市场情绪转向"谨慎的不确定性"（LME 周反馈）。 美国吸铜近九成： 全球显性库存升至 1.1Mt （8 月中 975kt），其中 约 90% 位于美国 ；SHFE+中国保税库存降至仅 60kt （3 月底 +400kt）——关税墙外可用库存极低。 实货紧张显性化： 中国阴极铜溢价大幅飙升（~$215/t），铜精矿 TC 深度负值（约 -$230/t）；冶炼检修、废铜供应受限与低社会库存共同推高溢价、托底价格。 供需双弱： 1-8 月全球铜产量同比 -1.3% （智利 9 月矿产同比 -15%），全球表观需求同比亦约 -2% 。 情绪转弱： LME 投机净多持仓大幅回落，远期曲线明年各月均低于现货；全球/美国 PMI 仍强（52.6 / 54.9），AI 资本开支放缓担忧尚未在数据中体现。 套息交易逆转： COMEX-LME 溢价基本消失，美国继续累库的经济性不复存在（溢价 +$1,000/t 时净收益 +$650/t；无溢价 -$350/t）；但已融资头寸不会立即去库。 风险点位： 持续跌破 ~$13,850/t 将打开进一步下行空间；中期更大风险是关税"只闻楼梯响"——滞留美国的铜回流将缓解中国短缺、侵蚀价格支撑。 个股观点： 澳洲 OW CSC / BHP / RIO / GLC / SFR；美国 OW FCX；EMEA OW Antofagasta、UW Lundin Mining。 Section 01 库存：总量新高、结构极化 Inventories: 1.1Mt global, ~90% in the US 库存是本期的核心矛盾。总量上，全球显性库存（LME+COMEX+中国）自 8 月中的 975kt 回升至 1.1Mt ，全部增量来自美国—— 约 90% 的交易所库存已在美国 ，处于"关税墙"之内。关税墙外市场可实时取用的库存（LME 除美国 on-warrant + SHFE + 中国保税）已降至约 350kt 低位，其中中国两地合计仅 60kt （3 月底尚有 +400kt），为多年极端低位。 库存天数同样显著低于 2014 年以来均值；季节性图上 2026 年库存水平高于过去五年，但增量几乎全部"锁"在美国。LME 取消仓单自 8 月以来回落，暗示关税墙外需求边际走弱。 图 1 · 全球铜库存 vs LME 价格：显性库存回升至 1.1Mt | Figure 4: Global copper inventory vs price — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p5） 图 2 · 全球仓库库存季节性（LME+COMEX+中国）：2026 年（红线）高于往年同期 | Figure 5: Global copper warehouse inventory seasonality (kt) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p5） 图 3 · 美国占全球交易所库存比重升至约 90% | Figure 7: Exchange inventory located in the US — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p6） 图 4 · 关税墙外可用库存（LME 除美国 on-warrant + 中国 SHFE/保税）降至低位 | Figure 8: LME inventory on warrant ex US + China inventory (kt) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p6） Section 02 价差与套息交易逆转 Arbitrage & the carry trade unwind 过去一年美国累库由 套息交易（carry trade） 驱动：贸易商买现货运往美国、同时卖出 3-12 个月 COMEX 期货，锁定足以覆盖融资/仓储/运费的溢价。如今 COMEX 对 LME 溢价已基本消失（回落至物流成本带内）， 继续向美国运铜的经济性不复存在 ；但存量头寸仍处于融资与对冲状态，显性去库需等待境外出现更优回报（持续的 LME 溢价或中国/欧洲现货溢价走强）。 情景（Table 3） COMEX 溢价 · 累库 无溢价 · 中性 LME 溢价 · 去库 LME / COMEX 价格 $13,000 / $14,000 $13,000 / $13,000 $13,200 / $13,000 COMEX-LME 价差 +$1,000/t $0/t -$200/t 运费+仓储+融资 ($350/t) ($350/t) ($350/t) 净经济性 +$650/t -$350/t -$550/t 行为 / 后果 把铜运往美国 · 抽紧墙外市场 持有现有库存 铜回流全球市场 图 5 · COMEX 对 LME 溢价已回落至物流成本带内 | Figure 12: Comex copper price premium to LME copper price — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p7） 图 6 · 套息交易三情景：无溢价时净经济性 -$350/t，继续累库停滞 | Table 3: Copper carry trade examples — Source: J.P. Morgan estimates（原文 p8） Section 03 情绪与宏观：投机退潮、PMI 仍强 Sentiment vs macro 情绪面明显转弱： LME 投机净多持仓自高位大幅回落，接近 5 年均值下方；与之相对，宏观面并不差——全球/美国 PMI 仍处扩张区间（ 52.6 / 54.9 ），"AI 交易动摇"的担忧尚未在实体数据中体现。中期看，超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）资本开支的加速上行仍是铜需求的潜在重要驱动，数据中心、电力设备与新能源用铜占比持续抬升。 图 7 · LME 投机净持仓大幅回落至 5 年均值附近 | Figure 13: LME net speculative positioning — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p9） 图 8 · 铜价 vs 美国 PMI：制造业 PMI 54.9 仍处扩张区间 | Figure 14: Copper price vs US PMI — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p9） 图 9 · 超大规模云厂商季度资本开支 vs 铜价 | Figure 15: Hyperscaler capex vs copper price — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p9） Section 04 冶炼与现货溢价 TC/RC & China cathode premium 矿端与冶炼端信号分化： 铜精矿 TC 已跌至约 -$230/t 的深度负值区间（零基线远下方），表明精矿市场极度紧张、冶炼厂议价能力薄弱；同期 中国阴极铜溢价飙升至 ~$215/t ，为现货紧张的直接证据——冶炼检修、废铜供应受限与低社会库存共同放大了溢价弹性，短期内对铜价形成支撑。 图 10 · 铜精矿 TC 跌至约 -$230/t 的深度负值 | Figure 20: Copper smelter treatment charge ($/t) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p11） 图 11 · 中国阴极铜溢价飙升至 ~$215/t | Figure 21: China cathode premium ($/t) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p11） Section 05 远期曲线与供应跟踪 Forward curve & supply tracking 远期曲线： LME 铜明年各月期限价格均低于现货（远期贴水），与情绪转弱一致。供应端， 智利 月度矿产 12 个月移动平均同比已滑落至约 -9%（9 月单月同比 -15%），秘鲁相对平稳； 中国 精炼铜产量维持约 15Mtpa 年化高位，但精炼需求同比已转负（约 -0.5%），表观需求走弱与矿端减产并存。 结论： 实货紧张（中国极低库存+溢价飙升+TC 深负）与投资情绪疲弱并存，短期价格有支撑；但技术面跌破 ~$13,850/t 将打开下行空间，中期最大风险是美国关税迟迟不落地引发库存回流。 图 12 · LME 铜远期曲线：明年各月均低于现货 | Figure 22: LME copper price forward curve ($/lb) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p12） 图 13 · 智利 vs 秘鲁矿产同比（12mma）：智利 9 月同比 -15% | Figure 27: Chile vs. Peru monthly copper production — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p14） 图 14 · 中国精炼铜需求同比转负（~-0.5%）| Figure 30: China refined copper demand, YoY change — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p16） 图 15 · 中国精炼铜产量维持约 15Mtpa 年化高位 | Figure 32: China refined copper production (Mtpa rate) — Source: Bloomberg Finance L.P.（原文 p16） 仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议，观点归属原机构。原文版权归 J.P.
