reports.ftext: M Idea Commodity Matters | Europe Thermal Coal: Still Too Early to Turn Bearish Thermal coal has been caught up in the post-midterms energy sell-off, but the drivers that supported prices this year remain. Tight Indonesian supply, expensive LNG and Indian restocking should support prices into 1Q27 (MSe $155/t) before China's supply push and lower gas prices push coal to $135/t Morgan Stanley & Co. International plc+ Charlotte Firkins Commodities Strategist Charlotte.Firkins@morganstanley.com +44 20 7425-3866 Amy Gower (Amy Sergeant), CFA Commodities Strategist Amy.Gower1@morganstanley.com +44 20 7677-6937 Martijn Rats, CFA Equity Analyst and Commodities Strategist Martijn.Rats@morganstanley.com +44 20 7425-6618 Ben Kelson Research Associate Ben.Kelson@morganstanley.com +44 20 7677-1392 Exhibit 1 : While gas prices remain high, this continues to put a floor under thermal coal prices. Source: Argus, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 2 : On an energy-equivalent basis, coal is trading at roughly 0.2x gas in both Europe and Asia, the deepest relative discount since the 2021–22 crisis. Source: Bloomberg, Morgan Stanley Research Holding out for winter: Newcastle 6000kcal fell to $138/t on 9th November as the geopolitical premium in the energy complex unwound, but has since recovered 60% of the decline. Indonesian exports are still tracking ~15% lower YoY, keeping low-cal supply tight, and government signalling on 2027 quotas indicates this will continue. North Asia gas-to-coal switching drove the rally in 1H26 but softened in 3Q26. However, low Japanese LNG and coal stocks, delayed Korean nuclear restarts and continued strength in gas prices should tighten JKT into 1Q27. Finally, Indian buying picked up in October but has underwhelmed vs re-stocking expectations; however, stocks remain low, and we see re-stocking accelerating into 1Q27. We see thermal prices rebounding near-term with MSe $155/t for 1Q27. China is the key bearish driver for 2027: Beijing's push to restore mine output returns it to domestic production growth early next year, weighing further on imports. Ample stocks at consumers also caps near-term upside. Lower gas price forecasts for 2H27 (MSe TTF of €40/MWh), assuming recovery in Qatari LNG flows, should also drive power sector switching back to gas. MS outlook: MSe $155/t for 1Q27, +7% vs forward curve as we still see risks skewed to upside near-term. We then see prices easing to $135/t in 2H27. An elevated cost curve near $127/t limits 2027 downside. Key risks: Upside from a cold winter, a prolonged Hormuz outage or further nuclear delays. Downside from a faster Chinese output recovery, a Middle East resolution or looser Indonesian quotas. Morgan Stanley does and seeks to do business with companies covered in Morgan Stanley Research. As a result, investors should be aware that the firm may have a conflict of interest that could affect the objectivity of Morgan Stanley Research. Investors should consider Morgan Stanley Research as only a single factor in making their investment decision. For analyst certification and other important disclosures, refer to the Disclosure Section, located at the end of this report. += Analysts employed by non-U.S. affiliates are not registered with FINRA, may not be associated persons of the member and may not be subject to FINRA restrictions on communications with a subject company, public appearances and trading securities held by a research analyst account. Key Takeaways Coal has held a ~$140/t floor through the energy sell-off, and we see upside potential into 1Q27, forecasting NEWC 6000kcal at $155/t, +7% vs the curve. Indonesia keeps low-cal supply tight, with exports still around 15% lower YoY and the government signalling tight control of 2027 quotas. North Asia should tighten again into 1Q27, on low Japanese LNG and coal stocks, delayed Korean nuclear restarts and continued strength in gas prices. Indian buying picked up in October but underwhelmed vs restocking expectations. With stocks still low, we see restocking accelerating into 1Q27. China limits the upside into 2027 as mine output returns to growth, and lower gas prices in 2H27 should reverse switching, taking Newcastle to $135/t. November 20, 2026 08:36 PM GMT M Idea 2 Also see: Thermal Coal: Not Time to Turn Bearish Yet (18 Aug 2026) and The Price Deck – 4Q26: Selective Optimism (6 Oct 2026) M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 3 Indonesia: Tight Supply Underpins Winter Upside Exports are still running well below last year: Thermal coal exports fell 20% YoY to 35.9 Mt in September after a 26% fall in August, taking Jan-Sep exports to 339 Mt, down 9% YoY. Slow 2H26 quota top-ups, diversion of supplies to the domestic market and low water on the Barito river were the main constraints on 3Q26 exports. This played out as we expected in Thermal Coal: Not Time to Turn Bearish Yet (18 Aug 2026), where we argued that quota "relaxation" would mostly go to domestic supply and ultimately around half of the extra volume has been directed to PLN, the state-owned utility. However, the pace of exports in 2H26 has been even slower than we forecast. Our FY26 forecast of 475 Mt now looks at risk to the downside, as a 4Q26 pace of 38-40 Mt/month would give FY exports closer to 455 Mt. Exhibit 3: Indonesia's thermal coal exports were 18% lower YoY in 3Q26, as slow quota top-ups, diversion to the domestic market and low river levels constrained supply... Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 4: ...with the weekly data pointing to continued declines in Oct and Nov Source: Refinitiv, Morgan Stanley Research Prompt supply is set to stay tight into year-end: River levels have been recovering since mid-October, but the market has not loosened. Several Indonesian producers are sold out of mid-CV coal through December, and Kalimantan 4200 GAR is still trading at around $78-81/t, close to its October peak. Uncertainty over DSI, which becomes the sole intermediary for coal export clearance from 1st January, is also keeping sellers from offering late-December cargoes. We see this as a near-term floor under low- and mid-CV prices, even with Chinese and Indian buyers holding back. 2027 quotas are now coming into focus: Applications for 2027 RKAB production quotas closed on 15 November, and producers expect the first approvals as early as December. The RKAB quota determines actual output levels, but this is released in batches throughout the year, so instead the market looks towards the government target as a signal of whether quota issuance is intended to be higher or lower next year. Currently the government seems to be taking a similar approach to 2026, with Energy Minister Bahlil promising "tight control" to avoid overproduction and support international prices. Mining association Perhapi has proposed a 2027 target of 700 Mt, below the energy ministry's (ESDM) 2026 target of 736 Mt and broadly in line with the 700-720 Mt ESDM expects Indonesia to actually produce this year. M Idea 4 We see broadly flat 2027 output spelling downside to exports: If total production is at best flat and at worst lower in 2027, then PLN's forecast 20 Mt rise in power-sector demand would require an increase in supply to the domestic market YoY, with the volumes coming straight out of 2027 exports. We see small downside YoY for Indonesia exports in 2027. The government is also moving to removing sales to captive power plants serving nickel smelters from the DMO, which could create further downside risk to export volumes. Ex-DMO smelter demand could support Indonesian FOB prices by competing with overseas buyers for the coal left after miners fulfil their mandatory domestic deliveries. But high prices create a bearish policy risk, limiting upside to prices: Energy Minister Bahlil's framing of 2027 strategy is price-dependent, with possible higher 2027 quotas under consideration as prices recovered. M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 5 India: Restocking Has Underwhelmed, But Stocks Are Still Low Summer draws set up the restocking call for 4Q26: Record power demand and weak hydro drove aggressive stock draws over the summer, with power plant stocks falling from 44 Mt at end-June to 29 Mt at end-August. By late October they were down to about 20 Mt, equivalent to roughly six days of burn and less than half the 45 Mt held in inventory a year earlier. We flagged this as setting up 4Q26 restocking, and a bullish near- term driver, in The Price Deck – 4Q26: Selective Optimism (6 Oct 2026). Exhibit 5: Indian power plant stocks fell to multi-year lows after aggressive summer draws and remain less than half last year's level... Exhibit 6: ...as power sector coal demand ran around 11% higher YoY over Jun-Sep on record power demand and weak hydro Source: Argus, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 7: India's domestic coal output has recovered since the monsoon, rising around 10% YoY in September... Source: Argus, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 8: ...which kept imports 12% lower YoY over Jan-Sep, although Kpler data show a rebound to 14.6 Mt in October Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Restocking then played out in October, but underwhelmed: Seaborne arrivals into India did firm in October, with Kpler estimating imports of around 14.6 Mt (+16% YoY), the first YoY rise since January. But the rebound was smaller than expected, as higher domestic supply met more of the gap. Coal India produced 67.2 Mt in October, up 19% YoY, and sent a record 57.1 Mt to the power sector under directive from the government. Consequently M Idea 6 the marginal buyer in the market in October was not the domestic-coal utilities, but instead industrial buyers such as sponge iron and cement producers, which have been squeezed out of the domestic market. Diwali holidays also kept most Indian buyers out of the spot market from late October into early November. Demand signals from India are still weak for now: Indian buyers are resisting offers for now, with bids for Kalimantan 4200 GAR at $78/t below seller expectations, and Indian buyers have largely stayed away above about $120/t CFR for Richards Bay 5,500 kcal. DRI producers are also loss-making on imported coal, which is weighing on demand. Local reports also suggest the government is unlikely to reissue its import-blending mandate at current prices. Some chemical and steel buyers with low stocks have returned after Diwali, but there is no sign yet of a broader pickup. However, the inventory problem is not solved: Plant stocks had rebuilt only to 23.6 Mt by mid-November, about eight days of burn against a norm of around 19 days, and while the number of plants with critical stocks has fallen to 69 from 94 in October, that is still high going into winter. Stocks have been rebuilding at around 5-6 Mt/month so far in November, only in line with seasonal norms. If stocks were to recover to March 2026 levels by end of March 2027, re-stocking rates would need to rise to ~8 Mt/month. Domestic supply is unlikely to be able to drive such significant stockbuilds alone, meaning India likely still needs to restock from the import market. We see India supporting seaborne demand through winter and watch for signals of stronger restocking efforts into year-end. M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 7 Gas-to-Coal Switching: A Support, Not a Driver The economics still favour coal over gas: Qatari LNG loadings are still only around a third of pre-war levels and QatarEnergy's force majeure notices to buyers now extend through December. Combined with European gas inventories at their lowest in more than a decade, this has helped push both European and Asian gas prices to their highest level since December 2022. Coal continues to remain the attractive option for utilities across both Europe and Asia where switching between fuels is possible, with Platts estimating Korean coal plants earn a margin of $6.60/mmbtu, compared with a loss of $32.90/ mmbtu for gas plants. On an energy equivalent basis and after accounting for plant efficiencies, gas is only competitive with current coal prices if JKM falls below $10/mmbtu. As long as JKM holds around $20-30/mmbtu, in-line with our house price forecasts, we see little incentive for Asian utilities to switch back to gas. But most of the demand boost from switching has already materialised: South Korea's coal-fired generation rose 15% YoY over Jan-Aug, but the majority of this boost was in 1Q26. Korean coal burn was 35% higher YoY in March-April after the LNG shock, but this narrowed to just 3% YoY growth in July-August, as coal plants usually ran close to capacity through peak summer demand so there was narrow room to raise utilisation rates further. Japan shows a similar pattern, with coal generation up 8-9% YoY in April- May but only 2% in June. With coal fleets already running hard, we see switching as a support for demand through winter rather than a source of fresh upside for prices. North Asia has therefore gone from a bullish driver in 1H26 to a softer market in 3Q26, but we expect it to tighten again into year-end and 1Q27, as Korean upside risks and Japan's thinner fuel buffer below show. Exhibit 9: LNG flows through the Strait of Hormuz are still running at only around a third of pre-war levels... Source: Vortexa, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 10: ...leaving coal far cheaper than gas in Asian power, with gas only competitive at current coal prices if JKM falls below ~$10/mmbtu Source: Bloomberg, Morgan Stanley Research M Idea 8 Exhibit 11: Gas inventories in Europe sit over 20pp below the seasonal norm for mid-November, as a tight LNG market has increased competition for supply... Source: GIE, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 12: ...which should keep coal burn in Europe supported over winter Source: ENTSO-E, Morgan Stanley Research Korea could surprise to the upside over winter: Korean coal burn hit a five-year high of around 29.5 GW in August and there is upside risk to winter coal demand if the government relaxes fine dust restrictions over winter. South Korea is due to finalise its winter fine-dust restrictions in late November, which in recent years have capped output at many coal plants at 80% over December-March. An easing towards 90% utilisation would add around 3 GW of coal-fired generation over the winter, according to S&P Global estimates. We estimate this could add ~0.8 Mt/month of coal burn (6,000kcal equivalent) over Dec-Mar, which would largely need to be met by imports, equivalent to a 10% increase vs last winter's imports. Korean buyers stockpiled coal aggressively ahead of summer, but imports fell back in-line with average of 3Q26, possibly leaving some uncovered demand into year-end if restrictions are relaxed. Korea also enters winter with less nuclear capacity than planned. Hanbit 2 went off line in September when its operating licence expired, pending a life extension, Wolsong 4 missed its end-October restart and remains off line, and the new 1.4 GW Saeul 3 reactor has no new start-up date after shutting down during testing. Overall, we see upside risk to South Korea imports into 1Q27, particularly for low-CV coal, given Indonesian flows into South Korea have halved YoY over Aug-Oct. M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 9 Exhibit 13: Korean coal generation hit a five-year high in August and rose 15% YoY over Jan-Aug... Source: Argus, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 14: ...as nuclear output ran around 12% lower YoY, and Korea enters winter with less nuclear capacity than planned Source: Argus, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 15: Korean imports have fallen back to the 5Y average since August after heavy stockpiling ahead of summer... Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 16: ...and Japan's imports were 7% lower YoY in 3Q26, leaving utility coal stocks thin heading into winter Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Japan also looks tighter going forward: Japan initially looked a soft spot heading into winter, as coal generation was effectively flat YoY across Aug-Oct amid strong nuclear and hydro output, with nuclear availability up 6% YoY across Aug-Oct. Utility LNG stocks also looked very healthy heading into winter, sitting 20% above average in mid-October, meaning gas burn should have been supported into year-end. However, the boost from nuclear is set to fade this winter. Argus data imply Japan's available nuclear capacity will average around 11.5 GW over December-February, only slightly above last winter's 11.4 GW, as maintenance outages at Kansai's Ohi 3, Takahama 1 and Takahama 4 and Kyushu's Genkai 4 largely offset the restart of TEPCO's 1.36 GW Kashiwazaki-Kariwa 6. Power plant LNG stocks have also drawn sharply since mid-October, and now sit 13% below last year and 9% below the 2021-25 average, with Kyushu Electric shutting gas-fired units to save fuel. This should be supportive for coal burn and import demand this winter while a colder-than-expected winter could add extra upside risk to imports. Coal stocks are also thin, with Kpler estimating Japanese utilities hold around 7 Mt, below seasonal levels and less than a month of winter burn at around 8 Mt/month, which implies 0.5-1 Mt of imports on top of burn this winter to rebuild the buffer. M Idea 10 Exhibit 17: Japan's coal generation was flat YoY over Aug-Oct amid strong nuclear and hydro output... Source: Bloomberg, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 18: ...but utility LNG stocks have drawn sharply since mid-October and are now 13% below last year Source: METI, Morgan Stanley Research South and Southeast Asia continue to be an area of import strength: The LNG shock and weak hydro have lifted coal burn across the region. In Pakistan, where Qatari LNG deliveries have largely stopped, coal's share of power generation rose to 26% in September from 18% a year earlier, and coal imports are up around 70% YoY over Jan-Sep. Bangladesh's imports are up 21% YoY over Jan-Sep as coal plants replace gas. Both countries should continue to import at elevated levels as LNG prices remain high over winter. In Vietnam, coal-fired generation rose around 68% YoY in October as hydro output fell, and buyers issued tenders for about 1.35 Mt of imported coal in late October and early November. Vietnam's demand should also hold up into 2027, as the government has told hydro plants to conserve reservoir water until the end of March ahead of an El Niño dry season and expects power demand to grow around 10% next year. Exhibit 19: Pakistan's coal imports are up around 70% YoY over Jan-Sep as coal replaces lost Qatari LNG... Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 20: ...and Bangladesh's imports are up 21% YoY as coal plants replace gas Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Upside risk to gas prices should continue to support coal over winter and recent geopolitical risk unwind looks overdone: Increasing optimism around an near-term end to the Middle East conflict following the results of the US mid-term elections drove a significant unwind of geopolitical premium across oil and gas. Coal also captured this move to a lesser extent, with API 6 and API 2 each dropping $13/t in a single week to a 3- M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 11 month low. However, we continue to see gas price risk skewed to the upside over this winter vs the current forward curve (see here and here) as European storage at its lowest in more than a decade and weather uncertainty keep the market tight. However, gas price support for coal could disappear into 2H27: We are currently modelling a return to strong LNG capacity growth in 2H27, as several new LNG projects come online in the US. If Qatari flows have also recovered significantly, then this could push the market into a sizeable gas oversupply by end of next year. In this scenario, we see gas prices in Europe falling to €40/MWh, which would put parity coal prices for ARA coal $80-100/t. Overall, we see gas-to-coal switching keeping prices supported through 1Q27 up to ~ $155/t but not driving coal to significant new highs. M Idea 12 China: Supply Push Caps the Upside Mine inspections curtailed output over summer: Safety inspections launched after the gas explosion at the Liushenyu mine in Shanxi in May, the deadliest since 2009, intensified over the summer and were reinforced by further accidents in Hunan in August. Sxcoal data show thermal coal output fell 6.2% YoY to 289 Mt in August, the lowest August in our 2022-26 data, and 7.2% YoY to 312 Mt in September. Shanxi accounts for almost all of the shortfall, with its thermal coal output down 31% YoY in August and 35% in September, which higher output in Inner Mongolia only partly offset. That supply-side tightness pushed QHD 5500 to a three-year high of Yn1,034/t on 21 October and kept the import arb open through September. However, Beijing has moved quickly to reverse the production shortfall: Since mid- September, a series of policy notices has called for mines to restart, while the NEA’s 30th October winter measures allowed mines that have reached their annual quotas to continue producing through December, provided they meet safety requirements. Shanxi had already pledged on 30th September to increase thermal coal output by up to 31 Mt a month vs current levels through year-end, according to China Coal News, roughly offsetting its monthly losses over the summer. These efforts appear to be gaining traction: utilisation at the 160 thermal coal mines surveyed by Sxcoal rose above 90% in late October for the first time since May. However, Shanxi continued to lag at around 82%, prompting a further notice on 3rd November urging faster restarts at suspended mines. Sxcoal estimates that even a normal fourth quarter would leave the province’s full-year output around 10% below 2025 levels. Exhibit 21: China's thermal coal output fell below its 2022-25 range over Jul-Aug, as safety inspections curtailed output in Shanxi... Source: Sxcoal, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 22: ...which has kept the import arb open since mid-year, albeit well below late-2025 levels Source: Bloomberg,, Morgan Stanley Research M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 13 Exhibit 23: China's thermal coal imports are still running 7% lower YoY over Jan-Sep... Source: Trademap, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 24: ...as soft power and building materials demand kept total thermal coal consumption up less than 1% YoY Source: Sxcoal, Morgan Stanley Research Soft demand has also offset output cuts and weakened import demand: The relative tightness in the China market this year has come from supply rather than demand. Sxcoal data show thermal power generation rose only 0.7% YoY over Jan-Sep and fell 1.4% in September as renewables absorbed most power demand growth, and weak property activity has cut cement demand. China's thermal coal imports fell 16% YoY to 28.6 Mt in September, and total coal imports were down 5.5% YoY in October. Seaborne suppliers have also lost share to overland coal, with Mongolian thermal coal imports running at around 3-3.5 Mt a month, roughly double the 2021-25 median. Demand side softness looks persistent for now as power plant stocks are comfortable at around 210 Mt, or roughly 35 days of burn, and coastal utilities slowed imported coal buying further in mid-November as domestic prices started to fall. Many are waiting to see how far domestic prices drop before buying seaborne cargoes, particularly with expectations of a warm El Niño winter weighing on the demand outlook. Exhibit 25: Stocks at China's six major coastal utilities sit near the top of their 2021-25 range... Source: Sxcoal, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 26: ...while northern port stocks are only in line with seasonal levels, leaving room for restocking if a cold snap arrives Source: Sxcoal, Morgan Stanley Research Cold weather presents a near-term upside risk to China import demand: An El Niño winter has less warming effect on North Asia than on Europe or the US. Cold winter M Idea 14 weather in 1Q27 can booth boost coal demand for heating while curtailing mine activity in China. Despite ample supplies at coastal power plants, lean stocks at southern import hubs leaves room for a quick return to seaborne buying if a cold snap arrives. Port stocks at Guangzhou and Fangcheng are currently at or below their 2023-25 lows. China is the main bearish driver into 2027: We expect domestic output to return to flat- to-positive YoY growth by December or January as restarts continue, and this is the key reason we see prices easing from 2Q27. Given Sxcoal forecasts for flat thermal coal demand in 2027, this leaves minimal room for an import recovery and presents downside risk to our forecast of broadly flat China thermal coal imports at around 350 Mt in 2027. Further out, output monitoring systems at underground mines, due to be in place by end- June 2027, with alerts above 110% of approved capacity, should limit the kind of overproduction that flooded the market in 2024-25. This builds on a rule in force since 1 July that treats any quarter above 30% of annual approved capacity at an underground mine as a major hazard requiring a halt, which limits how much of this year's lost output mines can make up with a late-year surge. M Idea Morgan Stanley Research 15 MS Outlook: Upside into 1Q27, Softer from 2Q27 Above the curve into 1Q27: We keep our Newcastle 6000kcal forecasts at $150/t for 4Q26 and $155/t for 1Q27, against a forward curve at around $145/t for both quarters. Tight Indonesian supply ahead of the first 2027 quota approvals, continued support from gas-to-coal switching and re-stocking demand from India leave upside risk through peak winter demand. Coal is also currently trading at the deepest relative discount to gas since the 2021–22 crisis and around half the 2024–25 range, which should limit coal's downside while gas prices stay elevated. We would not be too bearish on prices with these factors in play. Note, this upside does not rely on China, where we expect domestic supply gains to keep import demand soft into December. Below the curve from 2Q27: We see prices easing to $140/t in 2Q27 and $135/t in 2H27, compared with a flat curve at around $145/t. By then, we expect Chinese output to be growing again, Indian stocks to have rebuilt and the heating season to have passed, while the restart of Korea's Kori 3 and 4 units cuts into coal burn. This gives a 2027 average of $141/t, falling to $130/t in 2028. The cost curve limits the downside: The 90th percentile of the cost curve has risen by around $10/t over 2026 to $127/t, driven by higher diesel costs and royalty payments. Diesel prices have eased with crude since early November, but continued Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian refineries and high spring maintenance levels is likely to keep the diesel market tight into mid-2027 and costs elevated (see The Oil Manual: Diesel and the Coming Catch-Up in Refinery Maintenance). Our 2H27 forecast of $135/t sits only about $8/t above this cost curve support level, so we see limited room for prices to fall much beyond our forecast path even as the market loosens. This year's extra high-CV supply would be the first to go: Supply from the high-CV exporters has responded to this year's elevated prices, with our model showing Australian exports up 6% YoY to 222 Mt and South Africa and Colombia also higher, which has helped cap Newcastle. But much of the extra tonnage, such as trucked South African coal, is high-cost and would be the first to leave the market if prices fell towards $130/t. Wood Mackenzie estimates that at $125/t Newcastle around 13% of Australian and 31% of South African seaborne thermal output would be loss-making, with a further 18% and 29% earning margins below $10/t, and that around 90% of the Russian seaborne thermal output it tracks would also be loss-making at that price. M Idea 16 Exhibit 27: The production-weighted global average cost has increased by $8/t YoY, but if China is removed this moves to $17/t. Source: Wood Mackenzie, Morgan Stanley Research Exhibit 28: Higher costs for Russian and South African miners led the group. Source: Wood Mackenzie, Morgan Stanley Research Key risks: Upside risks include a cold winter in North Asia or Europe, a prolonged Hormuz outage, further nuclear delays, a renewed diesel squeeze as Ukraine steps up strikes on Russian refineries and a lower YoY Indonesian government output target. Downside risks include a faster Chinese output recovery, a diplomatic resolution in the Middle East that pulls LNG prices lower and a looser stance from Indonesia on quota issuance. Pack 钢铁与铁矿石 Steel & Iron Ore 煤炭 Coal 股票与商品相对表现 Equity vs. Commodity SECTION 00 · KEY TAKEAWAYS 核心观点：宏观压力压过结构性支撑，黄金走出趋势通道 金价跌出趋势通道： Fed 加息预期升温、长端美债收益率反弹、美元指数（DXY）创 2025 年初以来新高，叠加黄金作为"流动性来源"在市场动荡中被抛售，且与标普 500 的相关性上升——若金价此前仍跟随 3-7 月的实际收益率趋势，理论上早已跌至 $3,000/oz 附近。 结构性支撑仍在，核心是央行： 1-9 月央行及官方机构购金 675t（其中仅 290t 可归于具体国家），全年有望超过 FY25；波兰 YTD 150t（已达其 700t 目标，行长表态"没有理由停止购金"）、中国 YTD 129t，PBOC 在 2026 年每个月都在增持；中国黄金进口有望创历史新高。 ETF 有韧性但暗藏清算风险： Q3 在 Fed 加息、收益率飙升背景下 ETF 仍净增 210t（占年内增量的 84%）；但大摩估算约 420t（占总持仓 10%）的 ETF 持仓买入成本高于现价，若价格续跌可能形成额外下行压力。 持仓面： COMEX 总净多已接近 2025 年中以来区间下沿（仍高于历史）， Managed Money 自 8 月末持续减多，Other Reportables（CTAs 代表）10 月中旬才开始减仓；绝对空头仅 36k 手（对比 2020 年初低点 24k、2012 年 28k），说明下跌主要由多头平仓驱动。 Fed 路径是关键变量： 大摩经济学家预计 12 月与 3 月各加息 25bp，2028 年降息 50bp；FOMC 纪要显示多位官员主张观望"AI 投资需求、融资条件及 9 月加息的传导"。若就业与通胀数据继续偏强，1 月追加加息可能进入视野。 季节性提供缓冲： 过去 10 年中 7 年 12 月金价平均上涨 2.2%、1 月平均上涨 3.4%；印度婚礼季（11 月下旬-2 月）预计带来约 520 万场婚礼、~129 亿美元的珠宝与贵金属消费，中国春节前备货亦有支撑。 结论： 维持中期看多，但"金发姑娘"式的顺畅上涨已结束——短期波动将持续，投资者需看到 Fed 加息周期接近终点的清晰信号才会回流；上行风险为风险资产企稳、中国买盘加速、油价回落；下行风险为多头继续平仓、Fed 更鹰派、美元走强及 ETF/央行意外抛售。 Section 01 · Cover Story 主笔文章：黄金并非"金发姑娘" Not Goldilocks for Gold（Lead Article） 宏观逆风聚集 Macro pressures building 本周黄金遭遇多重宏观逆风：Fed 加息预期上升、长端债券收益率反弹、DXY 位于 2025 年初以来最高位；同时黄金作为传统的"流动性来源"，在市场波动加大时往往被动提供流动性、承受额外卖压。此前央行与 ETF 的实物买盘足以对冲这些压力，但 11 月以来风险资产全面抛售后，黄金被"顺带"拖低——与标普 500 的相关性上升，并跌出了与实际收益率的近期趋势通道（Exhibit 1/3）。 图 1 · 金价正在脱离与实际收益率的趋势通道 | Gold is moving out of its recent trend channel versus real yields — Source: Bloomberg, Morgan Stanley Research（metal&ROCK p3, Exhibit 3） 图 2 · 2026 年金价与美元指数（DXY）反向移动 | Gold has moved inversely with the DXY — Source: Bloomberg, Morgan Stanley Research（p3, Exhibit 4） 结构性驱动仍在：央行购金 Structural drivers: central bank bid 在政府债务上升与法币信用弱化的背景下，黄金作为实物资产的长期配置逻辑未变；大摩认为央行买盘是结构性的。1-9 月央行与官方机构购金 675t，同比 +6%，全年有望超过 FY25；但其中仅 290t 可归于具体国家——2022 年以来"总购金"与"IMF 申报口径"之间的缺口持续存在。最大买家为波兰（YTD 150t，占 2024 年 1 月以来 IMF 申报央行购金的约三分之一，已于 2026 年 1 月达成 700t 目标，且行长明确表示储备将继续随外储增长）与中国（YTD 129t，PBOC 2026 年逐月增持）。世界黄金协会（WGC）还指出 10 月中国批发需求反季节性偏强，中国黄金进口有望创历史新高，上海对 CME 的溢价总体走高。 图 3 · 央行购金 YTD 同比 +6%，但"总购金"与"可归属国家"口径缺口自 2022 年起扩大 | Central bank YTD volumes are up 6% YoY — Source: WGC（p3, Exhibit 5） 图 4 · Q3 央行购金尤为强劲，主因中国与波兰 | Q3 saw particularly strong gold buying by central banks — Source: WGC（p3, Exhibit 6） 图 5 · PBOC 年内累计增持约 130t，为 2023 年以来最高 | The PBOC has added 130t YTD, the highest since 2023 — Source: Bloomberg（p4, Exhibit 7） 图 6 · 中国黄金进口有望创历史新高 | China is on track for record gold imports — Source: Bloomberg（p4, Exhibit 8） ETF：持仓有韧性，但浮亏盘是隐患 ETFs resilient but liquidation risk rising 2024 年以来 ETF 黄金持仓（吨）与价格高度相关，降息周期中通常加仓；Q3 在 Fed 加息、收益率飙升的环境下 ETF 反而净增 210t、占年内增量的 84%，说明存在利率之外的买入动机。但大摩估算：约 420t（占总持仓 10%）的 ETF 持仓买入成本高于当前金价——若价格继续下跌，这部分仓位存在清算风险，可能放大跌势（Exhibit 2/96）。 图 7 · ETF 持仓随价格下跌依然保持稳健 | ETF Holdings vs Gold Price（Total known ETF Holdings）— Source: Bloomberg（p29, Exhibit 96） 持仓驱动行情 Positioning has been driving price action 截至 11 月 10 日，COMEX 黄金净多持仓已跌至 2025 年中以来区间下沿（绝对水平仍高于历史均值）。 Managed Money 自 8 月末起持续卖出；更能代表 CTA 的 Other Reportables 净多自 10 月中旬才开始回落。合计口径下绝对空头仅 36k 手，仍远低于 2020 年初低点 24k 与 2012 年 28k——说明本轮下跌主要是多头平仓，本周可能开始有少量新空入场，技术支撑位缺乏。 图 8 · COMEX 净多仍处高位但空头极低 | COMEX net long positioning was still elevated, with shorts particularly low — Source: Bloomberg（p4, Exhibit 9，持仓截至 11 月 10 日） 图 9 · Managed Money 自 8 月减仓，Other Reportables 自 10 月中旬减仓 | Managed money has been selling gold since August — Source: Bloomberg（p4, Exhibit 10） 不确定的 Fed 路径 Uncertain path ahead of the Fed 大摩经济学家预测 12 月与 3 月各加息 25bp，2028 年降息 50bp 。FOMC 纪要显示部分官员主张谨慎，希望有时间"评估 AI 投资需求、融资条件以及 9 月加息的传导效果"；其金融状况指标此后已收紧，疲弱的房地产数据与 AI 领域的压力信号也支持渐进加息。但团队同时提示"加快收紧的风险正在上升"——若就业与通胀数据再度偏强，1 月追加加息将成为可能。油价路径同样重要：2026 年大部分时间黄金与油价反向相关（油价通过通胀与利率政策的传导影响黄金）。 季节性支撑 Seasonality may provide some support 历史上 12 月与 1 月是金价最强的月份：过去 10 年中 7 年 12 月上涨、平均 +2.2%；1 月再涨 3.4%、同样是 7/10 年上涨。时点上叠加印度婚礼季（11 月下旬至 2 月），印度全印贸易商联合会（CAIT）预计 11 月 21 日-12 月 15 日将有 520 万场婚礼、带动约 129 亿美元的珠宝与贵金属消费；中国春节前备货亦可能提供年初支撑。 图 10 · 金价月度回报：12 月/1 月季节性最强（表内为 2015-2026 各月涨跌幅，%） | Gold's returns are typically strongest in December/January — Source: Bloomberg, monthly returns（p4, Exhibit 11） 大摩展望与风险 MS Outlook: volatility ahead, slower recovery 大摩认为黄金分析正变得越来越难：金价与实际收益率的关系快速变化、黄金被用作流动性来源、对结构性驱动敏感。本周的价格行为符合"流动性驱动的抛售 + 少量新空"，而 12 月 Fed action 的不确定性将使投资者观望，直到加息周期终点的路径更清晰。结构性方面，央行买盘将保持，中国需求强劲（上海溢价走高、进口创纪录在望）。 维持中期建设性观点，但看多兑现的节奏可能慢于预期，极短期内波动继续。 上行风险 Upside： 风险资产企稳带动投资者回流；低价刺激中国（PBOC 与居民）加速买入；油价回落缓解通胀与加息压力；或油价大涨引发滞胀担忧——两条油价路径皆可能利多黄金；若金价企稳，投资者可能重新聚焦中期叙事。 下行风险 Downside： 净多持仓仍然偏多，多头继续平仓与新空入场都有空间且技术支撑缺乏；经济数据坚挺或使 Fed 更鹰派；美元进一步走强；ETF 或央行/其他机构出现广泛清算。 Section 02 · Week in Review 一周回顾与价格快照 Morgan / Morgan Stanley）。 目录 Contents 核心观点 KEY POINTS 会议背景与供应展望 需求结构与价格、贸易政策 Key Points 核心观点 KEY POINTS 2027 供应仍偏紧： 国内矿产受开采指标与环保约束； 2026 年精矿进口同比 +13kt 至 27kt （以缅甸、哈萨克斯坦为主）。 海外增量在路上： 哈萨克斯坦 Bakuta 项目等海外矿山或于 2027 年贡献增量，但 投产延期仍是风险 ；2026 年小幅过剩，2027 年回归更紧平衡。 需求复苏可期： 3Q26 中国钨消费环比 -4.4% ；硬质合金占需求 53% 、钨材 28%、特钢 14%；传统制造仍弱， PCB 微钻与半导体 应用驱动增长。 六氟化钨（WF6）高增： 产量 2026 年同比 +55% 、2027 年 +37.5% ，印证半导体链景气。 价格支撑： 矿供增长有限+需求复苏+库存正常化，共同支撑 2027 年钨价。 海外 APT 溢价高位： 精炼产能有限+出口限制，海外仲钨酸铵溢价维持高位。 供应链碎片化： 海外钨政策收紧强化区域化定价，区域溢价获支撑。 出口与再生： 中国出口受两用物项出口管制收紧约束， 韩国成为关键增长市场 ；再生钨主要依赖国内废料回收，美国出口管制的直接影响有限。 Section 01 会议背景与供应展望 Context & supply outlook 本期 Update 为 Morgan Stanley 大中华材料团队（Rachel Zhang、Hannah Yang、Chris Jiang 等）与 上海有色网（SMM）分析师 Zhu Juno 的钨专家电话会纪要，行业观点维持 有吸引力（Attractive） 。 供应： 国内矿山产量受开采指标与更严环保监管约束，增长有限；2026 年钨精矿进口预计同比增加约 13kt 至 27kt，主要来自缅甸与哈萨克斯坦。海外新项目（如哈萨克斯坦 Bakuta 项目）有望自 2027 年起贡献增量供应，但投产延期风险犹存。专家预计 2026 年市场小幅过剩，2027 年重回更紧平衡。 图 1 · 原文 Key Takeaways 要点摘录（价格支撑、APT 溢价、供应链碎片化、韩国市场、再生钨）| Key Takeaways excerpt — Source: Morgan Stanley（原文 p1） Section 02 需求结构与价格、贸易政策 Demand, prices & trade policy 需求： 3Q26 中国钨消费环比下降约 4.4%，结构上硬质合金约占 53%、钨材 28%、特钢 14%。传统制造业需求依然偏弱，但 PCB 微钻与半导体应用 成为增长引擎——中国六氟化钨（WF6）产量预计 2026 年同比增长约 55%、2027 年再增约 37.5%，反映先进制程与存储扩产对钨原料的拉动。 价格与贸易： 国内矿供增长受限、需求复苏与库存正常化共同支撑 2027 年钨价；海外 APT（仲钨酸铵）溢价因精炼产能有限与出口限制维持高位；海外钨政策收紧强化供应链碎片化、支撑区域溢价。中国出口受两用物项管制趋严约束，韩国成为关键增长市场；再生钨供应以国内废料回收为主，美国出口管制的直接影响有限。 结论： 供给刚性+新兴需求（半导体/PCB）+库存正常化构成 2027 年钨价的三重支撑；政策端（出口管制、海外供应链重构）强化中国链条外的区域溢价，板块维持 Attractive。 图 2 · 原文正文摘录：2027 供应偏紧与需求复苏（硬质合金 53%/钨材 28%/特钢 14%，WF6 +55%/+37.5%）| Body excerpt: Tungsten supply tight, demand recovery likely in 2027 — Source: Morgan Stanley（原文 p1） 仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议，观点归属原机构。原文版权归 J.P. Morgan / Morgan Stanley 所有，本页为其中文精读笔记。

Request your ballot here. Greater China Materials Asia Pacific Industry View Attractive Tungsten supply likely to remain relatively tight in 2027. According to Ms Zhu, China's domestic mine production remains constrained by mining quotas and tighter environmental regulations. Meanwhile, she expects concentrate imports to increase by ~13kt YoY to 27kt in 2026, primarily from Myanmar and Kazakhstan. Overseas mine additions, including Kazakhstan's Bakuta project, could contribute incremental supply in 2027, although commissioning delays remain a risk. Ms Zhu expects a modest surplus in 2026 before the market returns to a tighter balance in 2027. Tungsten demand recovery likely in 2027, as per Ms Zhu, led by emerging applications. She noted that China's tungsten consumption declined ~4.4% QoQ in 3Q26, with cemented carbide accounting for ~53% of demand, followed by tungsten materials (28%) and special steel (14%). While traditional manufacturing demand remains weak, Ms Zhu expects PCB micro-drills and semiconductor applications to drive growth. She projects China's tungsten hexafluoride production to increase ~55% YoY in 2026 and ~37.5% in 2027. Ms Zhu Juno is an analyst from Shanghai Metals Market. She is not a member of Morgan Stanley's Research Department. Key Takeaways Ms Zhu, an analyst from Shanghai Metals Market, thinks that limited domestic mine supply growth, demand recovery, and inventory normalization could support tungsten prices in 2027. In her view, overseas APT premiums remain elevated due to limited refining capacity and export restrictions. She further thinks that tightening overseas tungsten policies could reinforce supply-chain fragmentation and support regional price premiums. China's tungsten exports remain constrained by tightening dual-use export controls, while South Korea has emerged as a key growth market, as per Ms Zhu. She also stated that China's recycled tungsten supply primarily relies on domestic scrap collection, limiting the direct impact of US export controls. reports.stext: 铁矿石专家电话会要点 | Morgan Stanley 2026-11-17 MORGAN STANLEY · 铁矿石 · GREATER CHINA MATERIALS 铁矿石专家电话会要点 Takeaways from Iron Ore Expert Call 机构： Morgan Stanley （Greater China Materials | Asia Pacific） · 行业观点： Attractive · 发布： 2026-11-17 （03:03 PM GMT） · 页数： 6 页 · 分析师：Rachel L Zhang / Hannah Yang / Chris Jiang 等 专家嘉宾：凌先生（Mr. Ling，浙江纳轩商品贸易分析师）——非摩根士丹利研究部成员，观点为其个人观点。 目录 Contents 核心观点 Key takeaways 库存：累库远低于预期 Inventory 供应：主流与非主流矿山增量 Supply 价格敏感性：到货量的价格弹性 Price elasticity 废钢与铁水生产 Scrap & molten iron 需求展望与 2027 价格区间 Demand & price outlook KEY TAKEAWAYS · 核心观点 要点速览 年初至今中国铁矿石累库仅 8.5mnt ，远低于市场预期的 20–30mnt；主因巴西低品位矿减产、非主流供应收缩、发运中国的比例下降及国产矿减产。 供应增量： 主流矿山 2026 年 +17mnt（+1.3%）、2027 年 +15mnt（+1.3%）；非主流矿山 2026 年 +17mnt、2027 年 +36mnt， 主要来自西芒杜（Simandou） 。 到货量对价格高度敏感： 价格从 US$120/t 跌至 US$100/t，年到货量约减 45mnt；若进一步跌至 US$80/t，再减约 48mnt/年；运力紧张使高成本矿难以及时发运。 需求端： 2026 年全球粗钢需求大致持平，中国下降（约 30mnt）被海外增长抵消；2027 年或增长约 7mnt（俄乌、中东冲突结束情景），中国需求或再降约 2.8mnt。 2027 年价格区间判断：US$80–95/t ——上半年 US$90–95，下半年随供应放量趋向 US$80–85 。 Section 01 库存：累库远低于预期 Inventory build well below expectations 年初至今中国铁矿石库存累积 仅 8.5mnt ，大幅低于此前市场预期的 20–30mnt 。 原因有四：①巴西低品位矿因矿价下跌而减产；②部分非主流供应收缩；③运往中国的发货比例下降；④国内（国产矿）产量下降。 另有一部分库存 不可交易 ：中国矿产资源集团（China Mineral Resources Group）与 FMG 的谈判仍在进行中。 展望：累库规模 2026 年可能达到 10mnt ，2027 年 32mnt 。 要点： 「累库不及预期」是本轮矿价韧性的核心——供给对低价的响应（巴西低品位矿减产、非主流矿退出）+ 发运结构转向非中国 + 部分库存被锁定不可交易，共同压低了实际可流通的累库量。 Section 02 供应：主流与非主流矿山增量 Supply growth: mainstream vs non-mainstream mines 主流矿山： 2026 年供应增长 17mnt（+1.3%） ，2027 年增长 15mnt（+1.3%） ——增速温和、节奏平稳。 非主流矿山： 2026 年增长 17mnt，2027 年显著放量至 36mnt ，主要驱动为 几内亚西芒杜（Simandou）项目 爬产。 运力侧：船舶供给紧张可能令发运成本维持高位，抑制高成本矿山的发运意愿（与价格弹性机制互相强化）。 结论： 2027 年供应压力主要来自非主流矿（尤其 Simandou），这是下半年价格趋向 US$80–85 的关键供给变量。 Section 03 价格敏感性：到货量的价格弹性 Shipment to China is price-sensitive 依据历史规律，矿价从 US$120/t 跌至 US$100/t 时，运往中国的到货量每年约减少 45mnt 。 若价格进一步跌至 US$80/t ，到货量将再减约 48mnt/年 ——即低价会自动触发供应收缩的减震机制。 此外，船舶供应紧张使发运成本居高不下，高成本矿石难以进入海运市场，进一步收窄低价下的有效供给。 Section 04 废钢与铁水生产 Steel scrap supply & resilient molten iron output 废钢： 迄今国内废钢供应尚未明显受增值税发票政策影响；但随着废钢价格走低，明年废钢供应量可能下降。 铁水产量韧性： 尽管钢厂毛利为负，铁水生产依然偏强。专家归因于三点：①现金毛利仍为正；②钢厂自身钢材库存偏低；③原材料备库维持在低水平（即按需采购、随用随买）。 Section 05 需求展望与 2027 价格区间 Demand outlook & 2027 price range 2026 年： 全球粗钢需求大致持平；中国下降约 30mnt ，被中国以外地区的需求增长所抵消。 2027 年： 若俄乌与中东冲突结束的情景兑现，全球钢铁需求或增长约 7mnt ；其中中国需求可能再下滑约 2.8mnt 。 价格路径： 2027 年铁矿石价格区间 US$80–95/t ：上半年 US$90–95（Simandou 放量前），下半年随供应增长逐步逼近 US$80–85 。 结论： 供应端「主流稳增 + 非主流（Simandou）放量」 vs 需求端「中国继续下滑、海外弱修复」，叠加到货量对价格的高弹性（US$120→100 减 45mnt、→80 再减 48mnt），共同框定 2027 年 US$80–95/t 的运行区间，前高后低。 本页为研报阅读笔记，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属 Morgan Stanley 原报告（2026-11-17）。 专家嘉宾观点（Mr. Ling，浙江纳轩）为个人观点，不代表 Morgan Stanley 研究部。Original: Greater China Materials | Asia Pacific — Industry View: Attractive · Morgan Stanley Research Update

Request your ballot here. Greater China Materials Asia Pacific Industry View Attractive YTD China's iron ore inventory accumulation was only 8.5mnt, below previous market expectation of 20-30mnt: This is mainly because production of low-grade ore in Brazil was cut in response to lower ore prices, reduced production of some non-mainstream supply, lower percentage of shipments to China, and lower domestic production. Also, some inventory is not tradable given ongoing negotiations between China Mineral Resources Group and FMG. Inventory accumulation may reach 10mnt in 2026 and 32mnt in 2027. Iron ore shipment to China is price-sensitive: Arrivals can decrease ~45mnt/year when prices fall from US$120/t to US100, woth a further reduction of ~48mnt/year if prices falls to US$80, based on historical patterns. Shipment cost might remain high given tight supply of ships, preventing shipment of high-cost ores. Domestic steel scrap supply so far has not been affected apparently by VAT invoice policy: However, this could decrease next year following lower scrap steel prices. Molten iron production is relatively resilient amid negative steel makers' margins: Mr.Ling believes this reflects positive cash margins, low steel inventory at producers, and procurement of raw materials at low levels. Key Takeaways Mr. Ling, an analyst from Zhejiang Naxuan, expects iron ore supply from mainstream mines to grow 17mnt/1.3% in 2026 and 15mnt/1.3% in 2027... ...while supply from non-mainstream mines grows 17mnt in 2026 and 36mnt in 2027, mainly driven by Simandou. Global crude steel demand is expected to be roughly flat in 2026, with China's decline (~30mnt) being offset by ex-China demand growth. Steel demand in 2027 may grow ~7mnt, considering the possibility of conflict ending in Russia-Ukraine and the Middle East. China's demand may slip ~2.8mnt. Mr. Ling expects iron ore prices to range between US$80 and $95/t in 2027, with 1H at US$90-95 and approaching US$80-85 in 2H following supply growth. reports.stext: 铜正流出美国、流向中国：短期承压 | Morgan Stanley 铜快评 2026-11-18 MORGAN STANLEY · 铜 · GREATER CHINA MATERIALS 铜正流出美国、流向中国：短期承压 Correction: Copper Out of US and Coming to China; Near-term Pressure 机构： Morgan Stanley （Greater China Materials | Asia Pacific） · 行业观点： Attractive · 发布： 2026-11-18 （当日更正版，04:00 PM GMT） · 页数： 6 页 · 分析师：Rachel L Zhang / Hannah Yang / Chris Jiang 等 目录 Contents 核心观点 Key takeaways 最新动态：美国铜流向亚洲 What's new 我们的解读：中国库存极低、升水走高 Our reading 短期展望与更正说明 Outlook & correction note KEY TAKEAWAYS · 核心观点 要点速览 约 20–30kt 铜已从美国西部流向亚洲市场 ：渠道多方核实确认；驱动是中国升水高企（当前约 US$360 ）与 LME 对 COMEX 约 US$100 的价差。 中国铜社会库存降至多年低位 ：仅约 76kt （约合 2 天用量），较 3 月初的 579kt 大幅回落，供应紧张推动中国升水持续上行。 套利窗口已打开 ：历史上 LME–COMEX 价差（含升水）达到 US$200–300/t 时，铜即会从美国流向非美市场；当前高升水下流出预计延续。 短期铜价承压 ：美国铜流出叠加宏观波动与美国加息，构成铜价近端的压制因素。 Section 01 最新动态：美国铜流向亚洲 What's new — copper flowing out of the US to Asia 基于多来源渠道核实（channel checks）， 约 20–30kt 铜已从美国西部发往亚洲市场 ，动力来自更高的中国升水（当前约 US$360）以及 LME 与 COMEX 铜价之间约 US$100 的价差。 与此同时，受 COMEX 铜价回落影响，美国国内近期还出现了 库存从 COMEX 仓库向 LME 仓库的小规模迁移 。 本次为当日更正版：原文于 2026-11-18 14:46 GMT 首发后，更正了「美国西部流向亚洲的铜量」数字后重新发布（更正后为 20–30kt）。 要点： 美国铜流出并非理论推演，而是已发生的事实流（20–30kt）；中国升水 US$360 + LME/COMEX 价差 US$100 是牵引铜物流向的核心套利信号。 Section 02 我们的解读：中国库存极低、升水走高 Our reading — multiyear-low China inventory, rising premium 中国铜社会库存已降至多年低位 ：约 76kt 、仅相当于约 2 天消费量，相比 3 月初的 579kt 已大幅去化，供应紧张是升水持续上涨的直接原因。 套利机制： 当 LME–COMEX 价差（含升水）达到约 US$200–300/t 时，铜通常就会从美国流向非美市场；当前中国升水处于高位，大摩认为美国铜流出在近期仍将延续。 对价格而言，流出本身反映的是「中国缺铜、美国过剩」的结构性错配，但短期内与宏观扰动形成叠加效应。 结论： 低库存 + 高升水支撑中国现货端，但美国铜持续流出（且可能继续）叠加宏观波动与美国加息，令铜价 短期承压 ；中期行业观点维持 Attractive 。 Section 03 短期展望与更正说明 Near-term outlook & correction note 近端判断： 美国铜外流延续 + 宏观波动率上升 + 美国加息 → 铜价近端继续承压；供需紧张的信号则体现在中国升水与社会库存上。 后续观察指标： 中国升水（US$360）、LME–COMEX 价差（约 US$100）、中国社会库存（76kt / 约 2 天）能否持续牵引美国库存向亚洲转移。 更正声明： 本文为 2026-11-18 当日更正版（原版当日 14:46 GMT 发布），更正内容为「美国西部流向亚洲市场的铜量」；如需原版可联系 Equity_Research_Publishing@morganstanley.com。 本页为研报阅读笔记，仅供研究参考、不构成投资建议；观点与数据归属 Morgan Stanley 原报告（2026-11-18）。 Original: Greater China Materials | Asia Pacific — Industry View: Attractive · Morgan Stanley Research Update

reports.stext: RBC Commodity Comment: Making Waves · 精读总结 RBC CAPITAL MARKETS · 全球大宗商品策略与 MENA 研究 Commodity Comment: Making Waves（掀起波澜） Geopolitics, Oil, Natural Gas, Gold, Clean Energy & MENA 机构： RBC Capital Markets · 报告日期： 2026 年 11 月 5 日 · 页数： 12 页 · 团队：Helima Croft（主管）、Christopher Louney、John Soughan、Allison Enck、Victoria Silva 整理：研报工作台 AI 精读 · 观点与数据归属 RBC Capital Markets，仅供研究参考 目录 CONTENTS 核心观点 KEY POINTS 地缘政治：选后终局博弈 原油：乌克兰炼厂打击重启，别高兴太早 天然气：数据中心用气预测面临下行风险 黄金：乘"蓝潮"重返 4,000 美元上方 清洁能源：蓝潮之下的绿色反弹 供需平衡与价格预测（附 CFTC 持仓） KEY POINTS 核心观点 "蓝潮"由高能源价格的选民怒火推动 ，但让不受欢迎的伊朗战争近期落幕的协议仍将艰难：年底前最可能的路径是 军事升级 ，或 封锁/袭船僵局延续 。 乌克兰对俄罗斯炼厂的打击于 10 月 30 日重启 （此前约 2 周间歇）：10 月俄罗斯炼厂开工率回升至 58% （9 月 52%）、成品油出口环比 +约 18 万桶/日 ——但每次"能源停火"都极其短暂，RBC 预计打击将持续压制俄罗斯炼厂与出口。 中期选举给数据中心用气预测引入下行风险 ：承诺暂停数据中心的候选人赢下 得州、俄亥俄、佐治亚 州长选举；9 个"州长当选人支持暂停"的州合计有 56.1 GW 在建配套燃气产能，其中 45 GW 在得州 ——竞选承诺能否转化为政策尚待观察，但预测风险已由上行转为下行。 黄金重获支撑、重返 4,000 美元/盎司上方 （美元走弱+收益率下行）；立法僵局令"赤字交易"担忧重定价——但 RBC 认为 来年黄金的命运将更多取决于不确定性 （国会调查、行政行动）而非宏观顺风。 清洁能源股选后大涨 （11 月 4 日 S&P 全球清洁能源指数 +3%，S&P 500 能源指数 -4.7%）：民主党控制国会或制约政府拆除联邦清洁能源支持，但 国会复会后乐观情绪将受考验 ——特朗普仍有否决权，恢复被取消的税收抵免并不容易。 价格预测（中位情形） ：布伦特 2026/2027 年均价 91/88 美元/桶 （2027 年逐季走低：1Q 98 → 4Q 77）；HH 天然气 2026/2027 年 3.29/3.84 美元/百万英热 ；黄金 2026/2027 年 4,503/4,225 美元/盎司 （2027 区间 3,661–5,296）。 SECTION 01 · GEOPOLITICS 地缘政治：选后终局博弈 Post Election Endgame 周二"蓝潮"（民主党大胜）由选民对高能源价格的怒火推动；但 RBC 地缘主管 Helima Croft 认为，让不受欢迎的伊朗战争近期收场的协议 仍将困难重重 。尽管副总统 Vance 公开表达不满，年底前最可能的行动路径仍是军事升级或封锁/袭船僵局延续。近期海湾之行中，RBC 遇到对"通过谈判全面重开霍尔木兹海峡"的普遍怀疑——伊朗坚持 全面落实 6 月谅解备忘录（MOU） 。美国使馆人员缩减、地区旅行警告、美政府与企业退出大型会议，都凸显进一步动武的现实风险。 市场与海湾的认知分化： 选举前的抛售似乎押注白宫会以宣布和平协议阻止民主党横扫；如今"惨败"已成现实，协议逻辑转为"总统止损"——在"美国优先"阵营公开指责与参议员 Schumer 承诺结束战争的背景下。若伊朗在核计划、资金转移与霍尔木兹控制权上做出重大让步，可持续协议的概率将上升（关注卡塔尔外交渠道），但伊朗领导层尚无软化迹象。袭船仍在继续；白宫至少会维持 CENTCOM 主导的封锁。"以升级促退出"（escalate to exit）的吸引力随选举压力消退而上升。 SECTION 02 · OIL 原油：乌克兰炼厂打击重启，别高兴太早 Russia/Ukraine — Not So Fast 乌克兰对俄罗斯炼厂的打击在约 2 周间歇后于 10 月 30 日重启 。受益于间歇期检修，俄罗斯炼厂开工率 10 月回升至 58% （9 月 52%）；叠加出口限制部分解除，俄罗斯成品油出口环比增加约 18 万桶/日 ，市场因此憧憬成品油市场获得喘息。但 RBC 提醒：双方之间每一次"能源停火"都 极其短暂 ，打击有时在停火宣布后立即恢复。乌克兰保持充分动机、美国杠杆有限，乌克兰的战略大概率延续——预计打击将继续干扰俄罗斯炼厂与石油工业运营、拖累出口量。 Fig 1 · 俄罗斯炼厂开工量（左轴，百万桶/日）与利用率（右轴）：10 月利用率回升至 58%（9 月 52%），但乌克兰打击 10 月 30 日重启 | Russian Refinery Runs and Utilization — Source: Petro-Logistics, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p1） Fig 2 · WTI 与布伦特远期曲线（美元/桶）：远期贴水结构，1 年前/1 月前/1 周前/最新曲线对比 | WTI & Brent forward curves — Source: Bloomberg, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p3, Figures 1-2） SECTION 03 · NATURAL GAS 天然气：数据中心用气预测面临下行风险 Data Center Downside 美国中期选举结果给 RBC 的 数据中心燃气发电用量预测 引入下行风险：承诺暂停数据中心的候选人赢下 得州、俄亥俄、佐治亚 三州州长选举。影响最大的是得州——民主党从州长当选人 Gina Hinojosa 到德州铁路委员会（本州油气行业主管监管机构）一路全胜；计划为数据中心供电的现场燃气电站的 空气许可审批 通常经州长掌控的部门，或将面临延期。在 9 个州长当选人支持暂停数据中心开发的州，合计有 56.1 GW 规划中的现场燃气产能，其中 45 GW 在得州 （Hinojosa 可延续 Abbott 的许可暂停）。竞选承诺能否落实为政策尚待观察，但中期选举已使该预测的风险由上行转为下行。 Fig 3 · 州长当选人支持暂停州的规划数据中心产能（GW）：9 州合计 56.1 GW，其中得州 45 GW 燃气共址产能 | Governor-elect Pause, Planned Data Center Capacity — Source: Clearview, Bloomberg, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p2） SECTION 04 · GOLD 黄金：乘"蓝潮"重返 4,000 美元上方 Riding the Blue Wave 中期选举"蓝潮"后，黄金在美元走弱与收益率下行的带动下 重返 4,000 美元/盎司上方 。RBC 重申选前黄金报告的观点：在黄金投资者眼中，可能的 立法僵局 令其对进一步"赤字扩张立法"的担忧重新定价，从而减轻了收益率上行与"货币贬值交易"的压力。市场或许还寄望新当选官员聚焦抗通胀，但油气与伊朗故事需要单独评估（见 Helima 最新观点）。同时 RBC 仍认为，新国会开工后不确定性 不会下降 ——国会调查启动、特朗普转向行政行动，头条、噪音与不确定性可能进一步升高。总体上多空力量并存：当前美元与收益率走弱让黄金重获支撑，但 来年更值得关注的是不确定性本身 。 Fig 4 · 美债 10 年期收益率与黄金的 1 个月/3 个月滚动相关性：近期收益率与黄金负相关加深 | 10yr US yield correlation with gold — Source: Bloomberg, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p2） Fig 5 · 金价（左轴，美元/盎司）与 30 天黄金波动率指数（右轴）：选后金价重返 4,000 上方、波动率回落 | Gold price versus 30-day volatility — Source: Bloomberg, Thomson Reuters Eikon, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p5, Figure 11） Fig 6 · 左：COMEX 管理基金黄金持仓（千手，多头/空头/净多）；右：黄金 ETP 流向（千盎司，SPDR 与 iShares） | Gold Managed Money positioning & Gold ETP flows — Source: Bloomberg, CFTC, ETP issuer websites, RBC Capital Markets（原报告 p5, Figures 14-15） SECTION 05 · CLEAN ENERGY 清洁能源：蓝潮之下的绿色反弹 Blue Wave, Green Rally 民主党中期选举横扫后，清洁能源板块重现乐观情绪——但 RBC 认为 国会复会后这种乐观将受考验 。11 月 4 日 S&P 全球清洁能源指数上涨 3% ，而 S&P 500 能源指数下跌 4.7% ：市场押注民主党控制国会将牵制政府拆除联邦清洁能源支持的努力，对未来几年将向东海岸送电的 海上风电 发展尤为有利。但现实约束仍在：特朗普保留否决权，恢复已被取消的税收抵免并非易事。RBC 认为 许可改革 仍是近期最有可能的立法机会，但在"跛脚鸭会期"结束前民主党不太可能让步通过。 Fig 7 · 能源类股指（以 11/3 收盘为基准）：11/4 清洁能源指数 +3%、S&P 500 能源指数 -4.7% | S&P Energy Indices, indexed to Nov 3 close — Geopolitics: Post Election Endgame helima.croft@rbccm.com While voter anger over high energy prices propelled Tuesday's blue wave, a deal to bring the unpopular Iran war to a near- term conclusion will remain challenging. From our standpoint, the most likely course of action for the remainder of the year is either a military escalation or a continuation of the blockade/ongoing tanker attack stalemate, despite the public airing of grievances by Vice President Vance. During our recent trip to the Gulf, we encountered significant skepticism about the likelihood of a negotiated settlement that would lead to the full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, given Iran's continued insistence on the full implementation of the June MOU. The US embassy drawdowns, regional travel advisories, and cancellation of US government and corporate participation in major conferences underscored the clear and present risk of further kinetic action. We were struck by the divergence between deepening escalation concerns in the Gulf and the headline-driven off-ramp optimism of market participants… …thousands of miles away. The selloff preceding the midterms seemed predicated on the White House being incentivized to stave off a democratic landslide by announcing a peace deal. Now that the electoral debacle has occurred, the deal case has shifted to one of the President cutting his losses in the face of public rebukes from the America-first camp and Senator Schumer's pledge to end the war. The prospects of a sustainable agreement would rise if Iran offered major concessions on the nuclear program, cash transfers, and Hormuz control rights, and we will be monitoring the Qatari diplomatic track accordingly. However, Iranian leadership has shown no signs of moderating such demands. Attacks on vessels continue, and at a minimum the White House will likely keep the current CENTCOM-enforced blockade in place. The appeal of an "escalate to exit" approach could still climb now that the electoral imperative has receded. Oil: Russia/Ukraine— Not So Fast christopher.louney@rbccm.com Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries resumed on Oct 30, following a brief period of respite that lasted around 2 weeks. Owing to this hiatus, refinery repairs were able to aid national throughput, with utilization up to 58% in October (versus 52% in September). Alongside these developments and a partial lifting of export constraints, Russia increased product exports by around 180 kb/d m/m, and we heard some anticipation of further improvement as a reprieve for product markets. However, each instance of energy ceasefire between the two has been fleeting, with attacks sometimes occurring immediately after the announcement. As we have continued to highlight, with Ukraine maintaining every incentive, and limited leverage from the United States, the Ukrainian strategy is highly likely to persist. As such, we expect strikes will continue to hamper Russian refinery and oil industry operations, impeding export volumes. The most consequential in our view is in Texas, where democrats won down the entire ballot from Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa to a seat on the Railroad Commission, the main regulatory body for Texas's oil and gas industry. On-site gas plants planning to power data centers will likely face delays with air permits, an approval that often goes through offices controlled by the Governor. Within the nine states whose governor-elect backed a pause on data center development, there are 56.1GW of planned on-site gas capacity and 45 GW of that is in Texas, where Hinojosa could extend Greg Abbott's permit pause. While it remains to be seen how campaign promises translate to policy, the midterms moved the risk to our forecasts from the upside to the downside. Gold: Riding the Blue Wave christopher.louney@rbccm.com After the blue wave in this week’s midterms, gold recovered back above the $4000/oz level, namely amid a weaker dollar and lower yields. We stand by our comments from our pre- midterm gold note that likely legislative gridlock in the eyes of gold investors has rerated their concerns about further deficit- increasing legislation and thus diminished upwards pressure on yields and the debasement trade. We suspect there is also hope about a general focus for incoming elected officials on fighting inflation, but we would carve out the oil and Iran story in terms of our expectations (see Helima’s latest). Likewise, we also still think that uncertainty will not decrease once a new Congress is underway, as congressional investigations begin and Trump focuses on executive action. We suspect headlines, noise, and uncertainty may be further elevated. Overall, there are some countervailing forces at play, and while right now dollar and yield weakness has allowed gold to regain its footing, we eye uncertainty in the coming year. Clean Energy: Blue Wave, Green Rally allison.enck@rbccm.com There’s a renewed sense of optimism in clean energy following the Democratic midterm sweep, optimism that we believe may be challenged once Congress reconvenes. The S&P Global Clean Energy Index rose 3% on November 4, compared to the 4.7% drop of the S&P 500 Energy Index, reflecting the relative optimism based on Democratic control of Congress potentially providing a check on the administration’s efforts to dismantle federal clean energy support, immediately beneficial for offshore wind development that is set to send gigawatts of power to the east coast in the coming years. While it is true that Democrats are positioned to increase oversight of permitting and challenge regulatory rollback, Trump still has veto power and restoring eliminated tax credits wouldn’t be easy. In our view, permitting reform is still the most plausible near-term legislative opportunity, but it seems unlikely Democrats will concede passage until after the lame duck. reports.stext: Commodity Compass：Tether 与数字黄金的崛起 · 法兴 · 精读总结 SOCGEN · CROSS ASSET RESEARCH – COMMODITIES · WEEKLY Commodity Compass：Tether 与数字黄金的崛起——当新钱遇上古老的黄金 Tether and the Rise of Digital Gold: When New Money Meets Ancient Gold 机构： Société Générale 跨资产研究（大宗商品） · 报告日期： 2026 年 10 月 29 日 · 页数： 12 页 · 作者：Mike Haigh（FIC 与大宗商品研究主管）、Jeremy Sellem（跨商品策略师） 整理：研报工作台 AI 精读 · 观点与数据归属 Société Générale，仅供研究参考 目录 CONTENTS 核心观点 KEY POINTS 数字黄金的崛起：金融科技成为黄金新买家 案例研究：Tether——介于央行与黄金 ETF 之间的混合体 储备 Nowcast：Q3 末或达约 161 吨，5 亿美元 XAUT 铸造 KEY POINTS 核心观点 黄金不再是央行/ETF/金银行的专属舞台 ：新一代金融科技公司以区块链为实物黄金创建数字凭证。规模最大的 15 只金本位加密代币合计市值已超 60 亿美元 、隐含黄金敞口约 45 吨 ；2026 年至今成交额突破 1,500 亿美元 ，已超 2025 年全年纪录。 但体量仍是"利基" ：全球黄金市场日均成交约 3,000 吨 （现货约 950 吨+衍生品约 2,000 吨），代币化黄金日均成交仅约 3 吨 ；整个代币化黄金板块仅相当于实物黄金 ETF 持仓（约 4,000 吨）的 1% ——但增速远快于传统投资渠道。 结构性优势 ：极小额分割所有权、7×24 全天候交易、即时结算、嵌入数字金融生态；部分发行方还通过金条出借计划提供 生息黄金 （金价敞口+利息收入）。 Tether 案例 ：据 SG 估算，Tether 集团黄金持仓 2026 年 6 月约 146.5 吨 ，相当于全球"央行级"持有者第 33 位（与利比亚相当、领先菲律宾）；若视为黄金 ETF 则为全球第 7 大。 混合角色 ：一部分黄金支撑类货币资产（稳定币）负债，另一部分支撑金本位代币 XAUT——Tether 正日益像"央行+黄金 ETF"的混合机构，SG 称之为黄金市场的"gold flow monster"。 Nowcast 预测 ：下一次季度储备证明定于 10 月 31 日 ；SG 模型预计 9 月末集团实物黄金持仓增至约 161 吨 （3Q 驱动：稳定币负债增长 + 数吨 XAUT 铸造；9 月 29 日单次铸造约 12 万枚 XAUT ≈ 5 亿美元）。 展望 ：WGC 估计数字黄金 2031 年或达 1,600–1,700 亿美元 （基准情形，约为当前市场 3 倍）；7,000 亿美元属"愿景上限"而非基准——需要当前持仓 5–10 年内至少增长 8 倍。 SECTION 01 · DIGITAL GOLD 数字黄金的崛起：金融科技成为黄金新买家 The rise of fintechs in the gold market 黄金市场参与者中，金融科技公司是最年轻的一类。短短几年内，数字资产提供商迅速扩张，一些已跻身实物黄金最大持有者之列，与央行及主要 ETF/ETC 比肩；某些时期的吸金速度甚至同时超过了央行购金与 ETF 流入。驱动力包括： 极细颗粒度敞口 ：散户几美元即可购买代币的碎片份额； 7×24 连续交易 ：全天候价格发现与可及性（传统交易所已开始应对：CME 于 2025 年 1 月推出 1 盎司黄金期货、2026 年 7 月延长交易时间，实现含周末的 24/7 交易）； 生息机制 ：部分发行方将代币背后的实物金条出租、把租赁收益的一部分分给持有人——在高名义利率环境下吸引力显著。 量级对比（2026 年 9 月日均，吨）： 现货 952（LBMA 902 + 非LBMA 50）＋衍生品 2,003（COMEX 931 / LBMA 542 / 上海 479 / 其他 51）＋黄金 ETF 51 ≈ 全球流动性 3,006 吨/日；金本位加密代币仅约 3 吨/日（其底层敞口多已在 OTC/现货市场对冲，不宜重复计入）。月度维度：央行净购金约 70 吨/月（官方储备约 36,000 吨）、COMEX 持仓月均变化约 105 吨、ETF 持仓月均变化约 45 吨。 数字黄金 101：Vaulted 与 Tokenised 保管式（vaulted） ：对托管实物金条的直接凭证，账本由提供商集中维护（BullionVault 逾 50 亿美元、GoldMoney 逾 40 亿美元）。 代币化（tokenised） ：同样的经济敞口包装为区块链代币，可在公链转移、不依赖运营商内部账本——龙头为 Tether Gold（XAUT，市值约 32.5 亿美元）与 PAX Gold（PAXG，约 18 亿美元）。 风险与"$7,000 亿"的定位 高换手率暗示该板块投资者持有期更短、更具战术性——这一新增需求池可能比传统黄金持有者 更不稳定、对价格更敏感，并在回调中放大流出 。对 WGC"7,000 亿美元潜在需求"的说法，SG 认为这是基于投资者调查的理论上限：按 4,150 美元/盎司折算约 5,250 吨，是 2031 年基准情形（1,600–1,700 亿美元 ≈ 1,235 吨，当前约 375 吨 / 450–550 亿美元）的四倍以上，需要行业以 Tether 为参照在 5–10 年内将当前持仓放大约 8 倍——远超该板块迄今任何成就（目前仅占约 13 万亿美元实物黄金投资市场的 1% 以下）。WGC 作为行业推广机构，其上限应视为倡导而非预测。但趋势确定：WGC 调查显示近九成散户在条件合适时会考虑数字黄金、认知偏向年轻人群，且约 65% 的潜在需求来自当前完全不持有黄金的人群——是增量资金而非存量再配置。 Fig 1 · 规模前 15 的黄金加密代币：市值（左轴，10 亿美元）与隐含黄金持仓（右轴，吨）2020–2026 持续攀升，2026 年加速 | Top 15 gold cryptos: the growth of tokenised gold in USD and in tonnes — Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, CoinGecko，截至 2026-10-21（原报告 p3） Fig 2 · 主要黄金支撑代币累计成交额：2026 年至今已超 1,500 亿美元、远超 2025 全年（约 850 亿）与 2020–2024 合计 | Cryptos cumulated trading volume ($bn) — Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, CoinGecko（原报告 p4） SECTION 02 · TETHER CASE STUDY 案例研究：Tether，介于央行与黄金 ETF 之间的混合体 Tether: a hybrid between a central bank and a gold ETF 与央行比：一年内从第 43 位升至第 33 位 Tether 发行全球最大的实物支撑黄金代币，同时运营多只以美债、抵押贷款和黄金等低风险资产支撑的稳定币。一年前 SG 首次研究该集团时，其黄金持仓若与央行相比仅列全球第 43 ；今年 2 月已升至第 36 ；根据公司 6 月报告，其目前名义排名第 33 ——持仓与 利比亚央行 相当、比 菲律宾 高约 13 吨。 Fig 3 · 若与央行同列，Tether（146.5 吨，2026 年 6 月）排全球第 33 位，介于利比亚（32）与菲律宾（34）之间 | Where Tether would rank among global central bank gold holders — Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities，Tether Transparency 报告与 WGC 央行黄金储备（截至 2026-06-30）（原报告 p4） 与 ETF 比：全球第 7 大"黄金 ETF"，距第 6 仅一步之遥 若将 Tether 视为一只黄金 ETF，SG 模型估计其 9 月 30 日 161 吨持仓列为全球第 7 大；持仓再增 7%（约 11 吨） 即可升至第 6 位。综合央行与 ETF 两个维度，SG 估计 Tether 集团现为全球第 40 大黄金持有者。更关键的是其"非被动"属性：多数央行持仓多年甚至数十年基本稳定，而 Tether 的吸金速度超过了任何央行或黄金 ETF——SG 今年早些时候称之为市场的"gold flow monster"。 Fig 4 · 若视为黄金 ETF，Tether（161 吨，SG 模型估算）列全球第 7，仅次于 Xetra（6） | Where Tether would rank among global ETFs gold holders — Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities，Tether Transparency 报告与 WGC 黄金 ETF 数据（原报告 p5） 混合角色： 一方面，XAUT 承诺以瑞士金库中 1 盎司实物黄金 1:1 支撑每枚代币，持仓随投资者申赎扩张收缩——类黄金 ETF；另一方面，Tether 还以自有资产负债表上的黄金支撑其负债（主要是稳定币）——黄金约占集团资产负债表（总资产约 1,850 亿美元）的 10%，类央行储备资产。两种用途并存，使其成为真正的"混合机构"。 增长速度：黄金市场增长最快的角落 2023 年初以来：黄金 ETF 持仓年均 +13.6% 、央行黄金储备年均 +1.8% ，而 Tether 黄金持仓年均 +31% ——遥遥领先。按 2023 年以来累计净购金计，Tether 以 87.5 吨 列全球第 5 ，仅有 1 只 ETF 与 3 家央行（波兰、中国、印度等，见下图）增持更多。2022 年 6 月–2026 年 6 月共增持 110 吨；按 WGC 调查约 65% 为"新钱"推算，相当于约 70 吨 真正的新增需求进入黄金市场——Tether 不仅在争夺存量需求份额，还在扩大黄金投资者基础、引入新一代买家。 Fig 5 · 2023 年以来累计净购金（吨）：Tether 以 87.5 吨列全球第 5，仅次于波兰、中国、SPDR Mini 与印度 | Since 2023, Tether has been the world's fifth-largest net buyer of gold — Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities，Tether Transparency 报告与 WGC 数据（原报告 p6） SECTION 03 · NOWCASTING RESERVES 储备 Nowcast：Q3 末或达约 161 吨 Nowcasting Tether Group's reserves SG 模型将每个季度经证明的美元数字换算为按市价定价的代理资产单位（贵金属用现货金、其他资产用总回报指数），在两次证明之间按集团总资产负债表的季度增速线性内插（"flow"假设），重建日度黄金与储备路径。对最近一次证明之后的外推，黄金获得特殊处理： XAUT 作为 1:1 实物支撑的链上代币，提供了实际购金的日度信号 ——模型将黄金变动拆为"支撑腿"（XAUT 供应量的逐日变化，铸造即时且全额抵押、不做平滑）与"残差腿"（集团其余购金，历史上约为 XAUT 发行量的稳定倍数，经短窗口平滑以免单次大额铸造被误读）；一致性约束要求各资产之和恰好等于集团报告总资产，由美短债（T-Bills）充当吸收残差的"插头"。 Q3 预测： Tether 下一份季度储备报告定于 2026 年 10 月 31 日 发布（6 月 30 日后无官方更新）。SG 预计三季度集团黄金储备增至 季末约 161 吨 ，增长由两因素均等驱动——(1) 负债增长（稳定币产品流入）与 (2) 数吨 XAUT 的铸造。即便 161 吨，Tether 也仍只是全球第 7 大"黄金 ETF 级"持有者——既彰显其扩张速度，也说明头部黄金投资工具体量之大。 5 亿美元的 XAUT 铸造 9 月 29 日，Tether 发行约 119,700 枚 新黄金支撑代币，对应近 5 Commodity Compass Tether and the Rise of Digital Gold: When New Money Meets Ancient Gold ◼ Gold is no longer the exclusive playground of central banks, ETFs and bullion banks. A new generation of fintech firms has emerged as a meaningful source of gold demand, leveraging blockchain technology to create digital claims on physical bullion. Although tokenized gold remains small relative to traditional gold markets, its growth has been exceptional. The 15 largest gold-backed crypto tokens now represent more than US$6bn of market capitalization and roughly 45 tonnes of implied gold exposure, while aggregate trading volumes surpassed US$150bn year-to-date in 2026, already exceeding the full-year record set in 2025. ◼ Yet perspective matters. The global gold market trades roughly 3,000 tonnes per day, including around 950 tonnes in spot markets and 2,000 tonnes in derivatives, compared with only ~3 tonnes of daily turnover in tokenized gold. Likewise, the entire tokenized gold universe represents just 1% of the approximately 4,000 tonnes held by physically backed gold ETFs worldwide. Digital gold remains a niche market today, but one growing materially faster than traditional investment channels. ◼ The advantages of digital gold. This growth is being driven by structural advantages that conventional gold products struggle to match: fractional ownership, 24/7 trading, instant settlement and integration into digital financial ecosystems. Some providers have gone even further by introducing yield-bearing mechanisms through bullion- lending programmes, creating a form of gold ownership that offers both price exposure and income. ◼ Tether as a case study. Among these new entrants, Tether stands out. The company has quietly become one of the world's largest gold holders outside traditional institutions. Based on our estimates, Tether's gold holdings reached approximately 146.5 tonnes as of June 2026, placing it 33rd globally among central-bank-equivalent holders, alongside countries such as Libya and ahead of the Philippines. If classified as a gold ETF, Tether would rank as the 7th largest gold ETF in the world, requiring only around 25 additional tonnes to move into sixth place. ◼ The hybrid role of the Tether Group. We argue that Tether occupies a unique position in the gold ecosystem. Unlike ETFs, part of its gold backs a currency-like asset ecosystem, while another portion backs its gold token, XAUT. In this sense, Tether increasingly resembles a hybrid institution combining characteristics of both a reserve-holding central bank and a gold ETF. ◼ Nowcasting Tether Group’s reserves. Tether's next quarterly reserves attestation is scheduled for 31 October 2026 and will provide the first official update on the group's gold holdings since June. Based on our estimates of balance-sheet growth, XAUT issuance activity and gold-price developments during Q3, we forecast that Tether's physical gold holdings increased to approximately 161 tonnes by quarter-end. If confirmed, this would mark another significant step in Tether's rapid expansion as a gold holder, extending the steady rise that has seen the company climb the ranks of both institutional and sovereign holders in recent years. Nevertheless, even at 161 tonnes, Tether would remain the 7th largest gold ETF-equivalent holder globally, highlighting both the remarkable pace of its growth and the substantial size of the largest established gold investment vehicles. ◼ Looking ahead. The World Gold Council estimates that digital gold could reach US$160-170bn by 2031, while also highlighting a longer-term theoretical opportunity of US$700bn. We view the latter as an aspirational ceiling rather than a realistic base case. Achieving such scale would likely require current digital gold holdings to increase by at least eightfold within a few years. Weekly Extract from a report Head of FIC & Commodity Research Dr Mike Haigh +44 20 7762 4427 michael.haigh@sgcib.com Cross Commodity Strategist Jeremy Sellem +44 20 7762 4649 jeremy.sellem@sgcib.com Commodity Compass 2 29 October 2026 Tether and the Rise of Digital Gold: When New Money Meets Ancient Gold The rise of fintechs in the gold market Among the key participants in the gold market, fintechs are arguably the newest. In just a few years, digital asset providers have proliferated, and some have already risen into the ranks of the largest holders of physical gold, rivalling central banks and major ETFs and ETCs. Not only have their gold holdings grown rapidly, but the pace of accumulation has, at times, exceeded both central bank purchases and ETF inflows. Several factors help explain this growth. First, tokenized gold products provide retail investors with highly granular exposure, allowing them to purchase fractions of a token for only a few dollars. Second, these products trade 24/7, offering continuous price discovery and accessibility. Finally, some providers have gone a step further by transforming gold-backed tokens into yield-generating assets. By lending the physical gold backing their tokens and distributing part of the leasing income to token holders, they have introduced a feature traditionally absent from gold ownership. In a period of elevated nominal yields, this feature has attracted considerable interest from investors. Traditional market venues have begun to respond to this trend. For example, CME launched its 1- Ounce Gold futures contract in January 2025 and extended trading hours in July 2026, making it a true round-the-clock market with 24/7 trading, including weekends. This reflects a broader effort to offer retail investors greater flexibility and accessibility while preserving the advantages of regulated futures markets. Later in this note, we show that digital gold is growing far faster than traditional gold investment vehicles. Yet, despite this rapid growth, tokenised gold remains a niche segment of the global gold market relative to the size and liquidity of established trading venues. As of September 2026, average daily gold trading volumes are estimated at approximately 3,000 tonnes, comprising around 950 tonnes in the spot market, 2,000 tonnes in derivatives markets, and 50 tonnes through gold ETFs. By comparison, gold-backed crypto tokens account for only around 3 tonnes of daily trading volume. This volume should not be added to total global gold market liquidity, as the underlying exposure is likely hedged through established venues such as the OTC market and/or the spot market. Similar conclusions emerge when comparing investment holdings. Net central bank purchases average roughly 70 tonnes per month, while changes in COMEX gold futures open interest average around 105 tonnes per month. On their side, ETFs holdings vary on average by 45 tonnes per month. Against this backdrop, the 15 largest gold-backed crypto tokens have a combined market capitalisation of more than US$6 billion, equivalent to roughly 45 tonnes of implied gold exposure. In the next section, we explain the distinction between "tokenised" gold and "vaulted" gold. The key point is that, although the sector remains small in absolute terms, investor turnover is exceptionally high. Trading volumes of around 3 tonnes per month on a market worth just US$6 billion, or roughly US$40 billion when vaulted gold is included, are proportionally far larger than those observed in traditional gold investment vehicles. By comparison, physically backed gold ETFs trade roughly 51 tonnes per day against a stock of around 4,000 tonnes of gold. Similarly, monthly central bank purchases of around 70 tonnes are modest relative to official gold reserves of approximately 36,000 tonnes. This highlights an important characteristic of the digital gold ecosystem. While it remains a relatively small source of gold demand, it is associated with a much higher velocity of capital than traditional channels. In other words, the same ounce of gold changes hands more frequently. September 2026 daily trading volumes (tonnes) Spot LBMA 902 Non-LBMA 50 Total Spot 952 Derivatives COMEX 931 LBMA 542 Shanghai 479 Other 51 Total Derivatives 2,003 Gold ETFs North America 38 Europe 3 Asia 10 Total gold ETFs 51 Total Global gold market liquidity 3,006 Crypto 3 Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, CoinGecko, the World Gold Council, Bloomberg Commodity Compass 29 October 2026 3 Digital gold 101 Vaulted digital gold Vaulted digital gold gives investors a direct claim on physical bullion held in custody. Ownership is recorded in a centralised ledger maintained by the provider, and transactions occur within that provider's platform. Examples include BullionVault (US$5bn+) and GoldMoney (US$4bn+). Tokenised gold Tokenised gold wraps the same economic exposure into a blockchain token. Each token typically represents a specified quantity of vaulted gold and can be transferred on public blockchains without relying on the operator's internal ledger. The leading examples are Tether Gold (XAUT) with a market capitalisation of roughly US$3.25bn and PAX Gold (PAXG) at roughly US$1.8bn. The risk This expansion can be viewed both as an opportunity and a risk. On the one hand, tokenised gold broadens access to the gold market and attracts new participants. On the other hand, the high turnover suggests that investors in this segment may have shorter holding periods and a more tactical mindset than traditional gold investors. Whereas central banks and many ETF investors typically hold gold as a long-term reserve or portfolio allocation, participants in digital gold markets appear more inclined to trade gold as a liquid financial asset. As a result, this emerging pool of demand is likely to be more volatile and more sensitive to price changes than traditional sources of gold ownership, particularly amplifying outflows during corrections. $700bn? An aspirational ceiling, not a base case The World Gold Council suggests digital gold could unlock up to US$700bn of latent demand if adoption barriers fall. We treat this cautiously: it's a theoretical upside built from investor surveys. The WGC's own base case targets US$160-170bn by 2031, triple today's US$45-55bn market, equivalent to roughly 1,235 tonnes at US$4,150/oz, up from about 375 tonnes today. Plausible, if ambitious. The US$700bn figure is different: at the same price it implies ~5,250 tonnes, over four times the 2031 base case. Using Tether, the largest gold-backed token by assets, as a reference, the industry would need to multiply current holdings by at least eight times in five to ten years, far beyond anything achieved to date in a segment that still represents less than 1% of the US$13tn physical gold investment market. It's a useful ceiling for framing addressable demand, not a base Top 15 gold cryptos: the growth of tokenised gold in USD and in tonnes Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, CoinGecko, based on the following 15 gold-related tokens: XAUT, PAXG, KAU, XAUT0, CGBR, PGOLD, XAUM, GLDY, DGLD, VNXAU, XGZ, XGLD, CGO, XNK, ORO, as of 21 October 2026 0 10 20 30 40 50 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026 Aggregated Market Cap (LHS) Gold Holdings (RHS) tonnes $ bn Commodity Compass 4 29 October 2026 case. Worth noting too: the WGC is an industry body whose mandate is to promote gold ownership, so its upper bound should be read as advocacy, not forecast. However, one trend is undeniable: new investors appetite and the WGC survey data sees nearly nine in ten retail investors would consider digital gold under the right conditions, awareness skews young, and ~65% of latent demand comes from people who don't currently own gold at all, incremental demand rather than reallocation. Tether as a case study One major player stands out in the digital asset space: Tether. Not only does it issue the world's largest physically backed gold token, but it also operates several stablecoins backed by relatively low risk assets, including US Treasuries, secured loans, and gold. In this section, we explore how this new category of investor can influence gold prices, if it is not doing so already. How does Tether compare to Central Banks? In terms of total gold holdings on its balance sheet, Tether's position continues to rise rapidly. When we first wrote about the group a year ago, it would have ranked 43rd globally if compared with central banks. By February this year, we showed that it had moved up to 36th place. According to the company’s June report, Tether ranks 33rd in this notional ranking, with gold holdings comparable to those of the Central Bank of Libya and around 13 tonnes higher than those of the Philippines. Crypto trading activity in major gold-backed tokens supports the growth story Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, CoinGecko, based on the following 15 gold-related tokens: XAUT, PAXG, KAU, XAUT0, CGBR, PGOLD, XAUM, GLDY, DGLD, VNXAU, XGZ, XGLD, CGO, XNK, ORO, as of 21 October 2026 Where Tether would rank among global central bank gold holders Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, data from Tether’s Transparency reports and from the WGC’s Central Banks Gold Reserves as of 30 June 2026 20 40 60 80 100 120 140 160 2020-2024 2025 2026 YTD 100 110 120 130 140 150 160 170 180 metric tonnes of gold Cryptos cumulated trading volume ($bn) Commodity Compass 29 October 2026 5 We view Tether as a hybrid player, sitting somewhere between a central bank and a gold ETF. Why? On the one hand, through its gold token (XAUT), Tether commits to backing each token with one ounce of physical gold held in Switzerland. As a result, its gold holdings are directly influenced by investor inflows and outflows, much like a gold ETF, where bullion holdings expand or contract in line with demand. On the other hand, Tether also holds gold on its own balance sheet as part of the reserves backing its liabilities, primarily its stablecoins. Gold represents roughly 10% of the group's balance sheet, which totals around USD 185 billion. As a result, Tether's gold holdings serve two distinct purposes: supporting a currency-like liability base and backing a tokenised gold investment product. In our view, this makes Tether a genuine hybrid player. It combines characteristics of a central bank, which holds gold as a reserve asset to support confidence in its liabilities, with those of a gold ETF, whose bullion holdings are driven by investor demand for gold exposure. How does Tether compare to ETFs? If Tether were treated as a gold ETF, its 161 tonnes (estimated by our model) of gold holdings as of 30th September would rank it as the 7th largest gold ETF globally. Moreover, a further 7% increase in its gold holdings, or 11 tonnes, would be sufficient to move Tether into 6th place, highlighting how rapidly its position is strengthening. Combining both rankings, we estimate that Tether Group is now the 40th largest gold holder globally. More importantly, it is far from a passive participant. While the gold holdings of most central banks tend to remain broadly stable for years, and sometimes even decades, Tether's pace of accumulation has outstripped that of any central bank or gold ETF. For that reason, we described it earlier this year as the market's "gold flow monster". The significance extends beyond the scale of its purchases. Using the World Gold Council's survey of digital gold owners as a proxy1, we estimate that around 65% of these inflows represent new money entering the gold market. In other words, a majority of investors buying Tether's gold products appear not to have previously owned gold in any investment form. This suggests that Tether is not merely competing for a share of existing gold demand but may be expanding the investor base and 1 Digital Gold: Unlocking a $700-Billion Opportunity | World Gold Council Where Tether would rank among global ETFs gold holders Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, data from Tether’s Transparency reports and from the WGC’s Gold ETF: Stock, Holdings and Flows as of 30 June 2026 0 100 200 300 400 500 600 700 800 900 1000 metric tonnes of gold Commodity Compass 6 29 October 2026 attracting a new generation of gold buyers. With 110 tonnes added between June 2022 and June 2026, this would imply around 70 tonnes of genuine new demand entering the gold market. We showed earlier that the crypto ecosystem remains a relatively small venue for trading gold-linked assets. However, when it comes to the accumulation of physical bullion, it has been the fastest- growing segment of the gold market. Since early 2023, gold ETF holdings have increased by an average of 13.6% per year, while central bank gold reserves have grown by 1.8% per year. Over the same period, Tether's gold holdings have expanded by 31% per year, making it by far the fastest-growing corner of the gold market. In absolute terms, Tether ranks 5th in cumulative gold purchases since 2023, having added 87.5 tonnes. By comparison, only 1 ETF and 3 central banks accumulated more gold over the same period. Nowcasting Tether Group’s reserves Our model reconstructs Tether Group's daily gold (and broader reserve) holdings by converting each quarterly attested dollar figure into a number of units of a market-priced proxy (spot gold for Precious Metals, total-return indices for other asset classes). Between two attestations, holdings are linearly interpolated in proportion to the growth of the group's total balance sheet over the quarter (a "flow" assumption, falling back to straight calendar-time interpolation when the balance sheet barely moved), so the reconstructed path reflects when money came in, not just a straight line between two points. Nowcasting beyond the last attestation. Once there is no next attestation to anchor to, every other asset class is extrapolated at its trailing-quarter trading pace, but gold receives a sharper treatment because XAUT, an on-chain token backed 1:1 by physical gold, gives a live daily signal of actual gold purchases. The nowcast splits the gold move into two legs: a backing leg equal to the raw day-by-day change in XAUT supply (since minting is instantaneous and fully collateralized, this leg is never smoothed), and a residual leg capturing the rest of the group's gold buying (estimated historically as a stable multiple of XAUT issuance), which is smoothed over a short rolling window so that a single large, lumpy mint does not get misread as an implausible one-day jump in total reserves. Since 2023, Tether has been the world's fifth-largest net buyer of gold (by tonnage) Source: SG Cross Asset Research/Commodities, data from Tether’s Transparency reports and from the WGC’s Gold ETF: Stock, Holdings and Flows and Central Banks Gold Reserves as of 30 June 2026 0 50 100 150 200 250 300 350 400 450 Cumulative tonnes of gold purchased since 2023 (Net) Commodity Compass 29 October 2026 7 Consistency constraint. At every point in time, the sum of all modelled asset values is forced to equal the group's total reported assets exactly, with US Treasury Bills acting as the plug that absorbs the residual, guaranteeing the model reproduces each attestation to the cent while still producing a smooth, economically plausible daily series in between and beyond them. The next release of their Reserves report (quarterly) is expected on 31 October. Since we have not had any update sine 30 June, the values for Q3 are from our model and assumptions. We estimate that the group's gold reserves increased over the summer, driven equally by two factors: (1) growth in its liabilities, reflecting inflows into its stablecoin products, and (2) the minting of several tonnes of XAUT, its gold-backed token. On 29 September, Tether issued roughly 119,700 new gold-backed tokens, corresponding to nearly US$500mn of additional gold- linked exposure. Although the newly minted tokens were initially transferred to treasury inventory rather than directly entering circulation, the transaction nevertheless represented one of the largest single expansions of XAUT supply to date. Beyond its immediate impact on the token's market capitalization, the issuance highlights both the growing scale of the tokenized gold market and Tether's willingness to expand capacity ahead of anticipated investor demand. If sustained, such issuance activity would further reinforce Tether's position as one of the largest and fastest-growing sources of private-sector gold demand. 日日本电力公司 LNG 库存周环比持平（进口周环比 +14.0%、同比 -18.0%）；亚洲四周进口同比持平，其中中国过去四周进口同比 +18.0% 。若供应持续受限，货源竞争料将激烈，除非天气转暖。 美国仓位舒适： 截至 11 月 13 日当周库存 +20 Bcf 至 3,882 Bcf（低于共识 +27 Bcf）；此时段往年通常已转入抽取模式（去年 -14 Bcf、五年均值 -25 数据）。 展望： UBS 预计近月价格围绕近期水平宽幅波动，直至外交或天气任何一方出现实质性转变；日内欧洲理事会与议会就甲烷法规达成临时协议（推迟两年至 2029 年初），边际降低了供应端合规扰动风险。 图 3 · 流出阿曼湾的 LNG 流量（Bcf/d，7 日滚动均值）| LNG flows exiting the Gulf of Oman (Bcf/d, 7-day rolling
